name: DM_AAC_FLUSH
meaning: `0` keeps a movie's AAC converter across a `Flush` (a seek or a loop), as before; by default a Flush disposes it as `Stop` does, in the same hold of the decoder's lock as the rest of the Flush, and the next packet opens it again, so the sound after the Flush starts afresh, without the old position's overlap, as MediaCodec's decoder does (`hle_movie.c` `md_reset`)

name: DM_AAC_LAYOUT
meaning: `1` hands a movie's multichannel AAC sound out in the console's (Android MediaCodec's) order with the same channels, 5.1 as L R C LFE Ls Rs, set through `kAudioConverterOutputChannelLayout` before the first packet; unset or `0` (the default in release 1, until a device A/B with a 5.1 movie confirms the order) keeps AudioToolbox's own order, as before. Either way the order AudioToolbox reports is logged once per stream (`[movie] AAC: … channels in AudioToolbox's order …`; `hle_movie.c` `md_aac_layout`, `hle_movie_aac_order.h`)

name: DM_AB
meaning: `=<frames>` splits the run into phases of that many frames and alternates every switch set to `ab` (on in the odd phases); logs an `[ab]` line per phase with GPU and frame time and attachment traffic

name: DM_ABOUT
meaning: `=<about.json>` gives `build_ipa.sh` the launcher's "About this game" text (`dm/about.json` in the app: name, intro, description, publisher, release date); the NSP script sets it to `<build folder>/art/about.json` when the title database has the game

name: DM_ALIAS_SIZE
meaning: `=<bytes>` gives the guest an alias region of that size instead of the platform's, which is at least the Switch's 64 GB on the Mac and the profile's `mem_alias` on an iPhone (at least 256 MB, whole host pages; the heap and stacks stay as they are): the profile's value reproduces an iPhone's address space on the Mac, as the NSP script's heap check does; its address region check sets 64 GB (Mac only: an iPhone has no room)

name: DM_ALIAS_WINDOWS
meaning: `=<MB>` logs every 30 s how much of each window of that size in the alias region is mapped (windows aligned to their size in absolute addresses)

name: DM_ALLOW_OTHER_METAL
meaning: `1` lets `own_compilers.py` build the shader libraries with a Metal compiler other than the one in `dmsh_chain.lock` (it stops otherwise, GitHub issue #242); the NSP script sets it for `--allow-other-metal`

name: DM_AOC_DIR
meaning: Folder of add-on content: one numbered subfolder per DLC index holding that DLC's RomFS, reported by `aoc` and mounted read-only; the app, the Mac launcher and the NSP script set it when the build has DLC

name: DM_AOC_OWNED
meaning: `0` reports no add-on content even when `DM_AOC_DIR` has some, for runs without the DLC

name: DM_APP_DM
meaning: Set by the iOS app of a game of several programs: the running program's `dm/p<N>` folder, where the settings screen finds its `launcher.json`

name: DM_APP_VERSION
meaning: Overrides the IPA's version in `build_ipa.sh`; by default it is the packed game's display version from its control data (the update's when one is packed)

name: DM_ART
meaning: `=<image>` gives `build_ipa.sh` the launcher's key art, `dm/art.jpg` in the app (a JPEG copied as it is, a PNG converted with sips, longest side at most 1920; a failure leaves the app without art); the NSP script sets it to `<build folder>/art/art.jpg` (`--art`, else the title database or SteamGridDB); without it the launcher blurs the app icon

name: DM_AUDIO
meaning: `1` plays audio through Core Audio, `0` uses the silent sink; real output is the default on iOS, the silent sink on the Mac (the Mac launcher sets `1`)

name: DM_AUDIO_CAPTURE
meaning: `=<file>`: `tests/t_audio_live.c` records the output device's input (a loopback device such as BlackHole) there as 32-bit float samples, for `dm/tools/audio_channel_check.py`

name: DM_AUDIO_CAPTURE_CH
meaning: `=<n>`: the channels `tests/t_audio_live.c` records with `DM_AUDIO_CAPTURE` (6 by default)

name: DM_AUDIO_CAPTURE_DEVICE
meaning: `=<part of a device name>`: `tests/t_audio_live.c` records that device instead of the one playing at start (the target of a switch)

name: DM_AUDIO_DEVICE
meaning: `=<part of a device name>` (Mac) plays the audio on the output device with that name (a virtual device such as BlackHole 16ch, for tests); the default output otherwise

name: DM_AUDIO_DUMP
meaning: `=<file>` writes every PCM block the game appends as is (16-bit, 48 kHz, channel count as in the OpenAudioOut log), to judge whether a sound played

name: DM_AUDIO_IO_MS
meaning: `=<ms>` asks the audio session (the Mac: the output device) for that I/O buffer duration instead of 5 ms, 5-20 whole milliseconds, for a power A/B; the host's audio renderer then keeps a callback's worth of 5 ms blocks and two more in flight (`audio_io.h`). A game's own AudioOut keeps its own queue and can underrun at 20 ms. Logs the asked and granted duration (`audio session: …`, `audio I/O buffer (DM_AUDIO_IO_MS=N): …`); docs/reference/audio.md

name: DM_AUDIO_LIVE_PCM
meaning: `=<file>`: `tests/t_audio_live.c` plays that file (16-bit, 48 kHz, six channels interleaved in the guest's order) instead of its test tones

name: DM_AUDIO_MUTE
meaning: `=1` runs the real Core Audio output path (callback pacing, background take-over) with the output silenced, for lifecycle tests on the Mac without noise

name: DM_AUDIO_ROUTE
meaning: `=0` only logs an audio route change (AirPods or headphones connecting, the Mac's default output device changing) and leaves it to the audio watchdog, as before; by default the playing outputs restart at once on the new route

name: DM_AUDIO_WD_MS
meaning: `=<ms>` sets the audio watchdog's tick while every playing output's device calls back (default 250, 50-1000); `50` is the old fixed tick. A slower tick that sees no callback, or a last one over 50 ms old, only suspects a stall and goes back to 50 ms ticks, which decide it from the last callback's time (a stall is caught 200-350 ms after it at 250)

name: DM_AUDREN_RT
meaning: `0` keeps the host audio renderer's thread under ordinary time-sharing; by default it asks for a real-time time-constraint policy (5 ms period and deadline, 1 ms computation budget) after its output starts and restores the standard policy before the output closes (`hle_audren.c` `render_rt`). The off side of an A/B; a player build keeps it from env.txt (no filter names it). Logs `audren: render thread time-constraint policy … set` or the default kept; docs/reference/audio.md

name: DM_AUDREN_TRACE
meaning: When set, the CPU audio renderer logs every update with the number of frames rendered since the previous one

name: DM_AV1_DAV1D
meaning: `=1` decodes AV1 movies with dav1d even where VideoToolbox decodes AV1 (Apple M3 and A17 Pro on), to compare the two or to check the path older chips take (`hle_movie_av1.c`)

name: DM_BG_TRIM
meaning: `0` keeps the idle graphics caches when the app goes to the background (`dm_gfx_suspend`), as before; by default they are released after the drain, as under memory pressure (`DM_MEMORY_TRIM`), and the kept vertex conversions with them

name: DM_BOOTPROF
meaning: When set, logs boot timing: the loader's breakdown (mapping, relocation, probes), Metal library loading, pipeline creation, texture uploads and the first present

name: DM_BRIGHT_PROBE
meaning: `=<0.05-1.0>` (iPhone and iPad, off by default; unset, empty or `0` is off; any other value is refused with a red line): once, 3 s after the game's scene is active, saves the screen's brightness and sets it to that value, then logs whether the change notifications that follow are the set's own (`; … s after the probe's set, the set's own`) and reads `UIScreen.brightness` back 1 s and 10 s after the set, and 60 s, 180 s and 600 s after it while the value is still set (`front end: brightness probe: N s (T s measured) after the set …`, with `with no notification so far` when the screen changed without one); the saved value is put back once, on resign active (a swipe in the app switcher), in the background or at a program handoff (the app ending to start another program or itself again), with a line; a crash leaves the screen at the probe's value until the player or Auto-Brightness moves it. For the heat ladder's M1 questions: does an app's own set post the notification, does iOS keep the value with Auto-Brightness on, does a low value hold (`front_ios.m`, `dm/host/front_bright.h`). Every brightness change also gets a line, probe or not: `front end: brightness A → B (thermal N, T s after launch, scene active)`, at most 4 a second; after a storm (a Control Center slider drag) `front end: brightness settled at X (…; N changes before it not logged)` a second later gives the value it ended on. Not filtered from a player build

name: DM_BUILD_ID
meaning: The build ID the NSP script hands `build_ipa.sh` (G17, `build_stamp`): written into Info.plist as `DMBuildID`; `build_ipa.sh` makes one when it is not given

name: DM_BUILT_BY
meaning: The builder's Profile name at build time (G17, `build_stamp`, only when it passes GW21): written into Info.plist as `DMBuiltBy`; shown on the NX 18 card and in About

name: DM_BUNDLE_ID
meaning: Overrides the iOS app's bundle ID in `build_ipa.sh` (default `org.nxnative.<title ID in lowercase>`)

name: DM_CAPTURE_SYSTEM
meaning: `0` stops saving NX 18's own picture to `Captures` when iOS takes a screenshot during play (side and volume buttons, or a controller's Share button iOS keeps for itself); on by default; launcher setting Save screenshots to Captures, also in the in-game menu (`DmCapture.m`)

name: DM_CHEATS
meaning: Folder of Atmosphère cheat files: `<folder>/<build ID>.txt` or an SD-card layout (`atmosphere/contents/<title ID>/cheats/`) under it (default `<DM_ROOT>/cheats`); the Mac menu lists and toggles them

name: DM_CHEATS_ANY_BUILD
meaning: `1` loads a cheat file written for another build of the game when it is the only one (its addresses may not fit: for `cheat_anchor.py` checks)

name: DM_CHEATS_DEBUG
meaning: Logs every memory write a cheat makes, its reads (a pointer chain's addresses and values; the first 600 access lines, then one in 300) and what each refused address is (a host image, the host's malloc heap, another mapping), and the cheat file context the menu's "another version" rows come from

name: DM_CHEATS_ON
meaning: Comma-separated cheat names turned on at launch, besides the saved per-build enabled states

name: DM_CHEATS_WINDOW
meaning: `1` opens the Mac Cheats panel beside the game from the start

name: DM_CLOCK_KICK
meaning: `<ms>` (20 to 300; the profile's `clock_kick` sets the default, Donkey Kong Bananza's 120; `0` turns it off; it stands back only at critical heat, thermal 3): once the GPU clock is stuck (the last two probe readings 2.3x or more, the GPU at least 45% busy, the frame rate under 90% of the game's top rate for 2 s, no movie, critical heat, Low Power Mode or Battery Saver hold), the next present holds the game that many ms so the GPU drains to idle, and the game's frame-rate controller may try 60 at once; no sooner than 10 s after, doubling to 160 s while kicks fail (`hle_nvn.c` `clock_kick_tick`). For Bananza, whose clock comes back after even an instant pause. A `GPU clock kick #N` line at each kick

name: DM_CLOCK_KICK_PIN
meaning: `<s>` (0 to 10, default 0, off: Bananza run 17 held 60 for ~4 s after each kick and the clock stayed down): after a GPU clock kick the frame-rate controller is held at interval 1 for that many seconds (its pin), so a game stepped down to 30 does not step back before iOS raises the clock; `0` turns the hold off (`hle_nvn.c` `clock_kick_tick`)

name: DM_CLOCK_KICK_SLOW
meaning: `<ms>` (20 to 300, default 250): the GPU clock kick's hold when the game is at its 30 fps step (a 120 ms hold rarely lifted the clock there, 250 ms did); at the 60 fps cadence the hold stays the profile's `clock_kick` (`hle_nvn.c` `clock_kick_tick`)

name: DM_CLOCK_RESCUE
meaning: Off where the profile's clock kick is on (Tears of the Kingdom, Bananza, Mario Kart World, Star Fox; since 2026-11-21: `1` turns it on there too), and off by default in the Mario Kart World family since 2026-11-18 (no version brought Bananza's clock back on the iPhone): `cool` turns the cool-down on there, `classic` the rescue that holds 60, `0` keeps both off everywhere. `0` turns off the GPU clock rescue; `classic` keeps the rescue that holds 60 with 0.75-sized views where the cool-down is the default (the Mario Kart World family), `cool` asks for the cool-down in a game with a render-scale stub. The cool-down: the views at their smallest for 8 s with the game held at 20, then the game probes back to 60 itself ([the cool-down](reference/frame-rate.md#the-gpu-clock-stuck-at-a-third-of-its-speed-with-the-phone-cool-the-clock-rescue)). Before it: `0` turns off the GPU clock rescue: a game with a render scale lever (a render-scale stub, or `heat_gpu_stretch on`: the Mario Kart World family) stuck below its 60 fps target with the GPU probe at 2.3x or more draws its 3D views at 0.75 for 3 s, its factor composed with the player's Render scale and the heat ladder's through the render scale's setter (`hle_nvn.c` `clock_rescue_tick` / `scale_set`, `nvn_rescue.h`); in a game whose own frame-rate controller the host gates (Donkey Kong Bananza) the rescue also lets it probe back to 60 at once (`hle_fctl.c` `dm_fctl_rescue`)

name: DM_CLOCK_RESCUE_S
meaning: `<s>` (3 to 20; unset, 3 s as before): the GPU clock rescue's hold, and while a rescue is under way the game's frame-rate controller is kept at interval 1, its steps up to 2 blocked (`nvn_fctl.h` `pin`, `hle_fctl.c` `dm_fctl_pin`), then released as usual; only where the host gates the controller (`DM_FPS_CTL=host`), and under `hold30` the rescue stays off. Logs the hold on the rescue's start line and `interval 1 released: N steps to interval 2 blocked (M frames handed interval 1's band)` on its end line; a bad value is a red line and keeps 3 s. Also from `Documents/env.txt`, player builds too ([A deadline at 60 at any interval, and a clock rescue that holds interval 1](reference/frame-rate.md#a-deadline-at-60-at-any-interval-and-a-clock-rescue-that-holds-interval-1))

name: DM_CNTFRQ
meaning: `0` makes a guest `mrs xN, cntfrq_el0` give the host's counter frequency (24 MHz on earlier Apple chips, 1 GHz on a development Mac), the value it gave before the rewriter sent the read to the host gate; unset, the gate gives the guest's 19.2 MHz (31.25 MHz for a Switch 2 game), the frequency of the ticks the counter reads return ([rewriter](reference/rewriter.md#counter-frequency-reads-give-the-hosts-frequency))

name: DM_CODEC_PACE
meaning: `0` turns off picture pacing only: every picture of an nn::codec video decoder (the Switch 2's: `hle_codec_video.c`) is handed out in decode order and none is skipped, as before pacing. It does not turn off the movie signal: the decoder still tells the frame step a movie plays and its picture rate, so a movie of 30 pictures a second or fewer still caps the frame step at 30, a faster one still holds the fastest hold the cap allows, and on a 120 Hz Mac screen the cap is still 60 while one plays; the movie's log line still comes, marked `off (DM_CODEC_PACE=0)`. So `0` is not the behaviour from before both changes, where these decoders never raised the movie signal. By default a released buffer gets the newest decoded picture whose time is at or before the movie's clock (the guest clock from the first picture the player gives back, not running in the background, while a buffer waits for a picture, or across a gap of 0.25 s or more between two asks) and the older ones are dropped, so a player that takes one picture per game frame (Ocarina of Time's) plays a 60 fps movie at its own speed at any frame rate; one log line per movie gives its picture rate and the pictures skipped

name: DM_CONTROL_NACP
meaning: `=<control.nacp>`: the game's control data, for the save sizes `fs::GetSaveDataSize` and `GetSaveDataSizeMax` answer (`hle_fs.c`); default `control.nacp` beside `DM_ROMFS`; without one, 256 MB data and 16 MB journal, and save extensions have no limit

name: DM_COPY_GAME_RESOURCES
meaning: `NO` skips the Xcode build phase that copies the game's resources into the app (`stage_resources.sh`, on by default); `build_ipa.sh` sets it for its unsigned build, which packs them itself

name: DM_COPY_ROMFS
meaning: `NO` keeps the game files out of the app, in the Xcode build phase (`stage_resources.sh`) and in the unsigned IPA of `build_ipa.sh` (on by default): `main.m` takes the validated `Documents/romfs.img` copied by `scripts/push_romfs.sh`, then a `Documents/romfs` folder; the build writes the image's identity as `romfs.id` into the app, and `main.m` uses only a matching image (`--romfs separate` of the NSP script sets this)

name: DM_CRASH_PEEK
meaning: `="sp+0x248*,x22-0x20"` adds 0x100 bytes at each address to the crash report: `sp` or a register plus or minus an offset, a trailing `*` reading the pointer stored there first

name: DM_CTL
meaning: `=<file>` (Mac): the host polls the file every 100 ms and runs each appended line: button presses, `shot`, `passdump`, `texdump`, `env KEY=VALUE`, `peek`, `memdump`, `addr <hex>` (what the host knows of a guest address), `drag`, `pressure <0|1|2>` (acts as the system's memory pressure, as macOS lets only root simulate one) and more

name: DM_CTRL_PROMPT_TEXT
meaning: The texts of the controller applet's prompt (a game wants more players than have joined; `ctrl_prompt.h`) in the player's language, one per line: the title, the hint, the count, the done and the cancel button, with `{min}`, `{max}` and `{joined}` replaced by the numbers; a front end sets it ([Starting a game](frontends.md#starting-a-game)), an empty or missing line keeps the English text

name: DM_DBG
meaning: When set, prints the guest's `svcOutputDebugString` text to stderr as `[guest]` lines

name: DM_DBG_AU_FRAMES
meaning: `=<frames>` asks the Mac's Core Audio output for that many frames per callback instead of about 5 ms (1024 reproduces the iOS default that caused crackling)

name: DM_DEPTH_BOUNDS
meaning: `0` ignores the games' depth bounds (`SetDepthBounds`) as before they were applied: no Metal depth bounds test, and draws whose bounds pass nothing are drawn. On by default where the GPU has the test (Apple10 and later, the iPhone 18 Pro Max); a GPU without it (the M4 Max, Apple9) draws every draw as before either way, with one red line. Outside `DM_NVN_` so that a player build's `env.txt` can still turn it off

name: DM_DEPTH_ZERO_COPY
meaning: `1` / `0` overrides the profile's `depth_zero_copy`: a new single-sample Depth16Unorm or Depth32Float texture is zeroed by copies from the zero buffer (`1`) or by a clear-only render pass (`0`, every other game's way) (`nvn_mtl.m` `tex_zero_fill`). Default: the profile's (Ocarina of Time on). With the key on or the switch set either way, a depth texture of 64 MB or more logs, 12 frames on, `[nvn-mtl] depth zero: the WxH format (N MB) made in frame F, zeroed by N copies / clear passes (…): the upload batch with them … ms on the GPU; that frame's submissions … ms on the GPU, … and … the next two`, the line an A/B compares (up to 4 textures wait at once; written by the replay worker, so not with queue replay off); `0` in `Documents/env.txt` turns it off (a player build keeps the line)

name: DM_DETCLOCK
meaning: `=<step ns>`: from the first present on, the guest clock advances a fixed step per present instead of following the wall clock, and the random source becomes a fixed-seed stream (replay and test runs). Relative thread sleeps and synchronization timeouts stay on host time

name: DM_DETCLOCK_PACE
meaning: `=1` with `DM_DETCLOCK`: each frame takes at least one clock step of wall time, so background loading keeps up with the fixed clock (used by the screenshot gate)

name: DM_DISPLAY_NAME
meaning: Overrides the iOS app's name in `build_ipa.sh` (default the game name in the base NSP's control data)

name: DM_DRAWABLE_COUNT
meaning: `2` or `3`: the game layer's `maximumDrawableCount` on the iPhone, iPad and Mac (`front_drawable.h`); unset keeps Metal's 3, as before. Two save one drawable (7.9 MiB at 1080p) and may drop frames: an experiment for a device A/B

name: DM_DRAWABLE_NATIVE
meaning: `1` keeps the iPhone's and iPad's drawable at the game view's pixels everywhere, as before; by default it has the picture's render size (`front_picture_size`) where the present scales bilinearly anyway (Upscaling Standard, Picture Stretch, Ultrawide) and Core Animation scales the layer to the view

name: DM_DRAWABLE_SHADER_ACCESS
meaning: `1` makes the iPhone and iPad game layer's drawables readable and writable by shaders (`framebufferOnly` NO, the old behaviour), for an A/B of the present or a diagnostic that reads a drawable; unset, they are render targets only, as on the Mac (`front_ios.m`; `nvn_mtl.m` logs the drawable's usage once)

name: DM_DRS_GPU_SCALE
meaning: `0` turns off the GPU headroom controller in a game whose profile sets `drs_gpu_scale on` (Donkey Kong Bananza, Mario Kart World, Splatoon Raiders, Breath of the Wild, Tears of the Kingdom; the Quality preset sets it): by default, while the GPU time per frame stays over the target (`DM_DRS_GPU_TARGET`, 75% of the target's frame time) the host lowers the game's render scale one step more through its live lever (`nvn_drs_gpu.h`, `hle_nvn.c` `drs_gpu_tick`) and takes back a step that did not lower the GPU time per frame. Read again each 250 ms window, so the in-game menu's preset change applies at once

name: DM_DRS_GPU_TARGET
meaning: GPU headroom under the game's dynamic resolution (`nvn_drs_gpu.h`, `hle_nvn.c` `drs_gpu_tick`), on by default at `75`: where the game's own dynamic resolution runs through a level stub with the floor (Ocarina of Time, `DM_DYNAMIC_RESOLUTION=1`: Balanced and Battery Saver), the host holds a floor under its level, one level past it when the GPU stays busy over the target (2 windows of 250 ms; the merged busy of every command buffer) or the performance cores sit at 45% or less of their highest clock with the GPU 50% busy or more (1 s), and one level back after 2 s under the target less 15 points; `=<50-95>` another target in percent; `0` / `off`: the game's own steps alone. Each change logs `dynamic resolution floor A → B …: <reason>`, and the `dynamic resolution up to frame` line ends with the window's summary. Not filtered from a player build. [A saturated GPU caps the performance cores while dynamic resolution waits for late frames](reference/frame-rate.md#a-saturated-gpu-caps-the-performance-cores-while-dynamic-resolution-waits-for-late-frames)

name: DM_DYNAMIC_RESOLUTION
meaning: `1` lets the game's own dynamic resolution run, `0` (default) keeps full resolution; only on the builds that declare the DYNAMIC_RESOLUTION capability: NieR:Automata 1.0.3 (its patches.py; scales between 70 and 100 %, `hle_fpslock.c` `k_nier_dr`) and Ocarina of Time (its frame step stub of the level function, state page +0x40: on, it steps one level at a time on the measured load, as the game's own extrapolation from pixel count kept it at its lowest level on Apple GPUs; no level above the host's GPU headroom floor, `DM_DRS_GPU_TARGET`). The launcher's Dynamic resolution

name: DM_EMBED_TAG
meaning: Set by the iOS app of a game of several programs: the tag of the running program's embedded sections (`p<N>`, `gen_embed.py --tag`)

name: DM_ENTITLEMENTS
meaning: `=<plist>` gives a prepared Xcode project another entitlements file instead of the Increased Memory Limit one, and the ad-hoc signature of the unsigned IPA's executable carries them; empty means no entitlements

name: DM_ENV_FILE
meaning: `=<file>` makes `build_ipa.sh` bake its `KEY=VALUE` lines into the app as `dm/env.txt`, applied at boot; `Documents/env.txt` overrides them

name: DM_ENV_FILE_KEYS
meaning: Set by the iOS app and the Mac launcher at launch to the space-separated names an env file set; the settings screen keeps those values and shows them greyed out

name: DM_ENV_LAUNCH_KEYS
meaning: Set at launch by the Mac launcher (the launcher settings already in the environment) and the iOS app (every DM_* variable already in it) to the space-separated names; the settings screen keeps those values and shows them greyed out

name: DM_EXEC_OUT
meaning: File `oe::ExecuteProgram` records the next program and its parameters in, then the app ends (the iOS app of a game of several programs sets it to `Documents/program.bin`)

name: DM_FACTS
meaning: About this game's facts file, `facts.json` from `dm/tools/about_facts.py` (age ratings from the control data, the profile's tested line and known issue, the packed mods' credits): `build_ipa.sh` copies it to `Gen/dm/facts.json` once per app (the NSP script's `ipa_env`; the Mac's `pack_app.py --facts`)

name: DM_FD_LOG
meaning: `=<seconds>` logs, every that many seconds, the number and kinds of file descriptors the process has open

name: DM_FIELD_LOG
meaning: `0` writes the frame step, thread policy and long-frame lines as X1.0 did. By default (logging only): every change of the frame step's hold with its reason (how many of the last 30 frames were late, the late frames' CPU and GPU and which side ran long, the fit trial or probe), 40 change lines in each window of 1800 presents instead of 40 in a run, that window's own counts on the `game time` line, a `dynamic resolution up to frame N` line where a stub runs the game's dynamic resolution (Ocarina of Time), the `thread policy` line read on the thread the policy was set on (X1.0 read the thread presenting) with both named and, with `replay_rt` / `DM_REPLAY_RT`, each replay thread's declaration read on that thread, the `translation detail` line's split of the submit cost into the game threads' command copy and the replay with the wall time each waited for `g_sub_mu`, `g_rmu` and the encode thread, and `; N ms of it in the background` on a long frame across a stay in the background (`scripts/devlog.py` does not count it)

name: DM_FIXED_TIME
meaning: `=<seconds>`: the user clock always returns that time and the host time zone is pinned to UTC, for deterministic comparison

name: DM_FOCUS_KEEP
meaning: `1` keeps the game in focus while its Mac window is up, whichever app is active (minimizing still counts); `scripts/regress.py` sets it, so another app taking the key window during a run does not pause a game that stops out of focus

name: DM_FONT_DIR
meaning: Folder of the shared-font stand-ins, one per type (`standard.ttf`, `chinese_simplified.ttf`, `chinese_simplified_ext.ttf`, `chinese_traditional.ttf`, `korean.ttf`, `nintendo_ext.ttf` with the button icons; `make_shared_fonts.py`); the app, the Mac launcher and the NSP script set it

name: DM_FORCE_STRICT
meaning: `=1` makes the loader fail on forced-hook entries no module references, instead of only noting them (for checking a mistyped list)

name: DM_FOREGROUND_ROLE
meaning: `0` (Mac, without `DM_WINDOW`) keeps the task role of the shell or script that started the host; unset, the host takes the foreground-application role a focused app has (`front_role.h`), so its threads are not held up behind background daemons (audio underruns in headless runs, [audio](reference/audio.md#underruns-in-a-run-without-a-window))

name: DM_FPS
meaning: `30` or `60` pins the frame rate the display link and frame pacing aim for; otherwise it follows the game's present interval (60, or 30 when the game asks for 30)

name: DM_FPS_CTL
meaning: `game` hands a game's own frame-rate controller its own measure of each frame (Donkey Kong Bananza: its rule alone decides 30 or 60); by default (`host`, or empty) the host decides when the controller comes back from a longer interval, as the clocks it measured on follow the interval on an iPhone (`hle_fctl.c`, `nvn_fctl.h`; only a game whose `patches.py` has the gate). `hold30` holds the controller at interval 2 (30 fps) for good: no probes back to 60, the GPU clock rescue off, and the profile's `gpu_time_scale` off (the reports' true times; an explicit `DM_GPU_TIME_SCALE` stays); the Battery Saver preset sets it for a game whose profile has `preset battery DM_FPS_CTL=hold30` (launcher.json `preset_env`) and clears it for the other presets. Read again once a second under the in-game menu's lock (`front_env_copy`), so the menu's preset change applies while the game runs. Also from `Documents/env.txt`: the A/B switch (the summary lines give the time at each interval under any rule)

name: DM_FPS_CTL_PROBE
meaning: On by default (unset or `1`); `0` turns off two rules on the probes of a game's own frame-rate controller back to interval 1 (`nvn_fctl.h`, `hle_fctl.c`; Donkey Kong Bananza; NX18-X2.0 bananza-alldata-analysis.md ranked fix 5): after an ordinary timed probe failed (no load or 8 s at interval 1 since), the next timed probe waits while the 8-frame mean at the longer interval is over the gate, 20.8 ms (`<ms>`, 15 to 40, sets another), and starts at the first frame under it; and an ordinary probe whose frames after its 30-frame grace run 4 of the last 8 over 18.3 ms by the game's own measure is ended at once (the controller handed interval 2's band until it steps up, a failed probe). The first probe after a step up, a light scene's probe and a GPU clock rescue's or kick's (`dm_fctl_rescue`) run as before, and Battery Saver's `hold30` and `DM_CLOCK_KICK_PIN` are untouched. Lines `the probe waits (DM_FPS_CTL_PROBE …)` and `the probe is ended early (DM_FPS_CTL_PROBE …)`; the summary line adds `DM_FPS_CTL_PROBE: probes ended early N, waits the gate held M`. Kept in player builds (`player_env.h`), also from `Documents/env.txt`: the A/B switch

name: DM_FPS_HOLD
meaning: `on` / `off` overrides the profile's `fps_hold`: whether late frames may raise the hold above the frame cap's vsyncs (on by default)

name: DM_FPS_HOLD_BACKOFF
meaning: `double` / `burst` overrides the profile's `fps_hold_backoff`: whether a short burst on the CPU side at hold 1 (late frames whose GPU was under the late line) steps the frame step up, so that a held probe's run at hold 1 it ends within 8 s doubles the waits at 30 fps (`double`, the default), or is paid back without a step up (`burst`; Ocarina of Time). `double` in `Documents/env.txt` turns Ocarina of Time's off (`nvn_fstep.h` `FSTEP_BURST_N`)

name: DM_FPS_RESUME
meaning: `1` / `0` overrides the profile's `fps_resume`: under the frame step, the frame across a stay in the background is on time and owes nothing, and the 30 frames after it pay their lateness back without stepping the hold up (`1`; Ocarina of Time), instead of a late frame owing up to 15 vsyncs that the game runs fast to pay back (`0`, the default). `0` in `Documents/env.txt` turns Ocarina of Time's off (`nvn_fstep.h` `nvn_fstep.away`)

name: DM_FPS_TARGET
meaning: Frame-rate cap: `30` or `60`, `120` for a game whose profile has `fps_max 120` (60 otherwise), or `0` for the game's own limit; overrides the profile's `fps_target`

name: DM_FRAMEGEN
meaning: `1` frame generation (X2.0, off by default; no launcher row): at the 30 fps cap on the 60 Hz display link, MetalFX's frame interpolator shows a midpoint frame before each game frame, from the depth and motion copied where the game's upscaler runs (NVN2's DLSS; NDSR with `DM_FRAMEGEN_MOTION=zero`); turns present snapshots on and keeps the 60 Hz link where the 30 fps cap would take the 30 Hz one. Real frames reach the screen one tick (16.7 ms) later. It steps aside (real frames, no captures, the 30 Hz link) at thermal state serious or worse and in Low Power Mode (until both have been gone 30 s; on the Mac the system's own, from NSProcessInfo, as its host reports neither), on a rung of the heat ladder (its 30 fps heat hold included, until its calm wait has passed) and in the Battery Saver preset (`DM_PRESET=battery`, read once a second), and is off with `DM_PRESENT_REPEAT=1`. The 30 fps cap keeps its 30 Hz link where it cannot generate: before the game's upscaler gave a capture, without MetalFX's interpolator, and in variable-refresh fullscreen without a fixed-rate 60 Hz mode (no depth or motion copied there). Vitals then reads `60 fps, 30 rendered`. Off it costs nothing (no allocations, no per-frame work); on, what it made goes after 300 frames without use, at a memory trim while it is not generating and going to the background, and is made again on demand. A status line every 600 frames counts generated and real frames by reason; a player build keeps it from env.txt ([rendering](reference/rendering.md#frame-generation))

name: DM_FRAMEGEN_JITTER
meaning: `1` passes DLSS's camera jitter to the frame interpolator (with `DM_FRAMEGEN=1`); 0 by default, as the colour it interpolates is the upscaled, de-jittered picture

name: DM_FRAMEGEN_MOTION
meaning: `zero` lets frame generation run on the NDSR path (Ocarina of Time, Mario Kart World, Splatoon Raiders, Bananza without DLSS) with zero motion (the interpolator estimates none: generated frames are close to a blend of the two pictures and ghost when the camera moves); unset, that path has no motion and shows real frames only

name: DM_FRAMEGEN_SHOT
meaning: `=<path prefix>:<count>` (with `DM_FRAMEGEN=1`; also through `DM_CTL`'s `env`) writes the next <count> generated frames as `<prefix>_<k>_G.png` and the real frame each leads into as `<prefix>_<k>_F.png`; both are copied inside the generated frame's command buffer and written on a queue of their own, so the link does not wait

name: DM_FRAME_WG
meaning: `1` / `0` overrides the profile's `frame_wg` (off for every game): one work interval made by `AudioWorkIntervalCreate`, finished by the thread that acquires the window texture just before its pacing wait and started just after it with the real-time period as its deadline, once a frame (`frame_wg.c`, `hle_nvn.c` `frame_wg_on`). Each thread that acquires takes the time-constraint policy and joins at its first acquire (so an acquire that moves to another thread joins there too), the 'NVN queue replay' and 'dm-encode' threads at their first declaration (`replay_rt`); a thread that did not join calls neither start nor finish, and its frame counts as skipped. Needs `DM_RT` on: with `DM_RT=0` it logs that it is not armed. A player build keeps it from `Documents/env.txt`. Logs each thread's join result once and a `frame workgroup up to frame …` line every 300 frames: intervals started and finished, finished past the deadline, frames skipped, errors ([A frame deadline told through a work interval](reference/frame-rate.md#a-frame-deadline-told-through-a-work-interval))

name: DM_FRAME_WG_PERIOD
meaning: `<ms>` (8 to 34; 8, 11, 16 and 33 name 120, 90, 60 and 30 Hz's period, so 16 is 16.667 ms), only with the frame workgroup armed (`DM_FRAME_WG=1`): each frame's workgroup deadline is that period at any present interval instead of the real-time period (33.3 ms at the game's interval 2), and the present thread's and the replay threads' time-constraint period follow it; the pacing stays the game's interval (`hle_nvn.c` `frame_wg_period`). One `frame workgroup deadline (DM_FRAME_WG_PERIOD=…)` line at the start (`ignored` without the workgroup, a red line for a bad value), and the 300-frame line adds the deadline and how many frames were at a longer interval. Also from `Documents/env.txt`, player builds too ([A deadline at 60 at any interval, and a clock rescue that holds interval 1](reference/frame-rate.md#a-deadline-at-60-at-any-interval-and-a-clock-rescue-that-holds-interval-1))

name: DM_FS
meaning: When set, logs file opens, paths not found or not mounted, and a read summary every 64 MiB or 1000 reads

name: DM_FSLOG
meaning: `=<file>` writes one TSV line per ReadFile: seconds since boot, guest path, offset, length and guest buffer address

name: DM_FSLOG_HASH
meaning: With `DM_FSLOG`, adds a column with the FNV-1a 64 hash of the bytes read

name: DM_FSTEP_GPU_RETRY
meaning: `0` takes upstream's rule for the frame step's GPU ratio (nvn_fstep.h `nvn_fgpu.ratio_at`, upstream b1ba6570f): once two failed probes have given a hold's ratio and it says the scene does not fit hold 1, no probe starts while the scene costs the same. By default (`1`) NX 18 still starts one each 32 s since the last step up while the GPU reference calls the GPU slowed, so a lighter scene whose clock follows the hold is found again after a heavy area as slow at either hold ([frame-rate.md](reference/frame-rate.md#a-scene-that-does-not-fit-the-shorter-hold-probed-against-another-scenes-gpu-time)). `ab` alternates with `DM_AB`, for an iPhone battery A/B. Not a player setting

name: DM_FSTEP_PROBE_RAMP
meaning: `0` ends a frame-step probe's grace after its 30 frames as before; by default the grace is renewed while the probe's frames keep getting cheaper (macOS raises the GPU clock for the shorter deadline over seconds); `ab` alternates with `DM_AB`

name: DM_FULLSCREEN
meaning: `1` (any value but `0`) starts the Mac window in fullscreen; `0` or unset, a window. The Mac settings window's Display mode

name: DM_GAME
meaning: Selects the game profile (a title ID under `dm/games` or `DM_GAMES_DIR`) for the Python tools and the rewriter; there is no default

name: DM_GAMES_DIR
meaning: Profile folders outside the repository, separated by `:`, searched after `dm/games`; the NSP script points it at a provisional or derived profile

name: DM_GAMES_FIRST
meaning: `=1` searches `DM_GAMES_DIR` before `dm/games`, so a provisional or derived profile wins over the game's own (the NSP script's `--provisional`)

name: DM_GAME_ENV
meaning: `KEY=VALUE` pairs, separated by spaces, that the game's own `getenv` returns, in place of the profile's `game_env` (`hle_os.c`); any other name goes to the SDK's empty environment

name: DM_GAME_MENU
meaning: `system` makes the iPhone and iPad in-game menu the system's menu (a `UIMenu`, as before NX 18's panel) instead of NX 18's own panel; the rows, notes and actions are the same, but the system's menu takes no controller and keeps the system font

name: DM_GFX_FIXTURE_OUT
meaning: `=<dir>`: graphics tests write their raw result textures and buffers there

name: DM_GFX_SCALE
meaning: The graphics scale tier `oe::GetCurrentGraphicsScale` answers, on every platform: `0` (the full picture), or `1` or `2`, the reduced tiers at which a Switch 2 game renders smaller. Unset (or any other value), the platform's default: `0` in both modes on the Mac; on the iPhone and iPad the operation mode, `1` docked and `0` handheld (0.5's answer, kept for heat), so `DM_GFX_SCALE=0` gives the full picture docked there. The host logs the answer and why at the first query

name: DM_GLSLC_CAPTURE
meaning: `=<dir>` saves every GLSLC output the game compiles at run time; `shader_split.py` reads it (default `<version dir>/glslc_capture`)

name: DM_GLSLC_PLAY
meaning: Where the host saves a GLSLC output the game compiles while it is played with a stage whose shader key the shader map lacks (default `glslc_play/` in the parent of `DM_SAVE`: the app's `Documents/glslc_play`; `off` saves none); the NSP script takes the folder into the next build (`gather_glslc_play`). For `shader_split.py`, the folder of those outputs (default `<version dir>/glslc_play`)

name: DM_GPU_CAPTURE
meaning: `=<frame>[:<frames>]` or `gpu:<ms>[:<after frame>]` writes a Metal GPU trace of those frames for Xcode's Metal debugger; can be set while running through `DM_CTL`. Set at the start (as `MTL_CAPTURE_ENABLED` is), it gives the GPU capture profile: no pipeline archive is opened or written, so the start is slower (docs/reference/shaders.md)

name: DM_GPU_CAPTURE_DIR
meaning: Folder for `DM_GPU_CAPTURE`'s traces (default `gpu_captures/` in the working directory)

name: DM_GPU_CAPTURE_KEEP
meaning: Before each GPU capture, prunes the capture folder's `dm_*.gputrace` entries so that the newest `KEEP - 1` stay (default 2)

name: DM_GPU_LOST_S
meaning: the GPU hang watchdog (`nvn_mtl.m` `gpu_watch`, the idea from d2r-metal): with work waiting (a fence, an upload batch, a present or a command buffer on the GPU) and no GPU work finished for that many seconds (default 10; fractions allowed; `0` turns it off), the GPU is taken as lost: nothing more is committed to it, every wait on its completion returns, and the front end saves and quits (the iPhone: a line on a dark screen, the graceful exit with the cloud save and the pipeline archive, and a note at the next launch; the Mac: its GPU-lost alert). A `[RED] GPU stall (the stall report)` line with the stuck fence, its command buffers that came back and its shaders, and the freeze detector's dump come 2 s into such a stall (half the limit under 4 s), and again with `[RED] GPU lost:`. The time is counted in the watchdog's ticks, so a process iOS suspended counts none ([A GPU that finishes no work is taken as lost](reference/nvn-objects.md#a-gpu-that-finishes-no-work-is-taken-as-lost))

name: DM_GPU_PROBE
meaning: `0` turns off the GPU probe (on by default while the power detail is, logging only): every other power tick one fixed GPU job (one SIMD group, a dependent chain of fused multiply-adds, `gpu_probe.metal`) is timed, and the `GPU probe up to frame N` line after each `power` line gives the window's fastest, mean and slowest probe and the fastest's ratio to the session's fastest, a GPU-clock signal (`nvn_mtl.m` `mtl_gpu_probe_tick`). Kept in a player build

name: DM_GPU_TIME_SCALE
meaning: the GPU time scale of a game whose profile sets `gpu_time_scale` (Donkey Kong Bananza: 0.6144, the spans its counter reports read before NVN2 timestamps were nanoseconds), for an A/B: `1` gives the reports' true times, another value from 0.25 to 1 that factor. Each submission's reports move toward its end, which stays, between their own time and that end; the heat ladder's and the clock rescue's stretch multiply it (`nvn_heat.h` `nvn_scale_stretch_at`, `nvn_gpu_time_scale_parse`; `nvn_mtl.m` `post_run`). A game without `heat_gpu_stretch` or a refused value is a red line (`hle_nvn.c` `scale_lever`; kept in a player build)

name: DM_GUEST_FILE
meaning: `1` puts the guest's memory in sparse, unlinked files mapped shared over the guest block, `0` keeps it anonymous (`hle_svc.c`): file pages are out of `phys_footprint`, the figure iOS ends an app at, and the kernel can write them out when it needs the room. Unset: on iOS when the game's memory pool and half of it again, for the host's own memory (`DM_GUEST_FILE_HOST`), are larger than the room to the memory limit at start (the log's `[mem] guest memory` line says which), off on the Mac. The guest stays anonymous, with a `[RED]` line, when the files cannot be made, or the disk has less than `DM_GUEST_FILE_MIN_FREE` free (on the Mac that plus 8 GB)

name: DM_GUEST_FILE_CHUNK
meaning: `=<size>` (whole MB, K / M / G; default 1G, at least 64M, at most 1024 files): the size of each guest file; one file when it is not under the block's size. The stall at the system's periodic flush grows with the file (on a 16 GB M5 Mac up to 148 ms with one 20 GB file, 4 ms with 20 files of 1 GB)

name: DM_GUEST_FILE_DIR
meaning: Folder for `DM_GUEST_FILE`'s files (default the user's temporary folder; the iOS app sets it to `NSTemporaryDirectory()`)

name: DM_GUEST_FILE_HOST
meaning: `=<size>` (whole MB, K / M / G; `0` for none): the host's own memory that the iOS rule for `DM_GUEST_FILE` counts beside the game's memory pool, instead of half the pool (`hle_svc.c`, `guest_host_margin`; measured upstream from a tenth of the pool to all of it)

name: DM_GUEST_FILE_MIN_FREE
meaning: `=<size>` (whole MB, K / M / G; default 2G, `0` never): with `DM_GUEST_FILE=1`, the game is stopped (exit code 87) when the guest files' disk has less room than that: its free space less what the files' dirty pages may still take. When `f_bavail` alone is short it counts what the system can purge (`NSURLVolumeAvailableCapacityForImportantUsageKey`), as long as `f_bavail` keeps half the minimum

name: DM_GUEST_FILE_PUNCH
meaning: `0` keeps the disk blocks of guest memory the game gives back (with `DM_GUEST_FILE=1`); by default they are punched out (`F_PUNCHHOLE`, which also drops the pages): the heap's at once, the alias region's by a sweep every 10 s once they have stayed given back over a whole interval

name: DM_GUEST_FILE_SCAN
meaning: `=1` (with `DM_GUEST_FILE=1`): every 30 s a `[mem] guest file scan` line, the dirty guest pages by region (heap, alias, stack, other) and how many of them read all 0; each scan counts the dirty pages afresh first (otherwise counted every 60 s while the disk is far from `DM_GUEST_FILE_MIN_FREE`, every 10 s near it)

name: DM_GUEST_SPAWN_TEST
meaning: `=1` runs a self-test before `nnMain`: a host-started guest thread does SDK malloc / free and locks an `nn::os` mutex, and the result is logged; `=2` also keeps a resident thread

name: DM_HANDOFF_WAIT
meaning: How a same-core handoff waits for the thread it woke to block (`dm_yield_to_core_peers`, `hle_thread.c`): by default a spin of up to 20 µs, then a condition variable that thread's block wakes, with a 50 µs backstop; `=poll` the old 50 µs `nanosleep` loop, one timer wakeup per handoff; `=cv` no spin; `=spin:<µs>` (0-1000) another spin length. For a device A/B of CPU energy and wakeups

name: DM_HEAT_FORCE
meaning: the heat ladder's forced thermal state, for the Mac's test bench and an A/B's behaviour sitting: `0`-`3` for the whole session, or a timeline `state:from_s,...` (`1:60,2:240,0:420`: state 1 from 60 s after the first sample, 2 from 240 s, 0 from 420 s; before the first entry the device's own), at most 16 entries with finite times in order; anything else is a red line and the device's own state. Frame generation (`DM_FRAMEGEN`) steps aside on the rungs it brings, though it reads the device's own state itself. Logged as `[heat] DM_HEAT_FORCE: thermal state … at … s` (`nvn_heat.h` `nvn_heat_force_parse`; kept in a player build)

name: DM_HEAT_GPU_STRETCH
meaning: the heat ladder's and the GPU clock rescue's lever in a game of the Mario Kart World family (`heat_gpu_stretch on`), for an A/B: `k85,k70[,k_rescue]`, how many times longer its counter reports read the GPU time at 85%, at 70% and during a rescue, each 1 to 4 and `k70` at least `k85` (the defaults, cost following the pixel count, 1 / scale²: 1.38, 2.04, 1.78; together at most 4, the 0.5 floor). Each submission's reports move back from its end, never before the submission before it nor later than they were, so the frame's end time stays (`nvn_heat.h` `nvn_heat_stretch_parse`, `nvn_heat_stretch_ts`; `nvn_mtl.m` `post_run`). Refused values and a game without the key are a red line (`hle_nvn.c` `scale_lever`; kept in a player build)

name: DM_HEAT_STEPS
meaning: the heat ladder (NX18-X2.0 heat-ladder.md; to be the Gate's Auto scaling row): unset or `1` (the default) runs it, `0` is today's behaviour, the A arm of a heat A/B: only the 30 fps hold at thermal state 2 (its calm wait backed off 30 → 240 s) and in Low Power Mode. The resolution rungs (85%, 70%) act where the game has a live render scale lever: a build whose render-scale stubs read state +0x14 (`LIVE_SCALE`: Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom once repacked) and the Mario Kart World family (`heat_gpu_stretch on`, through the GPU time stretch, `DM_HEAT_GPU_STRETCH`); no game has an effects or 40 fps rung yet and nothing dims. `[heat]` lines log the ladder and each render scale change (`hle_nvn.c` `heat_sample`, `scale_set`, `nvn_heat.h`; kept in a player build)

name: DM_HEAT_TUNE
meaning: the heat ladder's placeholders, `key=value` pairs separated by commas, seconds unless said: `r1` (state 1 before 85%, 10), `evid` (60 not holding before 70%, effects or 40 fps, 30), `gap` (between down-steps at state 1, 30), `s2` (state 2 before 30 fps behind 70%, 15), `s2_40` (behind 40 fps, 30), `wait` / `wait_max` (restore wait, 60 doubled up to 300), `r4_wait` / `r4_wait_max` (the 30 fps hold's, 30 up to 240), `rearm` (600), `min_on` (60), `exit` (60 fitting again at state 1, 120), `dim2_off` (30), `share` (percent not holding, 10), `res1` / `res2` (0.85, 0.70). Times up to a day (86400), the waits above 0 and each first wait at most its `_max`, `share` 0-100, `res` 0.5-1; a value it refuses (an unknown key, an empty value, `nan`, `inf`, out of range) is a red line, and then none of the pairs is taken (`nvn_heat.h` `nvn_heat_tune`; kept in a player build)

name: DM_HID_LOG
meaning: `1` logs the HID button usage number of each button pressed on a raw HID gamepad (`pad_hid_mac.h`), to write a `DM_HID_MAP`

name: DM_HID_MAP
meaning: `=<map>` such as `A=1,B=2,X=4,Y=5`: which HID button usage presses each Switch button on a raw HID gamepad (names A B X Y LS RS L R ZL ZR PLUS MINUS LEFT UP RIGHT DOWN; default 8BitDo's D-input numbering by position, `pad_hid.h`); Mac only

name: DM_HID_PADS
meaning: `0` stops reading raw HID gamepads that GameController does not list, such as an 8BitDo in its own mode (`pad_hid_mac.h`); Mac only

name: DM_HID_TRACE
meaning: `1` logs the controller's start as the game sees it (`hid trace +<s>` lines, at most 400; `hle_hid.c`): each npad style event bound (the style it read, signalled or not) and signalled (the style before and after, bound or not), each style query's answer when it changes, and each npad's state read when its connected attributes change, the first read too. For a controller connected at boot that the game reads no input from until it is plugged in again (Ocarina of Time, Luigi's Mansion 3). Logging only; not filtered in player builds

name: DM_HITCH_DUMP
meaning: `=<ms>[:<s>]`: when no frame has been presented for that long (from s seconds on), logs every guest thread once per stall: wait, last SVC, pc, lr, frames and registers The first 24 stalls are dumped, then one in 10, up to 120 dumps in all.

name: DM_HLECOUNT
meaning: `=<file>` (`%d` = process ID) writes at exit a TSV of how many times the guest called each HLE function, zero counts included

name: DM_HOME_QUIT
meaning: `0` turns off quitting with the controller's Home button (Mac, on by default): held for 2 s it opens a quit prompt over the game, A quits as ⌘Q does, B or Home closes it (`home_quit.h`)

name: DM_HOME_QUIT_CAPTURE
meaning: `=<folder>`: `tests/t_home_quit_mac.m` also draws the Home button's quit prompt and hold indicator into PNG files there

name: DM_HOME_QUIT_TEXT
meaning: The texts of the Home button's quit prompt in the player's language, one per line: the hold indicator, the title, the note, the quit and the cancel button; a front end such as NX2Apple sets it ([Starting a game](frontends.md#starting-a-game)), an empty or missing line keeps the English text

name: DM_HOST_SPIN
meaning: How the host's short spin-waits wait (`dm/host/dm_spin.h`): by default on a CPU with FEAT_WFxT (M4, A18 and later) with WFET, which stops the core until the watched word's cache line is written or a few µs pass (the uniform copies' `ubc_wait` and the copy thread's poll after a burst, `nvn_rec.h`; the same-core handoff's spin, `hle_thread.c` `hand_spin`; `thr_free`'s wait for a wake in flight). Measured on an M4 Max: the same wake latency as the yield spin (42-83 ns) at about half the energy; `0` (or `yield`) keeps the old `yield` spins of fixed pass counts ([host spin-waits](reference/frame-rate.md#host-spin-waits-kept-a-core-running-flat-out))

name: DM_HTML
meaning: Folder of the offline HTML pages (default: `html` beside the RomFS; on iOS, the app's own `html` when its game files have none beside them, as in a build without the game files)

name: DM_ICON
meaning: `=<image>` gives `build_ipa.sh` another app icon (default the `icon.jpg` beside the RomFS, else the NX 18 icon in `docs/images/nx18`)

name: DM_IMPORTS
meaning: When set, logs each import the loader binds to a host function and each forced takeover

name: DM_IMU_ACC_SIGN
meaning: `-1` negates the acceleration of Switch 2 IMU samples (`GetNpadImuSamples`, `hle_hid.c`), for a test; by default it is the six-axis state's, G × 9.80665 m/s² at +0x10 of the sample (−9.8 on z lying face up), which the SDK's fusion negates into a specific force (`sdk+0x6d7334`)

name: DM_IMU_AXES
meaning: `=<map>` such as `y,-x,z`: a signed permutation of the axes of every Switch 2 IMU sample the game gets (`GetNpadImuSamples`, `hle_hid.c`), acceleration and rotation alike (rotation times its determinant, so it stays a proper rotation), for trying another frame with a real controller without a rebuild (default `x,y,z`); also through `DM_CTL`'s `env`

name: DM_IMU_DELAY
meaning: `=auto` (the default), `=0` or `=<ms>` (up to 40): how late the host plays a live controller's motion back in Switch 2 IMU samples (`GetNpadImuSamples`, `six_source` in `hle_hid.c`; `DM_SIX_DELAY` sets the six-axis states'). A source sends a sample every 15 to 30 ms while the game reads 5 ms ticks up to the present, so read at the present most ticks lie past the newest sample and can only hold it (76 to 79% of a Joy-Con 2's): a staircase for the SDK's sensor fusion, which integrates every tick. By default each stream plays back as late as the 90th percentile of how long after a sample the next one arrives over its last 32 (`motion_lag`, `motion_fusion.h`; about 30 to 34 ms for a Joy-Con 2, 15 to 18 for a DualSense, capped at 40 so a lost report does not add its stall), so every tick lies between two samples that have arrived; `0` reads at the present as before, a number fixes the delay. Only the data is late: the ticks keep their sampling numbers, and a change of delay (a new stream, a stale restart, another stream, a new setting) is slewed at 5% of the guest time passed, so the data a game takes never goes back or jumps. None while the guest clock is frozen or `DM_DETCLOCK`'s (every sample maps to one time: the newest is the state). Also through `DM_CTL`'s `env`

name: DM_IMU_GYRO_SIGN
meaning: `-1` negates the angular velocity of Switch 2 IMU samples (`GetNpadImuSamples`, `hle_hid.c`), for a test; by default it is the six-axis state's, revolutions/s × 2π rad/s at +0x1c of the sample, which the SDK's fusion takes as it is

name: DM_IMU_LOG
meaning: `=<n>`: logs every n-th raw motion sample as the host receives it, per stream (`imu raw <source> p<player> t=<host s> (<ms> before arrival) acc … G rot … rad/s`, before any axis map; sources `gc`, `hid`, `joyL` / `joyR`, `phone`) and every n-th `GetNpadImuSamples` answer (`imu out h=<handle> k=<count> s=<first>..<last> acc … m/s2 gyro … rad/s live|synthetic (<n> held, delay <ms>)`, the newest sample, how many of the answer's ticks held a sample instead of lying between two, and the playout delay `DM_IMU_DELAY` used), for comparing a real controller with the host's synthetic samples (`hle_hid.c`); `1` for a minute's session, about 20,000 lines

name: DM_IMU_NOISE
meaning: `0` leaves out (a single number scales it, `=<deg/s>,<mG>` sets each spread; also through `DM_CTL`'s `env`) the white noise of Switch 2 IMU samples (`GetNpadImuSamples`, `hle_hid.c`): by default each of the host's own samples (no live controller; a live one carries its own noise, and only its held ticks, those with no change of their own, get a tenth of the spread so no two in a row are identical) carries some noise (gyro 0.1 deg/s, acceleration 0.05 mG per axis, fixed per tick and device): with none the SDK's sensor fusion keeps resetting and never calibrates its gyro bias; more acceleration noise than that and its stillness detector never finds the controller still. On by default because the fusion is the SDK's own code, so every Switch 2 title on that SDK needs it, and it touches only `GetNpadImuSamples` (the six-axis states keep exact values)

name: DM_JC1
meaning: `0` stops the Mac host from reading original (Switch 1) Joy-Cons from their HID reports (`pad_jc1_mac.h`: buttons, sticks, motion, rumble, player lights, each Joy-Con a device of its own) and gives them back to GameController, without motion and with no lone Joy-Con; on by default

name: DM_JC1_LOG
meaning: `=1` logs each Joy-Con's handshake, its factory IMU and stick calibrations and its failed output reports; `=2` adds one line a second with the gravity and the rotation the host hands the game, per Joy-Con, `=3` the raw counts against the origin and the learned rest instead; each also logs every handshake the watchdog repeats; Mac only

name: DM_JC1_SIDE
meaning: `=L` or `=R` picks which half of a pair of original Joy-Cons also feeds the player's merged six-axis stream, which a game that supports no Joy-Con style reads (the default: the right one, or the left one when the right one is not streaming); each half always feeds its own Joy-Con's stream; Mac only

name: DM_JCMS_LOG
meaning: `=1` logs the game's Joy-Con mouse sensor and pointer calls (JcmsState reads, Nmouse handles, states and positions), at most once a second each

name: DM_JIT_CAPTURE
meaning: Folder the Mac host writes what a game's `nn::jit` plugin makes to, one `<key>.jit` per request, for `dm/tools/jit_capture.py`; the NSP script sets it

name: DM_JIT_LOG
meaning: `1` logs every `nn::jit` `GenerateCode` request

name: DM_JIT_MISS_DUMP
meaning: Folder for the input of each `nn::jit` request a served image lacks

name: DM_JIT_SERVE
meaning: Folder of a `nn::jit` image (`jit.img`, `jit.tsv`, `jit.out`): the Mac serves requests from it as the iOS app does, and the plugin does not run

name: DM_KBD
meaning: `=<text>`: the system keyboard returns that text as OK without showing an input box; unset with no window, it returns cancel

name: DM_KBD_PLAYER
meaning: `own` makes the Mac keyboard player 1 on its own, with controllers from player 2 on (by default the first controller shares player 1 with the keyboard)

name: DM_KEYS
meaning: Scripted input: `<seconds or f<frame>>:<key>[+key][~hold or ~f<frames>][*count/interval],…` presses buttons, sticks, touches and `Shake` at those times; `=@<file>` reads the steps from the file

name: DM_LANG
meaning: Game language as a language code (default `en-US`; the iOS app sets the one the IPA was packed with)

name: DM_LAUNCHER
meaning: `0` skips the iOS settings screen or the Mac settings window and starts the game at once, with the saved choices (on the Mac also `--no-launcher`); it skips the launchers' cloud-save check too, so the newer save wins when both changed (the iPhone logs `the cloud save was not checked`)

name: DM_LAUNCH_PARAM
meaning: File whose bytes `oe::TryPopLaunchParameter` returns once; `oe::ExecuteProgram` sets it for the program it starts; a relaunch removes it

name: DM_LINK_SIM
meaning: `1` (Mac) drives the display-link path from a timer of the host's own at the link's rate, taking the layer's drawables itself, for measuring on a Mac whose screen is locked or asleep (where the system's link calls back nothing and every frame goes through the rescue path); presented times stay the system's

name: DM_LINK_VTICK
meaning: `0` keeps the system's display-link rate on 144 or 165 Hz Mac screens; by default the link counts only the refreshes nearest a steady 1/60 s clock

name: DM_LOADHASH
meaning: `=1` logs an address-independent SHA-256 per module after loading

name: DM_LOGO
meaning: `=<image>` gives `build_ipa.sh` the game's logo, which the launcher shows in place of its name: `dm/logo.png` in the app (a PNG copied as it is, a WebP converted with sips to a PNG keeping its alpha, longest side at most 1200; a failure leaves the app without one); the NSP script sets it to `<build folder>/art/logo.png` (`--logo`, else SteamGridDB's with a key); without it the launcher shows the name

name: DM_LOG_COST
meaning: `1` measures what the log itself costs (`hle_bigstack.c` `dm_log`): every 5 s one `log cost over …` line with the lines written, the time spent writing them per second of the run (all threads: formatting, the lock and the write), the slowest single line and how many took over 1 ms. For a run with many logging switches on, to judge their overhead. Two clock reads a line while on

name: DM_LONGFRAME
meaning: `0` turns off the long-frame log (on by default), a line for a frame over 20 ms or with GPU time over 16.7 ms that is clearly above recent frames and longer than the hold of the frame step or the game's present interval asked for (a frame held 2 or 3 vsyncs ends with `; hold K × V ms`)

name: DM_LOW_POWER_CAP
meaning: Low Power Mode at 30 fps (iOS; the launcher's Performance row, and the in-game menu while the game runs): `1` holds 30 fps while iOS Low Power Mode is on, for the games the thermal cap covers (the frame step, an engine limiter the host writes at 60 and a display-mode 60 fps present cap without a limiter; a 120 fps target already runs at 60 on iOS), back to the chosen rate 30 s after Low Power Mode is turned off, at the game's real speed; a game the host does not pace (Persona 5 Royal) reads it too, with the heat ladder's sample, but nothing is held there (`[heat]` lines, no hold state); `0` or unset (the default; on in the Battery preset) leaves the frame rate alone in Low Power Mode. Before X2.0 it was on unless `0`. Independent of `DM_THERMAL_CAP`

name: DM_MANUAL
meaning: `=<file.pdf>` gives `build_ipa.sh` the game's manual, `dm/manual.pdf` in the app, which the launcher opens; the NSP script sets it for `--manual` / `MANUAL`

name: DM_MEASURE_LOCK
meaning: `=<file>`: `scripts/regress.py`'s default `--lock`, the measuring lock `scripts/bench.py --lock` shares: held only while a game runs, and the harness's shader builds pause while another process holds it

name: DM_MEMORY_TRIM
meaning: `0` only logs the system's memory pressure (footprint and the room left; the front ends' dispatch source or `DM_CTL pressure`) and gives nothing back; by default a warning or critical level also releases the idle graphics caches at the next submission's start (render-target heaps waiting for reuse, upload slot blocks above 4 MB, packaged-texture spares, feedback snapshots, effects that are off) and sweeps the guest's files

name: DM_MEMSTAT
meaning: `=<tsv>` writes one line per second of memory accounting: footprint, Metal allocation and resident and charged memory by region class (guest, code, malloc, gpu, …); on iOS a relative path is under `Documents`, and `Documents/env.txt` can set it

name: DM_MEMSTAT_DUMP
meaning: `=<seconds>`: with `DM_MEMSTAT`, at that second writes every VM region of 1 MiB or more to `<tsv>.regions`

name: DM_MEM_CAP_GB
meaning: `=<GB>`: the memory watchdog exits when resident memory exceeds that many GB (default 24 on the Mac, none on iOS; `0` turns it off)

name: DM_MEM_GUEST
meaning: `=1`: the memory line adds `guest charged N MB` (a walk of the guest block's VM regions, each VM object counted once); off by default because the walk held Ocarina of Time's frames 24-45 ms on the Mac each time the line printed

name: DM_METAL_CAPTURE
meaning: `=1` makes `build_ipa.sh` produce a build that can write GPU frame captures (`MetalCaptureEnabled` in `Info.plist`), for `DM_GPU_CAPTURE`; such a build always runs the GPU capture profile, with no pipeline archive

name: DM_METAL_HUD
meaning: `1` shows Apple's Metal performance HUD over the game (frame rate, frame and GPU time, memory)

name: DM_MOD_FPS
meaning: `1` puts the switchable frame-rate mod in place when the game starts (the launcher's High frame rate; the NSP script's mods folder, `loader.c` `dm_mod_variants_apply`)

name: DM_MOD_ULTRAWIDE
meaning: `1` puts the switchable ultrawide mod in place when the game starts and stretches the picture over a screen wider than 16:9 (the launcher's Ultrawide, iPhone and iPad; left off on a screen no wider than 16:9)

name: DM_MOTION
meaning: `0` ignores live motion: every six-axis sensor lies flat as before (a shake still plays), and neither controllers' motion sensors nor the phone's device motion are switched on (`hle_hid.c`, `motion_apple.h`, `DmGamepad.m`); the NSP script's `--no-motion` (`MOTION = False`) builds it in

name: DM_MOTION_ACC_SIGN
meaning: `-1` flips only GameController's acceleration, for a source that reports the specific force (+1 G up at rest) instead of the gravity direction (`motion_fusion.h`); phone and raw HID samples are already in the Switch frame

name: DM_MOTION_AXES
meaning: `=<map>` such as `x,-z,y`: maps Apple's controller axes to the Switch's, a signed permutation applied to acceleration and rotation alike, for a controller whose axes differ (default `x,y,z`; phone and raw HID samples are already in the Switch frame)

name: DM_MOTION_GAIN
meaning: `=<gain>`: how fast the orientation is pulled toward the measured gravity, in rad/s per unit error (default 0.5; `0` integrates the gyro alone)

name: DM_MOTION_HID
meaning: On the Mac, `0` disables the passive Switch Pro Controller HID motion fallback (`motion_pro_mac.h`); enabled by default when exactly one physical Pro and one GameController Pro can use the same player slot; usable GameController motion takes priority

name: DM_MOTION_LOG
meaning: `=1` logs player 1's mapped motion sample once a second per source (phone / GameController / controller HID; acceleration in G, gyro in revolutions/s), for checking the axes: flat and still reads acc 0 0 -1

name: DM_MOVIE_RESTART
meaning: `1` / `0`: a VideoToolbox movie session (AV1, H.264) that fails with kVTInvalidSessionErr (-12903), as iOS gives once it has ended the hardware decoder while the app was in the background, is dropped and a new one starts at the stream's next key frame, the last picture shown again until then at the skipped units' times, with one `[movie] … restarting` line, instead of failing every later picture with a red line. Default: the profile's `movie_restart` (Ocarina of Time on); `0` in `Documents/env.txt` turns it off (`hle_movie.c` `movie_vt_restart`)

name: DM_MOVIE_TRACE
meaning: When set, the movie decoder logs every call with its thread and decoder (by default the first 12 calls, then every 2^k-th)

name: DM_MSL_DIR
meaning: Parent folder of the shader libraries: NVN loads from `b-<chain version>/` or the one file `b-<chain version>.img` beneath it, Vulkan from `vk/`, GL from `gl/`; the app and the Mac launcher set it

name: DM_NDVE_ENGINE
meaning: nn::ndve's movie network (Ocarina of Time's title and opening movies): unset, the platform's default, MetalFX on iOS and iPadOS (`mfx`) and the host's kernels on the Mac (`1`). `mfx` skips the network's 12 dispatches after the colour conversion and the resampler, and MetalFX's spatial scaler writes the 2560x1440 canvas (or a 2048x1152 one) from the converted 1920x1080 picture (about 15.7 billion multiply-adds a movie frame less, and the network's 92 MB of tensors not made unless it runs after all; loses the network's learned clean-up and detail); `1` runs the network as the host's kernels (dm/gfx/msl/ndve_engine.metal: the same output as the game's, about half the frame's GPU time on an M4 Pro), so `DM_NDVE_ENGINE=1` in `Documents/env.txt` is the network side of an iPhone A/B (a player build keeps the line); `0` runs the game's translated dispatches; `ab` alternates MetalFX (its on phases) with the host's network with `DM_AB`; `check` runs the game's dispatches and the host's network beside them and logs every 300 frames how many texels of the two differ. Both host paths take only the model they were written for, bound by its shaders' keys and its weights' layout, and MetalFX falls back to the host's network with one line when it cannot draw or something other than the resampler reads the network's image first (under `ab` that line says the A/B is void from there) (docs/reference/shaders.md, The NDVE movie network by the host, and The NDVE movie network skipped for MetalFX on the iPhone)

name: DM_NICK
meaning: The account nickname the game sees (default `Player`); set by the Gate from the NX 18 Profile (`NX18Profile.swift`); never logged (env echoes show `(set)`)

name: DM_NRO
meaning: `0` turns off loading of the NRO modules the game's NRR files register (on by default): every `nn::ro::LoadModule` then fails

name: DM_NRO_CAPTURE
meaning: folder: a `nn::ro::LoadModule` with no rewritten copy writes the image to `<folder>/<SHA-256>.nro` and ends the run (the NSP script's capture of an NRO the game decodes at run time)

name: DM_NRO_DIR
meaning: folder of NROs the shader split reads like `main`, and in which it finds a CRA archive's file table (the NSP script sets it for a captured NRO)

name: DM_NVN_ACQ_DEFER
meaning: `0`: the window acquire takes its display wait itself for every game, as before; by default, once a game has waited on an acquired image's sync on the CPU, an acquire with a sync returns at once and the first `nvnSyncWait` on that sync takes the wait (or the window's next acquire, when none does), as on the console (`hle_nvn.c` `acq_defer_t`; upstream `c17a54984`). Kept in a player build for its phone A/B

name: DM_NVN_ACQ_NEXT
meaning: `0`: an acquired window image's sync is the commits at the acquire again (`mtl_last_fence()`); by default it is the GPU end of the first present after the image's last one, as Horizon hands the image back (`hle_nvn.c`, `nvn_sync_set_present` in `nvn_queue.inc`). Kept in a player build for its phone A/B

name: DM_NVN_ALLOCPROF
meaning: `=1` charges Metal allocation growth to each replayed op type and function, and logs command allocator sizes and each new texture (serial, size, format, storage); `=2` also gives each main submission a fresh command allocator and reports command memory by operation, by encoder, by submission size and the indirect-count multi-draws encoded

name: DM_NVN_ALLOC_TRIM
meaning: `0` keeps every command allocator of the main submissions for the whole session, as before; by default an allocator past the three made at start is released, the last first, once the GPU is done with it and no submission has taken it for 600 frames (`nvn_mtl.m` `mtl_sub_begin`; after MacNativeGames 99e42bc8 (MIT): an allocator keeps the command memory of the largest frame it served, none of it in the residency set)

name: DM_NVN_API
meaning: `=<major>.<minor>` overrides the NVN API version `nvnDeviceGetInteger` reports (by default decided by the SDK version or the profile's `device_api`: 55.15 for SDK 11 and later, 53.313 before)

name: DM_NVN_ARENA_SHARE
meaning: `0` gives each submission per-frame arena blocks of its own, as before; by default a submission goes on in the 4 MB block the one before it ended in while that has room, so the blocks follow the bytes in flight, not the submissions in flight

name: DM_NVN_ARENA_TRIM
meaning: `0` keeps every per-frame arena block of 32 MB or less for the rest of the run, as before; by default one the GPU is done with goes once no submission has used it for 600 submissions, and at a memory trim at once, down to 4 blocks

name: DM_NVN_ARGS_DRV
meaning: `0` makes a 2,560-byte c0 / c2 driver bank (cleared, then filled: c2 about 305 handle words, c0 the storage table, point size, base instance and sample rows) for every argument block of a shader that reads one, as before (kept in player builds, for the phone A/B). By default each graphics stage keeps its last c0 and c2 bank of the submission and every block that reads one takes it while the stage's binding history (`g_args_pk`) holds every hard change since it was made and none of them is a kind it is made from (textures and samplers for c2; storage buffers, the base instance and the sample count for c0); when the changes are all in the history the bank is copied and only the words they move are written again (the texture and sampler slots that moved; the storage table; the base instance; the sample rows); else it is made whole. Not compute (its dispatch size, and an indirect dispatch's counts written into the bank). Mac micro-benchmark, a shader with 16 textures, 8 samplers, c0 and c2: a texture-only partial patch 505 -> 300 ns, a full encode after a texture or storage change 790 -> 465 ns; the `[args-stats]` levers line counts the banks reused, patched and made

name: DM_NVN_ARGS_PARTIAL
meaning: `0` encodes a shader's argument block in full whenever a texture, sampler, storage-buffer or base-instance binding of its stage changed, as before (kept in player builds, for the phone A/B). By default such a block, when it is one a reuse would take but for those changes (of this pass with no new pass or program since, or kept by the cross-pass rule) and every hard change since it was a texture, sampler or storage binding of its stage (a short history per stage, `g_args_pk`, of 8 entries whose oldest are joined when it fills: any other hard change makes the next encode full), is copied and only the entries made from what changed are written again: the texture slots that moved (with their fix-ups: `tex_fit`, `tex_float_fit`, `tbuf_*`, dummies) and the samplers (all of them for a shader with border twins, and the border block), the handle arrays and c2, the storage buffers (with their storage-write notes) and c0, c0 for a base instance change, and the uniform slots when they moved too; vertex and fragment stages only, and only for shaders with no handles or addresses read from uniform memory, no raw pool table and no geometry emulation buffers. Also with it on: the uniform patch takes buffer textures, dynamic and driver-table handle arrays and pool shaders, and a shader that reads no uniform keeps its block after a uniform change (both were full encodes counted as `ubo_unpatchable`). The "argument blocks per frame" line counts the partial patches among the patched; `DM_NVN_ARGS_STATS=1` adds their counts by kind and time (`nvn_mtl.m` `args_partial`, `pk_take`)

name: DM_NVN_ARGS_REGCHK
meaning: `0` encodes every argument block in full after any texture or sampler registration, as before (kept in player builds, for the phone A/B). By default, when every registration since the last binding sync is a texture or sampler registration read back from its note (none overwritten, no memory pool, which remaps the uniform and storage addresses every block holds) and no guest write or replaced object came with it, the sync stamps each registered ID instead of moving every hard binding generation: a block from before it is reused or patched only after none of the texture, image and sampler IDs its stage's slots name was stamped since (`nvn_mtl.m` `args_rck`); a shader whose bindings name IDs any other way (handles or addresses read from uniform memory, the raw pool table, handle arrays) is encoded in full as before, and a pool shader (TEXP / SAMPP) takes its tables again through a partial patch (`PK_POOL`, also after another table's build or patch) instead of a full encode. Guest writes and replaced objects still encode every block in full. Mac micro-benchmark, 16 textures, 8 samplers, 4 uniform slots: an encode after a registration elsewhere 245-280 ns in full, 66-72 ns checked and reused; the `[args-stats]` levers line counts the syncs taken by ID and the blocks found current, stale or not checkable

name: DM_NVN_ARGS_STATS
meaning: `=1` (measurement only; kept in player builds) logs, each window of the "argument blocks per frame" line, four to six `[args-stats]` lines, per frame: full argument-block encodes by the reason the shader's block could not be reused or patched (the stage's last binding change: a texture, sampler, storage, image or push-constant binding, a pool base, a texture/sampler registration or a memory pool, a guest write, a replaced texture, a queue switch, restored state, a feedback snapshot, a host compute or draw encoder, a game dispatch encoder, a drain, an upgrade; or after only a new pass or program, a first encode, another submission's block, a kind never kept across passes, a base instance, a pool table, a uniform change on a shader that cannot be patched, an ID the block holds registered since or kinds the registration check does not take: `reg_id`, `reg_unchecked`), patches by uniform binding or inline update, the binding syncs by what moved, draws with a texture/sampler registration since the previous draw, `encode_args_`'s time for full, patch and reuse calls and the full encodes' split by binding kind with their fix-ups (texture lookups past the cached view, a texture made, uploaded again or its view made, in a group of their own whatever binding asked), with partial patches on (`DM_NVN_ARGS_PARTIAL`), a line of partial patches by kind written (texture, sampler, storage, base instance, uniform, pool tables), their time by class and the texture/sampler bindings they wrote against those they kept, and the full encodes counted `ubo_unpatchable` by the first binding kind that kept the shader off the uniform patch; a levers line: pool table lookups by how they ended (memo, first check, patch kept, patched, standing, walk) and handle table lookups (kept for the pass, read again, the same entries, built) with their time per call, the pool tables' patch path split (patch paths and the IDs each took again; collecting them, resolving them, texture lookups past the cached view, table copies; read-mark scans; whole builds), the c0 / c2 driver banks reused, patched and made, the registration syncs taken by ID or by every block and the blocks the check found current, stale or not checkable; with `DM_NVN_BINDLESS=1` the slot tables line (see there); and the 10 shaders with the most full encodes; at start the device's `maxArgumentBufferSamplerCount`. Clock reads inflate the times (shares hold); off, nothing is counted (`nvn_mtl.m` `ast_fresh_why`, `mtl_args_stats_log`)

name: DM_NVN_ARGS_XPASS
meaning: `0` reuses a shader's argument block only within the render pass that encoded it, as before; by default a block is reused in a later pass of the same submission, and after another program's draws, while its stage's bindings, registrations, guest writes and replaced textures leave it as it was (a hard binding generation: a new pass or program alone does not move it), with the pass's sample count, base instance and pool tables checked as before, and for a block holding copies of memory or handles read from uniform memory no write queued or made since; never across submissions (the arena holding it is reclaimed only after its submission). The per-frame TSV's `@args_xpass` counts the reuses and patches only this allowed (`nvn_mtl.m` `args_xpass_ok`)

name: DM_NVN_BARRIER
meaning: How draw passes are ordered: `full` (default) waits for all earlier GPU work, `game` only for the previous pass's fragment stage unless the game's barrier since the last pass ordered primitives or indirect data (a fragment-only one, such as 0x12, keeps the overlap), `ab` alternates with the `DM_AB` phases

name: DM_NVN_BCRT_CACHE
meaning: `0` takes the shadow of a render target in a depth or compressed texture (a D16 texture drawn through an R16 view, a BC4 one through an RGBA16UI view) by the attachment's number in the pass, made again whenever that number's format or size changes, as before; by default shadows are kept and reused by format and size (up to 8, 64 MiB; one unused for 5 s goes at the next submission), and the residency line counts them (`render-target shadows: passes, made, reused, retired`)

name: DM_NVN_BC_ALIAS
meaning: Set 0 to send copies to an uncompressed alias instead of its block-compressed storage, for an A/B check; default 1

name: DM_NVN_BF_WANT
meaning: `=<file>`: appends the key of each fragment shader whose passes could not be merged for lack of a readable-tile version to that file, once per key

name: DM_NVN_BG_LOOK
meaning: `0` looks up the bases of the pipeline look-ahead's predicted keys on the submit thread again, each making its pulling stand-in there (`hybrid_get`), as before the port of upstream 9d3a58364; `ab` alternates with the `DM_AB` phases. By default (`1`) each predicted key's base lookup goes to a background worker (`pso_bg_look`), which admits the key's build when neither its base nor its pulling base is there.
