For the phone A/B of Ocarina of Time's first-visit holds; the lookup-wait fix (upstream edc7eff9c) stays on either way (frame-rate.md, Predicted keys' bases looked up on the submit thread)

name: DM_NVN_BG_PURGE
meaning: `0` keeps the host's textures non-volatile while the app is in the background (`dm_gfx_suspend`), as before; by default, once the GPU has drained, its packaged textures outside heaps that the GPU has not written are marked purgeable so they leave the footprint (render targets and GPU-written textures stay non-volatile: their content is only on the GPU), and coming back the ones the system emptied are uploaded again (`nvn_mtl.m` `mtl_bg_purge`). The footprint is logged going and coming back either way. Kept in player builds

name: DM_NVN_BINDLESS
meaning: `=1` (measurement only in stage 1 of NX18-X2.0 bindless-plan.md; off by default, kept in player builds for the phone run) keeps a slot table for the fragment stage beside the slot path and checks it at every fragment encode that resolves textures or samplers (`nvn_mtl.m` `bl_note`): an entry per texture slot (combined and separate, a sampled 2D, 2D array, cube, cube array or 3D texture) and sampler slot (no border twin), holding what the slot path wrote (`tex_resolve` / `samp_resolve`), current while its handle, declared type and class and its epoch hold (registration, guest-write, storage and view generations, the submission); a version is copied into the arena when it moved (`bl_build`), and a shader whose last check saw the version, its stage's texture / sampler binding generation and the epoch would take it without a look. Shaders still read their slots: nothing drawn changes. With `DM_NVN_ARGS_STATS=1` an `[args-stats] slot tables` line gives per frame the encodes checked and those that would take the version without a look, the converted bindings the slot path resolved against the entries the table path would have resolved (the share the tables would replace, in all encodes and in full encodes, with the full encodes' texture and sampler time it stands for), slot-bound texture / sampler bindings, feedback snapshots (a draw's own version), versions built and their KB, new epochs by what moved, the checks' own time, and mismatches (a current entry different from the slot path's value, or an entry moved under a version taken without a look: logged `[RED]`, must be 0)

name: DM_NVN_BLEND_ZERO
meaning: `0` leaves a NaN or Inf colour under a zero blend weight to Apple's blender, which stores NaN; by default a pixel shader returns it as 0 where the draw's blend state gives its source colour a zero weight on a floating-point target, as NVIDIA's blender does with the option NVN's driver sets

name: DM_NVN_BORDER_KEEP
meaning: 1 keeps the border corrections in every pipeline, as before the DMSH_BORDER_FC specialization: a wrong border colour with the specialization, or its cost (ab with DM_AB)

name: DM_NVN_CACHE_VOLATILE
meaning: `0` keeps idle reuse-cache entries non-volatile, as before; by default an entry idle for 250 ms in a reuse cache whose content nothing reads again (render-target heaps waiting for reuse, the upload staging pool's blocks, same-pass feedback snapshots after 30 submissions unused and once their last submission's fence has passed) is marked `MTLPurgeableStateVolatile`, so it leaves the app's footprint and the system may take it under pressure; taken again it is made non-volatile first, and one the system emptied is dropped and made again (`nvn_mtl.m` `cv_mark`, `cv_back`). Packaged-texture spares, arena blocks and live textures are never marked. The memory line counts them (`idle cache entries volatile`). Kept in player builds

name: DM_NVN_CAPTURE
meaning: `=<frame>:1:<path>` writes that frame (from its first submit to its present) to one file: pool bytes, registries, program keys, the textures whose content lives only in Metal, each submission's records with pointers relocatable, and the presented frame's SHA-256 and pixels; `dm/gfx/tests/nvn_replay` replays it ([development.md](development.md#frame-capture-and-replay))

name: DM_NVN_CBDUMP
meaning: `=<dir>`: saves each draw's whole uniform blocks as `F<frame>_p<pass>_st<stage>_cb<slot>_<address>.bin`, and the source bytes of buffer-to-3D-texture copies, with `DM_NVN_PASSDUMP`

name: DM_NVN_CBDUMP_KEY
meaning: `=<shader key>`: limits `DM_NVN_CBDUMP` to draws using that shader; for a vertex shader key also saves the draw's vertex streams and index buffer

name: DM_NVN_CBLOG
meaning: `=1` logs the command memory the game adds to command buffers (`AddCommandMemory`: the first 60, then every 500th) and the out-of-memory callbacks

name: DM_NVN_CLEARED_LOAD
meaning: `0` loads a colour attachment the pass clears whole before any draw writes it, as before; by default, for a pass a draw opens (with `DM_NVN_UNWRITTEN_LOAD` on), the forward scan that finds colour attachments no draw writes (`ldc_scan`) also finds those whose first write is a clear of all four channels over the whole attachment: they load as DontCare, and the clear, drawn as a triangle into the pass, then covers every pixel; a clear that turns out partial ends the pass first and the next one loads it, as before (`nvn_mtl.m` `ldc_plan`, `clear_color_tri`). Kept in player builds; [Attachment loads and stores the next operations make unneeded](reference/frame-rate.md#attachment-loads-and-stores-the-next-operations-make-unneeded)

name: DM_NVN_CLEARLOG
meaning: `=1` logs the first 40 colour clears drawn as a triangle (inside a pass, with a partial channel mask or a partial scissor)

name: DM_NVN_CMDSTAT
meaning: `=1` logs every 300 frames the command recording usage: bytes and records per frame, command memory segment sizes, out-of-memory callbacks, host segments, count and bytes per command type

name: DM_NVN_COUNT
meaning: `1` counts every NVN call (the counting trampolines) and writes the per-frame call lines; off by default (on with a `DM_NVN_TSV` table that has call rows), the count is an atomic add all recording threads share

name: DM_NVN_CPUPROF
meaning: 1 records CPU wall/time/instruction totals by renderer operation; off by default.

name: DM_NVN_CSH_PRESCAN
meaning: `0` runs the compute-hoist scan at every pass's first draw even when no dispatch follows (as before; for timing)

name: DM_NVN_CS_HOIST
meaning: `0` makes a compute dispatch between the draws of a pass end it (on by default: the dispatch runs ahead of the pass when that changes nothing the draws before it read)

name: DM_NVN_CUBE_ALT
meaning: `0` draws a profile's `pass_alternate` `cube:<colour>` passes every frame (the Quality preset sets it); by default each level and face of such a cube target (Donkey Kong Bananza's environment cube mip chain and filters) keeps the previous frame's picture on every other frame it runs in a row (`nvn_pass_alt.h`, `nvn_mtl.m` `rp_begin_ex_`). Taken at the next frame. Also from `Documents/env.txt`, player builds too ([A pass drawn every other frame](reference/rendering.md#a-pass-drawn-every-other-frame))

name: DM_NVN_CUT
meaning: `=<draws>`: the replay commits its command buffer every that many draws, between passes (default 64; `0` one command buffer per submission, except the cut after a buffer-to-texture copy)

name: DM_NVN_CUT_BUSY
meaning: `=0`: a segment boundary commits whatever the GPU is doing (the default commits only when earlier work has reported back, keeping the boundary's GPU timestamp otherwise)

name: DM_NVN_CUT_EVENT
meaning: `0` makes a segment cut (`sub_cut`, and the long-pass split, `pass_split_try`) read the commit feedback's count of command buffers still running again, as before (with `DM_NVN_ENC_THREAD`; by default it reads the GPU's own event behind each of the encode thread's commits, written about 0.04 ms after the work's end where the feedback runs 0.08-1.2 ms after it, and the commits recorded but not yet on the queue); `ab` alternates with the `DM_AB` phases; kept in player builds. The `segment cuts` line counts the cuts the event let through while the feedback still counted work (`nvn_mtl.m` `cut_busy`, `nvn_rec.h` `rec_gpu_busy`)

name: DM_NVN_CUT_HOLD
meaning: `0` keeps a segment boundary open while earlier work still runs, as before (with `DM_NVN_ENC_THREAD` and `DM_NVN_SUB_MERGE`; by default the replay cuts there all the same and the encode thread holds the segment's command buffer with the submissions it holds, committing them together the moment the GPU runs out of work: at an encoder's end, at the start of each block of records, or within 50 µs while nothing is recorded); a copy's cut still commits at once; `ab` alternates with the `DM_AB` phases; kept in player builds. Logs a `segment cuts up to frame N` line every 300 frames: cuts made per frame, those handed over to be held, and boundaries kept open ([A segment boundary kept open while the GPU finishes earlier work](reference/frame-rate.md#a-segment-boundary-kept-open-while-the-gpu-finishes-earlier-work); `nvn_mtl.m` `sub_cut`, `nvn_rec.h` `RO_COMMIT`)

name: DM_NVN_DEPTHOVR
meaning: `=<fragment shader key prefix>,…`: those draws compare depth with `ALWAYS`; with `DM_NVN_HILITE`, tells "the depth test rejects every fragment" from "nothing rasterizes"

name: DM_NVN_DEPTH_LAZY
meaning: `1` turns on, `0` off; by default on on the iPhone and iPad (the X2.0 test round) and the profile's `depth_lazy` on the Mac (off for every game for now): a new single-sample, single-level 2D Depth16Unorm or Depth32Float texture of 64 MB or more is made a placement sparse texture with no tile mapped, which reads 0 everywhere as a newly zeroed one does, and each 64 KB tile is mapped and zeroed only where the GPU is about to write something other than 0: under a depth-writing draw's scissor and viewport, a scissored clear to another value, and the whole texture for a copy, a texture clear through a colour view, an image binding or a colour view (`nvn_mtl.m` `lz_make`, `lz_map`, `lz_draw`). A whole clear to another value than 0 (a load action or a texture clear of the whole level) makes it a normal texture instead, not zeroed (`lz_whole`), as every tile would be mapped, unless its mapped tiles and the placement heaps' free ones hold most of it (`lz_whole_pays`: the heaps are never freed), which then map the rest. Tiles stay mapped while the texture lives. Logs a `lazy depth texture ser=…` line for each such texture (size, format, MB not backed), a line when its mapped tiles reach each quarter, one when a whole clear makes it a normal texture or maps the rest instead, and `lazy depth (…)` totals every 3600 frames while they change and at exit. A GPU without placement sparse depth textures makes them as before, with one line. Kept in player builds for the iPhone A/B ([Large depth textures that are only sampled take their whole size](reference/memory.md#large-depth-textures-that-are-only-sampled-take-their-whole-size))

name: DM_NVN_DIRECT_UPLOAD
meaning: 0 disables bounded direct RGBA16F array uploads and keeps staged copies; on by default for supported non-sparse textures.

name: DM_NVN_DIRTYCHECK
meaning: `=1` fully hashes pool content on every use to find changes the dirty-page tracking missed

name: DM_NVN_DIRTY_INDEX
meaning: `0` makes the dirty-page tracker's page-fault hook, host pre-write hook and containing-range lookup (`find_span`) scan every registered memory pool for the ones holding an address, as before; by default (`1`) they find them through an address index (sorted by start, binary search, rewritten off the signal path at each pool registration or retirement and read lock-free), the same pools and the same claims. Read at the first pool registration; kept in player builds for its A/B. The packaged textures line's `fault hook N/s, M ms/s, T us each (index|scan)` gives the hook's cost either way ([the fault hook found its pools by scanning them all](reference/frame-rate.md#the-write-fault-hook-scanned-every-memory-pool); `nvn_dirty.c` `idx_find`, `idx_edit`)

name: DM_NVN_DISPATCH_OWN
meaning: `=1` gives every compute dispatch a compute encoder of its own with full barriers, as before (by default dispatches share the copy encoder)

name: DM_NVN_DISPATCH_RANGE
meaning: How a game's compute dispatch in the copy encoder is ordered. By default (`2`, ported from S2Arm a51b43f7, after NXNative 547c5db6) a dispatch whose ranges are known gets a barrier only when the game called `nvnCommandBufferBarrier` since the dispatch before it, when it touches a range a copy wrote or read since the encoder's last barrier, or when the dispatch tables are full; copies are checked against what dispatches wrote and read. `1` (or `range`): dispatches are checked against each other's ranges too, the rule of S2Arm 116fe90e: a barrier comes before one only when its storage buffers, uniform buffers or sampled textures' storage overlap memory written (or, for its storage buffers, read) since the last barrier. Either way a shader with images, global memory, buffer textures or handles it reads from memory, and every indirect dispatch, keeps the barrier and counts as writing everything (`dispatch_ranges`). `0` puts a barrier before every dispatch, as before both; `ab` alternates `1` and `2` with the `DM_AB` phases. Kept in player builds, for the iPhone A/B ([rendering.md](reference/rendering.md#compute-dispatches-ordered-by-the-games-barriers)). Not a player setting

name: DM_NVN_DLSS_BILINEAR
meaning: `=1` draws every DLSS evaluation with the bilinear stand-in, to tell MetalFX's part in a GPU fault or stall

name: DM_NVN_DS_DEAD_STORE
meaning: `0` stores every depth / stencil plane a pass wrote, as before; by default a pass's depth or stencil plane is not stored (DontCare) when the rest of the submission's recorded stream, from the op that ended the pass, reaches a clear of that plane of the same texture through the same view over the whole level with only state, target and buffer-update operations before it (no draw, dispatch, copy, texture clear, event, query or conditional rendering; no other texture object over its memory; `nvn_mtl.m` `ls_dead_scan`, `sd_finish`). Only GPU-only pools' textures (not over a buffer, not sparse or lazily backed), not in clear-only, layered, slice-merged, face-split or window-area passes, and not while the profile's `pass_alternate` `<W>x<H>` shapes are on. Kept in player builds; [Attachment loads and stores the next operations make unneeded](reference/frame-rate.md#attachment-loads-and-stores-the-next-operations-make-unneeded)

name: DM_NVN_DUAL_WANT
meaning: `=<file>`: appends the key of each pixel shader a pipeline blends with its output 1 as the second source, while it has no dual-source entry point, to that file, once per key (the profile's `dual_want.tsv`)

name: DM_NVN_EDGE_COLD
meaning: `0` takes a packaged texture's edge bytes (the storage's first and last host pages, shared with other data) at every upload, reading their pages in if they are out of memory. By default they are left out when either page is out (`mincore`): the upload deswizzles on the GPU, so that copy was the CPU's first read of those pages and a page-in on the submit thread at area loads. A page the game writes beside a texture often is in memory, so those writes are still kept from re-uploads; a cold one written later re-uploads the texture once (`nvn_mtl.m` `pkg_edges_take_`, `pages_incore`). An `[edges]` line every 600 frames counts the uploads left without them. Player builds keep it

name: DM_NVN_ENC_LABEL
meaning: `=1` labels every render encoder `p<pass in frame> <width>x<height> <first 8 digits of the first draw's fragment key> d<draws>` for Instruments traces

name: DM_NVN_ENC_THREAD
meaning: `1` runs the replay's Metal encoding on a thread of its own while the submit thread goes on translating; on by default on iOS (`0` turns it off), off on macOS

name: DM_NVN_END_ALIAS
meaning: `1` puts the resource-alias flush back on every encoder's end barrier (each costs the command allocator about 100 KB; the start barriers carry it); `ab` alternates it with the `DM_AB` phases

name: DM_NVN_EVENT_MAP
meaning: `0` keeps the GPU event writes still in flight in a list walked for every signal, and scans a command node's signals for each new one, instead of finding them by word in hash maps (`nvn_queue.inc` `nq_event_issued`, `nq_signal_on`), as before

name: DM_NVN_FACE_MERGE
meaning: `0` gives each face-split draw a pass of its own again; `ab` alternates it under `DM_AB` (on by default: later face-split draws of the same level size into other textures or layers join the open face-split pass as further attachments, `fsm_plan` in `nvn_mtl.m`)

name: DM_NVN_FACE_SPLIT
meaning: `0` keeps a draw into several layers of one texture level as one draw with a colour target per layer; `ab` alternates it under `DM_AB` (on by default: one draw per layer, each with one colour output, so the outputs run in their own threads)

name: DM_NVN_FAMILY_NOCOMPRESS
meaning: `1` makes the textures of a resolution family (one storage, several sizes) uncompressed, without the valid-size tracking, as before (a size reading what another wrote sees its texels, misplaced, as on the console; every member shader-writable when `DM_NVN_PCM` is on); by default they keep lossless compression and each family heap tracks the size whose compressed blocks it holds (`valid_wh` in `nvn_mtl.m`, after upstream NXNative 4015ce2c0): a cross-size load clears to 0, a partial cross-size write zeroes the member first, a cross-size read gives zeros (ASTRAL CHAIN's glow after the pause menu). Kept in a player build's `env.txt` for the phone A/B

name: DM_NVN_FAMILY_PFV
meaning: `0` makes the 32-bit integer textures of a resolution family (R32, RG32, RGBA32 Uint / Sint) without the format-view usage, as before; on by default they have it from the start (with compression too, which it costs these members), so a float view of one (Luigi's Mansion 3), or any other format view, needs no upgrade that copies it out of the family's shared heap

name: DM_NVN_FAST_WAKE
meaning: `0` makes the game's `SyncWait`s wake on the commit feedback handler instead of the GPU's own signal of the fence (on by default)

name: DM_NVN_FB_DEPTH
meaning: `0` lets a draw sample its render pass's depth/stencil attachment directly, which can give undefined contents when the pass writes the sampled plane. By default a draw that samples the plane it writes through a texture slot reads a copy reused until the next game barrier. A read after an earlier write to its plane first ends the pass

name: DM_NVN_FB_DSNAP
meaning: `0` makes every draw that samples a depth/stencil plane an earlier draw of its pass wrote end the pass and read what is stored, as before; by default such a draw reads one snapshot taken since the game's last barrier (in the submission): the first read in the barrier interval ends the pass to copy what is stored, later ones reuse the copy without ending the pass, a depth write between them or not (NVN shows rendering to texture reads only after a barrier), and a read with no write before it in its pass reads a live snapshot too, so a later depth write keeps the pass. A depth/stencil clear or a write other than drawing into a depth texture (copy, texture clear, image binding) since the copy makes a fresh one. Slots and single uniform-buffer handles (`nvn_mtl.m` `fb_depth_rule`; Donkey Kong Bananza's effects chain, 6-14 pass ends a frame). Counted in the `residency set` line (`depth reads from the barrier interval's snapshot`)

name: DM_NVN_FB_SNAP
meaning: Draws that sample a colour attachment of their own render pass: unset, those that write it (or follow a write in the pass) read a snapshot, reused until the game's next barrier; `0` none; `all` a fresh snapshot for every draw that samples one (slow, diagnostic, no tile reads)

name: DM_NVN_FB_SNAP_IDLE
meaning: `0` keeps every same-pass feedback snapshot texture (up to 8, attachment-sized) for the rest of the run, as before; by default a snapshot no draw has taken for 600 submissions is released (unless it came back after such a release: `DM_NVN_FB_SNAP_KEEP`), and the memory line counts them

name: DM_NVN_FB_SNAP_KEEP
meaning: `=<MB>` caps the same-pass feedback snapshots kept because they came back after the idle release (default 128); `0` restores the old rule, where such a snapshot is released again after 600 idle submissions and made again (with a residency commit on the submit thread) at its next use

name: DM_NVN_FB_TILE
meaning: `0` makes such draws that sample the attachment at their own pixel (a projective sample at the vertex shader's screen varying) read a snapshot too, instead of the tile

name: DM_NVN_FB_TILE_EARLY
meaning: `1` (default on the Mac; off on iOS until a Breath of the Wild battery A/B): a draw that samples an attachment it writes and opens its render pass reads the tile of the pass it opens, whose formats were learned from the first such draw of its program on those targets; `0` makes it take a snapshot, as it did before

name: DM_NVN_FLUSH_FILL
meaning: `0` starts a new GPU texture in a CPU-writable pool as zeros; by default one whose storage the game flushed before its first use is filled from that storage once

name: DM_NVN_FRAMES
meaning: `=<N>` prints the NVN call table frame by frame for the first N frames (default 3)

name: DM_NVN_FT_CACHE
meaning: `0` turns off the cache of fragment argument table writes across draws (on by default: an address the slot already holds is not written again), for A/B runs

name: DM_NVN_GEOMETRY_COLOR
meaning: full retains inactive geometry color attachments; default omits them only when attachment bounds and state prove equivalence.

name: DM_NVN_GEOMETRY_COMPUTE
meaning: split ends the geometry compute encoder after each stage for comparison; default combines compatible stages.

name: DM_NVN_GEOMETRY_CUT
meaning: 0 disables extra segment-cut checks at geometry encoder boundaries; default obeys the existing draw threshold and safety gates there.

name: DM_NVN_GEOMETRY_INDEX_CACHE
meaning: 0 disables exact-byte CPU primitive-map caching; default bounds it to 32 MiB and 4096 entries.

name: DM_NVN_GEOMETRY_JOIN
meaning: `0` makes a colour-less geometry draw (its colour writes masked off, `geo_color_omit`) end an open pass with colours and open one of its own, as before; by default it draws in the open pass, which it writes no colour of (`nvn_mtl.m` draw path). Also from `Documents/env.txt`, player builds too ([Colour-less geometry draws join an open pass](reference/rendering.md#colour-less-geometry-draws-join-an-open-pass))

name: DM_NVN_GEOMETRY_PACK
meaning: legacy uses the serial block-prefix scan for comparison; default fuses small draws and scans large block totals in parallel.

name: DM_NVN_GEOMETRY_QUERY_RUN
meaning: 0 prevents geometry runs across samples-passed query reports/resets; default retains independent captures while queries replay at their raster positions.

name: DM_NVN_GEOMETRY_WAIT
meaning: always drains before indexed geometry preparation for comparison; default waits only for possible writes to CPU assembly inputs.

name: DM_NVN_GEO_HOIST
meaning: `0` draws each geometry draw's capture and kernel at its own place, ending the render pass; by default a run of lean geometry draws is prepared before the pass opens and only their rasters are drawn in it (`geo_run_walk`)

name: DM_NVN_GEO_LEAN
meaning: `0` draws passthrough geometry shaders through their full kernel and reader, as before; by default a lean kernel culls and the program's own vertex shader draws (`nvn_geometry.inc`)

name: DM_NVN_GEO_MESH
meaning: `0` draws passthrough geometry pairs that have a mesh library (the prewarm list's `G` rows, `geo_mesh.tsv`) through the compute path; by default they are mesh draws in the render pass (`geo_mesh_draw`)

name: DM_NVN_GEO_MESH_RUN
meaning: `0` dispatches every mesh geometry draw on its own; by default consecutive mesh draws of one pair whose result does not depend on their order are drawn as one dispatch (`geo_mesh_take`)

name: DM_NVN_GHOST
meaning: `=<n>`: the ceiling of the finalized-texture table, how many textures of finalized texture objects it keeps at most (`nvn_mtl.m` `ghost_cap`; idle entries drain back to 512), held to 64 to 8192; a value that is not a number is ignored. Overrides the profile's `ghost_table` (512 without the key; Ocarina of Time 4096). Performance; a larger table holds more textures alive. Kept from `Documents/env.txt` in a player build (`DM_PLAYER_BUILD=1`, `player_env.h`): `512` there is the off side of Ocarina's A/B. The log's start names the size and its source, and the `finalized-texture table up to frame` lines every 300 frames count puts, thrash, evictions and their cost

name: DM_NVN_GMEM_KEEP
meaning: `0` builds the raw pool table (the pools a shader's raw global memory loads and stores search) again at the next draw after every change of the pool set, as before; by default a draw keeps the table built earlier in its submission while pools have only come since: every commit, whole or segment, points the table words of the blocks encoded so far at a table of the pools as they are then, and a pool taken out or a new submission builds it at the next draw (`nvn_mtl.m` `gmem_map`; adapted from MacNativeGames b964bd4e (MIT): Ocarina of Time makes up to 91 memory pools a frame on other threads while the replay encodes). Kept in a player build's `env.txt`

name: DM_NVN_GPUPROF
meaning: `=<f>`, `<f1>-<f2>` or `every:<n>`: logs the GPU start and duration of every encoder of those frames (`[gpuprof]` lines from Metal 4 counter heap timestamps; a render pass line ends with the texture it draws into, `tex <serial>`, and its first draw's shaders, `vs <key> fs <key>`, to tell passes of one shape apart; a compute line ends with its first dispatch's shader, `cs <key>`, and its largest direct dispatch's, `largest <key> <n> groups`); kept from `Documents/env.txt` in a player build too (`player_env.h`), use `every:600` on the phone and sum with `dm/tools/gpuprof.py`

name: DM_NVN_GPU_STORAGE
meaning: `0` stops what the GPU writes into a texture in storage the CPU can read (a GPU texture, or one uploaded from its storage) from being written into that storage on the GPU (on by default; `gsb_target`, `gsb_store`), to measure it

name: DM_NVN_GPU_TS
meaning: `segment_submit_gaps`, `segment_gaps` or `submission`: what timestamp reports record instead of the default `segment` (the GPU start / end of the segment holding each report, without the GPU's idle time between the submission's command buffers, nor its wait between submissions for the host's translation of one the game had submitted already): segment times with the wait between submissions (the earlier default), segment times with both idle times, or one time for the whole submission

name: DM_NVN_HILITE
meaning: `=<fragment shader key>,…`: those draws use a solid colour instead (magenta, green, cyan, yellow, blue, white in order), to tell wrong geometry from wrong shading

name: DM_NVN_HOST_BARRIER
meaning: `0` makes the host's own encoders (its compute and copy encoders, the upload batches, the clear, copy, texture-draw, resolve and zeroing passes) wait for all earlier work before every stage, as before; by default they still wait for every stage of earlier work, but only before the stages that touch its results: a compute encoder's dispatch and copy stages, and the fragment stage of a host render pass whose vertex shader reads nothing the GPU wrote (`nvn_mtl.m` `hb_on`, `enc_r_begin_frag`); `ab` alternates it with the `DM_AB` phases. Kept in player builds; [Attachment loads and stores the next operations make unneeded](reference/frame-rate.md#attachment-loads-and-stores-the-next-operations-make-unneeded)

name: DM_NVN_I2F_NATIVE
meaning: `=0` converts the 8- and 16-bit integer-read-as-float vertex formats (`*_UI2F` / `*_I2F`) on the CPU again, as before; by default (`1`) they feed a float input, or an integer input's float shadow, through Metal's own vertex fetch (`nvn_mtl.m` `vin_i2f`; adapted from ComicBit/nxnative 39cc2e79c; [Integer-to-float vertex formats converted on the CPU](reference/rendering.md#integer-to-float-vertex-formats-converted-on-the-cpu)). 32-bit ones and captures always convert; `DM_NVN_VCONV_CPU=1` turns it off too. Kept in player builds, for the phone A/B

name: DM_NVN_IDLE_TEX_FOOT_MB
meaning: `=<MB>`: while the footprint (`phys_footprint`, read at a commit at most once a second) is over it, the idle live textures `DM_NVN_IDLE_TEX_MB` releases at low headroom go too, least recently used first, until the footprint is about an eighth under it (a sweep that frees under 64 MB backs the next off, twice as long each time up to 8 s, until the footprint is under the cap or a sweep frees that much; said once); each is made again from guest memory at its next use, resident before the command buffer that uses it. By default on iOS two fifths of the device's memory (4,915 MB on 12 GB); none on the Mac; `0` off. For Ocarina of Time's area change on the iPhone 18 Pro Max (footprint 3.4 -> 5.5-5.8 GB, the residency set 4.1 -> 5.7 GB, with 2.6 GB still to the memory limit, so the headroom threshold never ran, and the phone paged and compressed on half a core). Lines: `idle live textures released for the footprint cap`, and every memory line a `GPU working set up to frame` line (GPU allocated against the recommended working set, the residency set, the footprint, the cap and what it released). Kept in player builds (`nvn_mtl.m` `tex_idle_commit`, `tidle_foot_cap`; [frame-rate.md](reference/frame-rate.md#residency-commits-paged-guest-files-in-holding-the-lock))

name: DM_NVN_IDLE_TEX_FOOT_TRIM
meaning: `0` turns off the footprint cap's cache trim: by default a sweep for `DM_NVN_IDLE_TEX_FOOT_MB` that frees less than it wants asks the next submission's start for a trim of the caches kept for reuse (render-target heaps waiting, packaged-texture spares, feedback snapshots, per-frame arena blocks, render-target shadows; not the upload staging blocks, the render targets drawn over, the finalized-texture table or frame generation), each behind that submission's fence, once a minute at most; a trim that freed under 64 MB doubles the wait, up to 10 minutes (said once); off with `DM_MEMORY_TRIM=0` too; a pressure warning's trim takes its place. Line: `memory trim (footprint cap)`. Kept in player builds (`nvn_mtl.m` `tidle_trim_ask`, `mtl_trim_at` level 5; [frame-rate.md](reference/frame-rate.md#the-footprint-cap-freed-nothing-in-ocarina-of-time))

name: DM_NVN_IDLE_TEX_MB
meaning: `=<MB>` (1536 by default; `0` off): while the headroom to the system memory limit is under it (iOS, `os_proc_available_memory`, read at a commit at most once a second; the Mac has none and never runs it), live textures whose texture IDs have all gone unbound for 3 s, that no pool table names, whose storage is what the host takes their content from and that the GPU has not written over go, least recently used first, until about twice it is free; each is made again from guest memory at its next use (`nvn_mtl.m` `tex_idle_commit`; ported from S2Arm 8adc5673, 987b31ef; [Live textures the game keeps but no longer draws](reference/memory.md#live-textures-the-game-keeps-but-no-longer-draws)). A line per sweep that releases any (the first 8, then one every 300 frames at most). Kept in a player build's `env.txt`

name: DM_NVN_IDLE_TEX_PKG
meaning: `0` keeps packaged textures (a packaged layout: the game's texture files) out of the idle releases (`DM_NVN_IDLE_TEX_MB`, `DM_NVN_IDLE_TEX_FOOT_MB`), as before. By default one goes under the same rules as a CPU-written texture when the GPU's writes into it reach its storage (not COMPRESSIBLE, LINEAR, LINEAR_RENDER_TARGET, an uncompressed IMAGE or a 1D array; a host texture holding the storage's bytes), its package holds no GPU store since its upload and no GPU write its storage missed (`gw_lost`), the GPU has not written its storage since the CPU did and the command buffer being encoded holds no store into it; its next use uploads it again from its storage, the same bytes. Not one mip drop shrank or could shrink (also for CPU-written textures, with the store and lost-write tests). `=0` restores the earlier rules exactly. Counted in the release lines (`packaged N MB`) and the cap's sweep line (`idle live textures for the footprint cap (DM_NVN_IDLE_TEX_FOOT_MB): sweep at frame`, by kind and by the first rule that kept each texture). Kept in player builds (`nvn_mtl.m` `tidle_src_why`, `tidle_tex_w`, `tidle_line`; [frame-rate.md](reference/frame-rate.md#the-footprint-cap-freed-nothing-in-ocarina-of-time))

name: DM_NVN_INDLOG
meaning: `=<n>`: the first n indirect draws (and those of pass-dumped frames) log their arguments at encode and as the GPU left them once the submission completed, with the first indices

name: DM_NVN_IXCLOG
meaning: `=<n>` logs the first n indirect draw and dispatch conversions (record to arguments) once the GPU has run them

name: DM_NVN_KEYDUMP
meaning: `=<fs key>[:n[:every]]`: for up to n draws of that fragment shader (default 6), logs the pass dump binding lines plus vertex formats, vertex streams and uniform values; meant for devices

name: DM_NVN_LAZY_CLEAR
meaning: `0` makes clears with no draw after them open a pass of their own, as before; by default they wait to become the load action of the next pass on that target

name: DM_NVN_LEVEL_GROUP
meaning: `0` keeps a run of one-draw passes into the levels and faces of one cube or array texture in the game's order (face by face), as before; by default it is replayed level by level so each level's faces become one slice-merged pass (`rg_plan`); `ab` alternates with `DM_AB`

name: DM_NVN_LINE_WIDTH
meaning: `0` draws every NVN line 1 pixel wide, as before; by default a line draw wider than a pixel is drawn as a quad per segment (`nvn_wline.inc`)

name: DM_NVN_LOG
meaning: `=1` logs the creation of NVN objects

name: DM_NVN_LS_STATS
meaning: `=1` (measurement only; kept in player builds) logs two `[ls-stats]` lines every 300 frames: per frame, render passes, attachment bytes loaded (and of them those the pass then cleared whole before any draw wrote them) and stored, each store's fate at the next pass that attaches the same subresource (loaded again; cleared or discarded with no use between, and of that what is registered in the texture pool, which shaders may sample; cleared or discarded after a use such as a binding, copy or present; not attached again within 2 frames; stored again by another pass), the bytes the reduction rules saved (`DM_NVN_CLEARED_LOAD`, `DM_NVN_DS_DEAD_STORE`, `DM_NVN_MSAA_RESOLVE_ONLY`), and the 8 pass kinds (size, colour count, colour 0 and depth formats, samples) with the most traffic (`nvn_mtl.m` `ls_pass_begin`, `ls_store`, `ls_report`); [Attachment loads and stores the next operations make unneeded](reference/frame-rate.md#attachment-loads-and-stores-the-next-operations-make-unneeded)

name: DM_NVN_MAGSCAN
meaning: `=<fs key>[:every[:phase]]`: device self-check that reads each pass's colour attachments every `every` frames (default 30) and logs `[mag]` lines for solid magenta 16×16 blocks or non-finite pixels

name: DM_NVN_MDX_PRESCAN
meaning: `0` copies an indirect-count multi-draw's records at its own first draw, which splits a render pass an earlier draw opened; by default the draw that opens a pass copies those of the multi-draws after it first (ab with DM_AB). Kept from `Documents/env.txt` in a player build (`DM_PLAYER_BUILD=1`, `player_env.h`) for the A/B

name: DM_NVN_MFX_CONTENT
meaning: `0` gives each input size of the game's upscaler drawn by MetalFX (`DM_UPSCALER=metalfx`) a spatial scaler of its own again, 4 slots in all; by default an input that is copied into the scaler's own texture takes one scaler made for the output's size, each dispatch giving its rectangle's size as the content (`inputContentWidth` / `Height`), its edge repeated 2 texels past it, so a dynamic resolution (Ocarina of Time: 8 sizes, about 60 scalers made a run) keeps one scaler and one scratch pair; the image is byte for byte that of a scaler made for the size (`t_upscaler_mfx`). The scaler line counts the scalers made (`#k made`); kept in player builds, `ab` with `DM_AB` (`nvn_mtl.m` `up_mfx_encode`, `up_mfx_pad`)

name: DM_NVN_MFX_DIRECT
meaning: `0` copies the game's colour into MetalFX's RGBA16F input (DM_UPSCALER=metalfx) unless it is RGBA16F; by default an input that is the whole rectangle MetalFX reads is taken in its own format (ab with DM_AB)

name: DM_NVN_MIP_DROP
meaning: `0` off, `1` or `2` levels (by default `1` on the iPhone and iPad for the X2.0 test round, off on the Mac): block-compressed 2D textures and 2D arrays uploaded from their storage (BC or ASTC, no flag but `MINIMAL_LAYOUT`, a whole mip chain, the larger side at least `DM_NVN_MIP_DROP_MIN` texels) are made without their top 1 or 2 levels while only texture IDs sample them, a quarter or a sixteenth of their memory and upload; any other host use of one (a copy, readback, clear, attachment or image) uploads it whole first and keeps it whole. Unset or `0` (the default): every level, as before. A phone memory and efficiency option for an A/B: a shader's integer reads, size queries or explicit levels of such a texture see the host's smaller texture (`nvn_mtl.m` `md_pick`; [Top mip levels left out on the phone](reference/memory.md#top-mip-levels-left-out-on-the-phone)). The line after the memory line counts the textures and MB. Kept in a player build's `env.txt`

name: DM_NVN_MIP_DROP_COMPRESSIBLE
meaning: `0` keeps whole the block-compressed textures that carry `COMPRESSIBLE` beside `MINIMAL_LAYOUT`, as before; by default, wherever `DM_NVN_MIP_DROP` is on, the mip drop takes them as it takes one without the flag (on NVN the flag asks for a render target's lossless compression, which a BC or ASTC texture never is, so the host sees and samples them the same). The mip drop line ends with `of those held now, through DM_NVN_MIP_DROP_COMPRESSIBLE N (M MB)`; with it off its tally counts them as `the COMPRESSIBLE flag` (`nvn_mtl.m` `md_shape_why`; [Top mip levels left out on the phone](reference/memory.md#top-mip-levels-left-out-on-the-phone)). Kept in a player build's `env.txt`

name: DM_NVN_MIP_DROP_MIN
meaning: `=<texels>`: the smallest larger side of a texture `DM_NVN_MIP_DROP` leaves levels out of (1024 by default; values under 64 are ignored)

name: DM_NVN_MIP_DROP_PARTIAL
meaning: `1` lets the mip drop take a chain of 3 levels or more that stops above 4 texels (a 2048 texture with 8 levels); off by default until a device A/B: an engine that cuts a chain short is likelier to sample it by explicit level, where the drop reads K levels blurrier. The mip drop line ends with `through DM_NVN_MIP_DROP_PARTIAL N (M MB)` when on; off, its tally counts them as `a chain that stops early` (`nvn_mtl.m` `md_shape_why`; [Top mip levels left out on the phone](reference/memory.md#top-mip-levels-left-out-on-the-phone)). Kept in a player build's `env.txt`

name: DM_NVN_MSAA_RESOLVE_ONLY
meaning: `0` stores a multisample texture's samples again when it is resolved (`nvnCommandBufferDownsample`), as before; by default the resolve pass stores only the resolve (`MTLStoreActionMultisampleResolve`) when the rest of the submission clears the multisample texture whole before anything could read its samples (the same scan as `DM_NVN_DS_DEAD_STORE`; `nvn_mtl.m` `copy_t2t_enc`). Kept in player builds; [Attachment loads and stores the next operations make unneeded](reference/frame-rate.md#attachment-loads-and-stores-the-next-operations-make-unneeded)

name: DM_NVN_NODE_POOL
meaning: `0` allocates and frees each queue node and receipt and every node's signals array, as before, instead of taking them from free lists and keeping a node's first signal inline (`nvn_queue.inc` `nq_pooled`)

name: DM_NVN_PASSDUMP
meaning: `=<f>`, `<f1>-<f2>` or `every:<n>`: logs every render pass of those frames (attachments, clears, shader keys, bindings, draw state, presents, and the host function and line that ended each pass) for the `tbdr_*.py` tools

name: DM_NVN_PASSDUMP_ALL
meaning: `=1` makes `DM_NVN_PASSDUMP` record every draw and binding change, not only the first per pass and stage, including copies and inline uniform updates

name: DM_NVN_PASS_ALT
meaning: `0` draws a profile's `pass_alternate` `<W>x<H>` passes every frame, as before (the Quality preset sets it; `DM_NVN_CUBE_ALT` is the cube shapes' own); by default such a pass (Donkey Kong Bananza's 128x128 view) keeps the previous frame's picture on every other frame (`nvn_pass_alt.h`, `nvn_mtl.m` `rp_begin_ex_`). Also from `Documents/env.txt`, player builds too ([A pass drawn every other frame](reference/rendering.md#a-pass-drawn-every-other-frame))

name: DM_NVN_PASS_REPEAT
meaning: `=1` counts, on the encode thread, the render passes whose recorded stream is byte for byte one of the previous frame's (`nvn_rec.h` `pr_note`) and logs `[pass repeat] up to frame N, per frame: …` every 300 frames: the share of passes and draws, and the encode thread's time in them, to judge whether indirect command buffers could save encode time. Measurement only; off by default (the hashing costs about 0.07 ms a frame on an M4 Max); needs the encode thread (`DM_NVN_ENC_THREAD`). Kept from `Documents/env.txt` in a player build (`player_env.h`)

name: DM_NVN_PASS_SPLIT
meaning: `=<draws>` (default 256 on the Mac, off on iOS until a battery A/B; `0` off): a render pass is ended and its segment committed after this many draws while the GPU has no segment left, so the GPU starts a long pass (a G-buffer) before it is all translated; its attachments are stored and loaded again

name: DM_NVN_PASS_SPLIT_MAX
meaning: `=<n>` (default 2, `0` no limit): the most splits of one render pass (`DM_NVN_PASS_SPLIT`), as each stores and loads its attachments

name: DM_NVN_PCM
meaning: `1` runs a render pass that holds one draw of one or two triangles into colour targets (up to 8; blending, write masks and a depth test without depth or stencil writes are done in the kernel; no discard, alpha test, logic operation or read of a written level) as one compute dispatch of the pair's kernel (`<vertex>_<pixel>_pc.metallib` in `DM_NVN_PCM_DIR`, made by `dm/gfx/tools/dmsh_pcomp_build.py`), where a render pass costs Apple GPUs a fixed 15-40 µs; `ab` alternates it with the `DM_AB` phases. Any value but `0` also makes colour render targets up to `DM_NVN_PCM_MAXPX` pixels (every size of a resolution family) shader-writable from creation. On by default through the profile key `pass_compute` (`off` per game); `0` turns it off for a run (NX18-X2.0 open-optimizations.md; Breath of the Wild's Mac A/B: render passes 145 → 92 a frame, GPU mean 10.9 → 9.8 ms). With `DM_NVN_GPUPROF`, passes that could run so end their line in ` pcm` (`nvn_mtl.m` `pcm_plan`, `pcm_run`, `pcm_usage`)

name: DM_NVN_PCM_DIR
meaning: the folder of the pass-as-compute kernels `DM_NVN_PCM` runs (`<vertex key>_<pixel key>_pc.metallib`); a pair with none draws its render pass and is logged once (`pass-as-compute: no kernel for pair`)

name: DM_NVN_PCM_MAXPX
meaning: the largest colour target, in pixels, `DM_NVN_PCM` makes shader-writable for its kernels (default 1048576: larger ones keep their render pass, so their lossless compression is not risked); a resolution family gets the usage on every member only when its largest size is within it, else on none (`fam_usage`; every member with `DM_NVN_FAMILY_NOCOMPRESS=1`)

name: DM_NVN_PCM_NO
meaning: `depth`, `blend`, `mask` (comma-separated): `DM_NVN_PCM` leaves passes with a depth test, blending or a partial write mask to their render pass, for finding which kind a picture fault comes from

name: DM_NVN_PCM_SKIP
meaning: `<vertex key>_<pixel key>,…`: those shader pairs keep their render pass under `DM_NVN_PCM` (a bisection over pairs found Breath of the Wild's hearts fault)

name: DM_NVN_PF_PARTS
meaning: `1` (a diagnostic, off by default; it costs frame rate: since adeeda7b4 it makes a task_info call at each part of every draw, and Ocarina of Time on an iPhone 18 Pro Max fell from 60 to 22-30 fps with it on, 2.3 -> 4-5 W, so leave it off outside page-in diagnosis and read no frame-rate or power figures from such a run) gives each long-frame line the replay's page-ins by part of its work: `; replay page-ins by part: other N, textures made N, storage scans N, pool tables N, uniform reads N, uploads N, residency N, index scans N, uniform shadows N, pool buffers made N, vertex buffers N, arguments N, pipelines N, images N, buffer-texture copies N` (a task_info call at each change of part, about 1 us; process-wide counts), and `; slow commands (DM_NVN_PF_PARTS): <type> N / T ms, ...`: the replay's commands that took 0.2 ms or more, by type (one clock read a command): [area loads waited on the replay's own page faults](reference/frame-rate.md#area-loads-waited-on-the-replays-own-page-faults)

name: DM_NVN_PKG_SPARE_IDLE
meaning: `0` keeps a packaged texture's spare (the texture its last re-upload replaced) for the rest of the run, as before; by default a spare no re-upload has used for 600 submissions is released, and the memory line counts the spares alive and released

name: DM_NVN_POOL_CHUNKS
meaning: `0` wraps a memory pool of 512 MB or more whole in one buffer, as before; by default it is wrapped in overlapping 16 MB chunks made as draws reach them, so only the parts in use are wired

name: DM_NVN_POOL_ENTRY
meaning: `0` takes a pool table entry's checks in their old order and asks the texture its type (kept in player builds, for the phone A/B). By default (`nvn_mtl.m` `pool_entry`) an ID whose texture type is known (`tt1`, cleared by its registration) and is not the table's is answered first, before the storage, budget and stand-in checks (a lock or three an ID), and the type comes from the view record (`tex_fast_rid_tp`); such an ID is no longer counted left out (a walk the next frame) or dead. A pool table patch takes each ID of the registration log again in every table of the pool. Mac bench (`t_args_levers`, two tables over 4,000 IDs, 300 registered again): 30.7 -> 29.2 us a patch

name: DM_NVN_POOL_FIRST
meaning: `1` logs every first read through the pool table of a texture ID whose texture was not made yet (up to 32 a frame): what the read found (the ID's stand-in, or the dummy, which reads 0), the texture, its view and how many frames before it was registered; it also checks at each such read whether the storage the stand-in was made from has been written since. The totals go to the log every 300 frames without it (`pool stand-ins up to frame`)

name: DM_NVN_POOL_MEMO
meaning: `0` sends every pool table lookup (a full argument encode of a shader with TEXP / SAMPP pools, `nvn_mtl.m` `pool_gpu`) through the table search and its checks, as before (kept in player builds, for the phone A/B). By default a lookup is kept, per table (sampler or texture, element type, pixel class, base), while nothing the search's first check reads can have moved: the registration and storage generations, the submission, `g_psnap_gen` (any table built or patched) and, for a table whose walk left textures out for a later frame, the frame. Mac micro-benchmark: about 5 ns a lookup through the search, 3 ns kept; the `[args-stats]` levers line (`DM_NVN_ARGS_STATS=1`) shows the pool and handle table lookups by how they ended (memo, first check, patch kept, patched, standing, walk; a handle table kept for the pass, read again, the same entries, built) and their time

name: DM_NVN_POOL_READAHEAD
meaning: `1` (off by default since its first phone run asked for about 317 GB in 137 s and made the worst load frame 937 ms) turns on the pool walk's read-ahead, in its second, narrow form: before a walk or a patch of a texture pool table resolves its IDs, it asks ahead (F_RDADVISE, together on the read-ahead queue) only for what it will read: the whole storage of the textures it will make this frame (within the frame's room, 32 MB) and the levels of the stand-ins it will make (up to 512 a walk), each texture once: [area loads waited on the replay's own page faults](reference/frame-rate.md#area-loads-waited-on-the-replays-own-page-faults)

name: DM_NVN_POOL_STANDIN
meaning: off by default since 2026-11-22 (Ocarina of Time made 43,000-83,000 stand-ins a run, each reading its storage, for about 57 reads that found one; off, area loads had fewer and shorter hitches and no visible dark frame): the dummy (reads 0) in the pool tables for a texture the walk does not make. `1`: once the walk's budget is full, such a texture holds a stand-in until a shader reads its ID: its own smallest levels, or its last level cut down to every n-th block, so the first read draws the texture's colours coarse for one frame instead of black (Ocarina of Time's cliff beside the castle town wall dark for one frame when the game streams a sharper texture into it, issue #1969)

name: DM_NVN_PREDICT
meaning: `0` turns off the parallel precompile look-ahead: a pipeline miss compiles only the pipeline it needs

name: DM_NVN_PREDICT_NEXT
meaning: `0` keeps the look-ahead's old bound: at most two of a submission's later draws' pipelines handed to the background after its first miss (`PSO_PREDICT_BUDGET`). By default (`1`) every later draw that would wait is admitted (upstream PR #1344, `pso_pend_kick_next`): the first two on the global queue at user-initiated QoS as before, the rest on NX 18's utility-QoS pipeline queues (`pp_bg_queue`, `DM_PSO_BG_QUEUES`), not the global queue as upstream; `ab` alternates with `DM_AB`. Kept in player builds, for the iPhone battery A/B ([shaders.md](reference/shaders.md#the-look-ahead-hands-every-later-draws-pipeline-to-the-background)). Not a player setting

name: DM_NVN_PREFETCH
meaning: `0` turns off loading a program's shader libraries in the background when the game makes it (`nvnProgramSetShaders`); they load at its first draw instead

name: DM_NVN_PREREAD
meaning: `1` turns on the read-ahead of pools, buffers and textures at setup (off by default since a same-route iPhone A/B: fewer page-ins at area loads, but no fewer frames over 100 ms, twice the long frames, more dropped frames, CPU and wakeups). With it, each memory pool the CPU can reach (when made), and each buffer and texture in one (not packaged textures), asks the kernel to read its guest range ahead (madvise `MADV_WILLNEED`, up to 64 MB a range, on a utility queue); a range asked within 2 s is not asked again (`nvn_mtl.m` `mtl_preread`; ported from kid-with-sword-remake L7.7, MIT). A `[preread]` line every 600 frames gives ranges, MB, time in the calls, failures and skips: [area loads waited on the replay's own page faults](reference/frame-rate.md#area-loads-waited-on-the-replays-own-page-faults). Player builds keep it

name: DM_NVN_PRESENT_FINISH
meaning: `=1` makes each present return once the GPU has run the frame, so the game never runs ahead of the GPU

name: DM_NVN_PRESENT_FX_EXACT
meaning: `=1` makes the present's MetalFX scaler take the crop's size as its input, a new scaler for each new crop size, as before the scaler took the window texture's size (`fx_input_size`); for an A/B on a GPU whose MetalFX may treat a content well below its input size differently

name: DM_NVN_PREWIRE_JOBS
meaning: `=<1-8>` how many mlock calls a residency page-in makes at once (4 by default; `1`: one call after another, as before): [a residency page-in faulted its file pages in one call at a time](reference/frame-rate.md#a-residency-page-in-faulted-its-file-pages-in-one-call-at-a-time)

name: DM_NVN_PROF
meaning: `=1` wraps the implemented NVN functions in a timing wrapper and collects the time each takes during recording

name: DM_NVN_PROGTRACE
meaning: `=<vertex keys,...>` logs matching ProgramSetShaders calls and their guest backtraces

name: DM_NVN_PUSH_DEDUP
meaning: `0` makes NVN2 push constants set to the bytes the state holds already copy them again and re-encode the argument blocks of the stages that read them, as before (`nvn_mtl.m` `state_op` `OP_PUSH_CONST`; kept in player builds). By default the same bytes change nothing, so the next draw can reuse its block (after S2Arm 5442e030f). `check_t_args_stats` counts it; not measured in a game here

name: DM_NVN_QUERY_POOL
meaning: `0` keeps the occlusion queries' records as before: a slot list allocated for each samples-passed report and every visibility slot retained in it, and a conditional render's two counters found by hash each time. By default a submission's slots go into one arena that its post ring record hands back once its completion has read them (each visibility buffer retained once per submission), a report carries the range of its slots, and a counter record keeps its +16 and -16 neighbours by pointer once found, so a steady frame allocates nothing for its queries (Ocarina of Time: about 1,500 queries and 1,500 conditions a frame; `nvn_mtl.m` `vis_add`, `vis_op`, `rc_values`; micro-benchmark in `t_query_pool`). Kept in player builds, for an A/B

name: DM_NVN_REFL_FIXED
meaning: `1` gives every loaded shader the fixed reflection block it embedded before (room for 128 bindings and both readable-tile tables, about 3.2 KB); by default its bindings and readable-tile tables are allocated at their real size, and the memory line counts the blocks

name: DM_NVN_REGLUM
meaning: `=x0,y0,x1,y1:<file>` (normalized coordinates): on every present records the present number, time, mean luminance and a grayscale thumbnail of that region, to check animation speed against frame rate

name: DM_NVN_REPORT_EXACT
meaning: `0` refuses a partly covered uniform shadow over the whole 4 KB page of a counter report of a running submission, as before; by default only over the report's own 16 bytes, which the host writes when that submission completes

name: DM_NVN_RES_ASYNC
meaning: `0` commits the residency set on the replay thread on the spot again, wherever something joins it (a pool's first lookup, the raw pool table, each upload batch, each submission); by default the replay hands those commits to the residency commit worker and goes on, and the encode thread commits whatever is still queued just before each queue commit, so a resource is in the committed set before the GPU runs what uses it (without the encode thread only the pool lookups and the raw pool table hand off). For the area-load hitches of Ocarina of Time (142-405 ms of residency commits and guest-file wiring on the replay thread in a load frame); the residency line gives the commits by where they ran (`on the replay thread`, `on the commit worker`, `before a queue commit`) and the hand-offs. Kept in player builds, `ab` with `DM_AB` (`nvn_mtl.m` `res_commit_soon`, `rca_queue_guard`)

name: DM_NVN_RES_PREWIRE
meaning: `0` pages a residency commit's guest-file ranges in (mlock) holding the residency commit lock again, and every commit takes the whole queue, as before; by default the page-in runs before the lock, in chunks of 64 MB, each committed after its own page-in, so a queue commit (the encode thread's, a present snapshot's, a one-off's) and a commit that needs none of the changes being paged in go through at once, and the encode thread's guard before a queue commit commits only the changes made before the replay recorded that command buffer (the record keeps the change number). A commit that needs a change being paged in waits for that page-in, as before; a resource is still in the committed set before the GPU runs what uses it. For Ocarina of Time's 174 ms residency commit (adds 374, 202 MB, mostly page-in) that the encode thread and the replay waited 178 and 177 ms behind. Lines: `[RED] slow residency prewire`, `[RED] slow wait for a residency prewire`; the residency line counts `prewired outside the lock`, `waits for a prewire` and the guards `with their changes committed`. Kept in player builds, `ab` with `DM_AB` (`nvn_mtl.m` `res_commit_to`, `res_prewire`, `rca_queue_guard`; [frame-rate.md](reference/frame-rate.md#residency-commits-paged-guest-files-in-holding-the-lock))

name: DM_NVN_RES_TRICKLE_MB
meaning: `=<MB>` (0-512; off by default since the same A/B as `DM_NVN_PREREAD`; the fork used 16): once a raw global memory pool table has been built, each submission puts up to this many MB of pools the game gave addresses in (64 MB or smaller, not a large pool's chunks) into the residency set ahead of the table, so an area's first draw finds them resident instead of committing them all at once (`nvn_mtl.m` `res_trickle`; ported from kid-with-sword-remake L7.8, MIT). A `[trickle]` line every 600 frames gives pools and MB. Player builds keep it

name: DM_NVN_REUPLOADS
meaning: `=1` logs the first 400 re-uploads, then one in 25 (each line numbered `re-upload #N`), of textures taken from their storage: shape, size, the pages written since the upload and where the first lies, and the GPU copies into it since then

name: DM_NVN_REUPLOAD_COALESCE
meaning: `0` re-uploads a packaged texture at every use that finds its pages written since its upload, and a written image whole, as before; by default (kept in player builds) a re-upload deswizzles only the block-row bands of an image written since and keeps the rest, and a use re-uploads only the writes the game made before it submitted the submission being replayed (later ones wait for the first submission that needs them); the packaged-textures line counts the deferrals and banded re-uploads with the bytes they saved (`nvn_mtl.m` `reup_defer`, `band_scan`; reference/frame-rate.md)

name: DM_NVN_REUPLOAD_PART
meaning: `0` re-uploads a texture's storage whole; by default a re-upload of a texture never drawn into or written as an image on the GPU deswizzles only the levels and layers written since (by the CPU, or by a GPU copy, clear or pass stored into the storage through any texture over it) and keeps the rest (from the spare it goes into, or copied from the texture it replaces)

name: DM_NVN_ROP_F16
meaning: `0` / `1` overrides the start-up probe (`nvn_mtl.m` `rop_f16_probe`) for float colours going into 16-bit float targets (R16F, RG16F, RGBA16F): `1` truncates them toward zero in the pixel shader as NVIDIA's colour unit converts them (`DMSH_ROUND_F16`), `0` keeps the GPU's own conversion; unset, the shader guard is on only where the GPU rounds to nearest even (upstream measured iPhone and iPad GPUs); `DM_NVN_ROP_ROUND=0` turns it off too

name: DM_NVN_ROP_ROUND
meaning: `0` leaves float colours going into 8-bit, 16-bit and RGB10A2 normalized targets to Apple's conversion (the exact product rounded to nearest); by default a pixel shader rounds them as NVIDIA's colour unit does (the float32 product rounded to nearest even) where blending is off, MIN or MAX, or a logic operation

name: DM_NVN_RP_AREA
meaning: `0` makes passes on targets of 16 M pixels or more cover the whole target, as before; by default a draw pass that loads what it keeps stops at the far corner of its scissor when that is at most half the target

name: DM_NVN_RT_CONTINUE
meaning: `0` ends the pass whenever the game sets render targets, as before; by default SetRenderTargets naming the open pass's targets continues the pass

name: DM_NVN_RT_DEAD
meaning: By default releases a shared render target of a GPU-only pool that another target drew over and that has not been used for the wait (`DM_NVN_RT_DEAD_MS`, 3000 ms), checked every quarter of the wait (100 ms steps, 100 ms to 1 s) when a submission begins; its next use makes it again. `0` keeps every such target while a texture object names it, as before. `ab` alternates it with the `DM_AB` phases. A line every 300 frames in which some went gives that window's textures and MB released early and those made again. Player builds keep it (memory A/Bs)

name: DM_NVN_RT_DEAD_FAMILY
meaning: `0` lets `DM_NVN_RT_DEAD` release a resolution family's members one by one, as before; by default a family goes only whole, when every member is dead, with its heap (`nvn_mtl.m` `alias_dead_families`; [Render targets drawn over stay while their texture objects live](reference/memory.md#render-targets-drawn-over-stay-while-their-texture-objects-live)). `ab` alternates it with the `DM_AB` phases

name: DM_NVN_RT_DEAD_MS
meaning: `=<ms>` (100-60000, default 3000, NXNative's) how long a render target drawn over must stay unused before `DM_NVN_RT_DEAD` releases it; a pass comes every quarter of it in 100 ms steps, 100 ms to 1 s (200 ms at 1000). NXNative's 3000 comes with a pass a second; a 2 GB Apple TV run used 1000. Player builds keep it

name: DM_NVN_RT_DEAD_PRESSURE
meaning: `0` keeps `DM_NVN_RT_DEAD`'s usual wait at memory pressure. By default a memory warning runs a pass at 300 ms at once in the trim, before the waiting heaps go, and while the headroom to the system memory limit is under 2048 MB (until it is over 2560 MB; iOS, `os_proc_available_memory`) the wait is 300 ms with a check every 200 ms, never shorter than the last 4 frames took; what such a pass releases frees its heap; when 8 or more, and a quarter, of its releases since the last step (or the low spell's start) are made again within 10 s the low-headroom wait doubles, and it comes down a step when the headroom recovers (`nvn_mtl.m` `tu_due`, `tu_press_warning`; [Render targets drawn over stay while their texture objects live](reference/memory.md#render-targets-drawn-over-stay-while-their-texture-objects-live)). `ab` alternates it with the `DM_AB` phases. Player builds keep it

name: DM_NVN_RT_RECYCLE
meaning: `0` makes each render target in a GPU-only pool, each feedback snapshot and each resolution family heap its own exact Metal allocation, freed with its texture, as before; by default they are placed in heaps from one free list, and a freed one's heap waits, resident, for the next texture it fits (`ab` alternates it with the `DM_AB` phases)

name: DM_NVN_RT_RECYCLE_CAP
meaning: `=<MB>` sets a fixed cap on the freed texture heaps kept for reuse (`=256` is the flat cap before); by default the Mac keeps 256 MB and iOS 256 MB down to 32 MB as the headroom to the memory limit falls from 3 GB to 1 GB

name: DM_NVN_RT_SUBSET
meaning: `0` makes SetRenderTargets naming only the first colour targets of the open pass (same depth) begin a pass of its own, as before; by default the pass goes on with the other targets attached and unwritten (`rt_prefix`); `ab` alternates with `DM_AB`

name: DM_NVN_SAME_CLEAR
meaning: `0` opens every clear-only pass, as before; by default a clear-only pass (a lazy clear landed, or a clear with no draw) leaves out an attachment that already holds that clear: its texture (a GPU-only pool's single-level, single-layer 2D texture without the shader-write usage) was last written by an identical clear through the same format and nothing has written it since, so its memory already holds the bytes the clear would store, whatever reads it later. Every GPU write into a game texture forgets the record (`nvn_mtl.m` `sc_note`; Donkey Kong Bananza's never-read 2880x1620 pair, ~42 MB of stores a frame). Counted in the `residency set` line (`clears the target already held left out`, `clear-only passes not opened`; of them, with a stencil clear triangle: `DM_NVN_SAME_CLEAR_TRI`)

name: DM_NVN_SAME_CLEAR_TRI
meaning: `0` draws a stencil clear with a partial write mask at once in a draw pass of its own, as before (`DM_NVN_SAME_CLEAR`'s first version); by default such a clear with no pass open, over the whole target, on a target that can take a same-clear record waits like the other clears and its triangle (compare always, replace through the mask) is drawn as its pass begins, so a pass of clears alone stays clear-only: the stencil record keeps which bits it knows, and a clear-only pass whose triangle writes only bits the record holds with the same values leaves the stencil out, the whole pass when colour and depth are held too (`nvn_mtl.m` `clear_s_tri_pass`, `sc_note_tri`; Donkey Kong Bananza's 2880x1620 pair: colour and depth cleared, stencil bit 0 cleared by a mask of `0x1`). No effect with `DM_NVN_SAME_CLEAR=0`. Counted in the `residency set` line (`with a stencil clear triangle`)

name: DM_NVN_SHADER_SHARE
meaning: `0` turns off sharing one preparation of a shader library between the loading paths (the draw's own load, the program-creation prefetch, the look-ahead, the prewarm and the shader-only lines after the first frame): each prepares its own copy again, as before; by default a path that misses a library another is preparing joins it, and the log counts `shader sharing: … preparations joined, … made` (`nvn_mtl.m` `shader_acquire`; adapted from ComicBit/nxnative bee12ec)

name: DM_NVN_SHARED_IDLE
meaning: `0` (the default since 2026-11-22: Ocarina of Time's field drew blocks of other ground textures with it on, docs/reference/memory.md) keeps every shared texture the sharing table alone keeps; `1` releases one no lookup found for `DM_NVN_SHARED_IDLE_SUBS` submissions goes when its storage holds what it holds (a texture the GPU cannot draw into in a pool the CPU can read, or one whose GPU writes are stored into its storage); `2` releases those whose content is the GPU's alone too (a render target in a `CPU_NO_ACCESS` pool), off until a device A/B shows no game reads such storage again long after (`nvn_mtl.m` `shared_idle_locked`; [Shared textures kept by the sharing table alone](reference/memory.md#shared-textures-kept-by-the-sharing-table-alone)). Its line follows the mip drop line. Kept in a player build's `env.txt`

name: DM_NVN_SHARED_IDLE_SUBS
meaning: `=<submissions>` (at least 1024; 65536 by default, about 40-60 s of Ocarina of Time) how long a shared texture kept by the sharing table alone goes without a lookup before `DM_NVN_SHARED_IDLE` releases it. Kept in a player build's `env.txt`

name: DM_NVN_SHDUMP
meaning: `=<dir>` saves programs missing from the shader map as `<key>.ctl` (control section) and `<key>.code`, to find the files that hold them

name: DM_NVN_SHMAP
meaning: The shader map (`shader_map.tsv`); `c1_full.tsv` and `pso_manifest.tsv` are taken from the same folder. Default: the game profile's folder on the Mac; the iOS app sets it

name: DM_NVN_SHOT
meaning: `=<frame>[,<frame>…]:<path>` saves the swapchain texture as an image at those frames (`%d` in the path = frame number)

name: DM_NVN_SHOT_OUT
meaning: `=<W>x<H>` makes `DM_NVN_SHOT` capture the picture as the present pass upscales it to that size, the crop included, instead of the raw swapchain texture

name: DM_NVN_SIGNAL_EVENTS
meaning: `node` or `split`: whether a GPU event signal stays in its command node and publishes when the node completes (`node`, the default) or ends it (`split`, one Metal submission each; a fallback), instead of the profile's `signal_events`; any other value is logged and the profile's is used

name: DM_NVN_SKIP_FS
meaning: `=<fragment key>[,…]` (up to 16) drops all draws of those fragment shaders, to measure their GPU cost or bisect a wrong draw; the picture is wrong

name: DM_NVN_SKIP_MESH
meaning: `=1` drops every task and mesh draw, to measure what they cost in all; the picture is wrong

name: DM_NVN_SKIP_SMALL
meaning: `=<width>` drops all draws whose target width is at most that, to measure the cost of tiny render passes; the picture is wrong

name: DM_NVN_SLICE_MERGE
meaning: `0` keeps passes into other layers of one array or cube texture level apart (on by default: they run as one layered pass)

name: DM_NVN_SLICE_MRT
meaning: `0` slice-merges only passes into one colour target of an array or cube texture, as before; by default passes into several colour targets that step through the same layer together, and into the depth planes of 3D textures, are merged too; `ab` alternates with `DM_AB`

name: DM_NVN_SNAPRAW
meaning: `=1` makes `DM_NVN_TEXDUMP` also save each target's raw bytes, with a text header line, since converting an HDR target to an 8-bit image truncates

name: DM_NVN_SPARSE_HEAP_MB
meaning: `=<MB>` (1 to 4096) sets the size of the placement heaps sparse tiles come from; `=256` gives the 256 MB heaps and their last-freed-first tile order of before; by default heaps are 64 MB and a tile takes the lowest free slot

name: DM_NVN_SPARSE_LOG
meaning: `0` checks a sparse texture made whole (not placement sparse) by walking every page of its page table at each submission that moved the dirty clock or the mapping generation, as before; by default (`1`) a clean walk keeps the runs of physical memory behind it and the pool's change log position, and while no mapping request since overlaps the texture only those runs are looked at, each from its dirty range's largest write generation first. Ported from S2Arm de791716; kept in player builds for its A/B. The line `[nvn] sparse texture checks: page-table walks N, from the change log M` after the packaged textures line counts both ([a whole sparse texture's check walked its page table every submission](reference/nvn-objects.md#a-whole-sparse-textures-check-walked-its-page-table-every-submission); `nvn_mtl.m` `pkg_sparse_clean`)

name: DM_NVN_SPARSE_TILES
meaning: `0` makes a sparse texture of 64 MB or more whole, as before; by default it is a Metal placement sparse texture with only the mapped tiles backed

name: DM_NVN_STAGE_POOL_MB
meaning: `=<MB>` caps the upload staging pool, where a batch's retired temporary 32 MB staging blocks stay resident for the next burst instead of leaving the residency set and being freed (`nvn_mtl.m` `up_pool_put`; ported from S2Arm 01afd92a, 6e708d3e); `0` frees them after each batch, as before. By default 128 MB on iOS and 512 MB on the Mac; the pool goes after 5 s unused, at once when the headroom to the memory limit is under 1 GB, at a memory trim and going to the background. Kept in player builds, for the phone A/B

name: DM_NVN_STALE_FLOAT
meaning: `1` fills a new floating-point texture in a `CPU_NO_ACCESS` pool from its storage as it is, NaN and infinity included; by default storage with any non-finite float element starts the texture from zeros (`storage_has_nonfinite` in `nvn_mtl.m`)

name: DM_NVN_STORAGE_FIRST_USE
meaning: `0` keeps a sampled block-compressed texture in a CPU-writable pool to the one-time fill instead of making it CPU-written when its storage holds data at first use (on by default; `tex_cpu_content`), to measure it

name: DM_NVN_SUBMIT_PROBES
meaning: `full` reads the submit-cost probes as before (`clock_gettime`, and a thread port made and released for each kernel-time reading), about 1.6 us a scope against 0.9 us for the default single `THREAD_BASIC_INFO` call on a kept port (`nvn_queue.inc` `nq_cost_begin`)

name: DM_NVN_SUB_DRAIN
meaning: `1` makes the replay wait for the encode thread at the end of every submission, as before (with `DM_NVN_ENC_THREAD`; by default a submission's end hands its records over and the replay goes on, and a present of the game's own texture waits for its commit); `ab` alternates with the `DM_AB` phases, to measure it; kept in player builds

name: DM_NVN_SUB_IDLE_FB
meaning: `1` holds submissions while the commit feedback's count of command buffers still running is above zero, as upstream's first version did (with `DM_NVN_ENC_THREAD` and `DM_NVN_SUB_MERGE` on; by default the encode thread reads whether the GPU has run out of its work from an event it signals after each of its commits, which the GPU writes as it gets there, before the feedback runs); `ab` alternates with the `DM_AB` phases, to measure it; kept in player builds

name: DM_NVN_SUB_MERGE
meaning: `0` commits every submission in a command buffer of its own again (with `DM_NVN_ENC_THREAD`; by default a submission that ends while the GPU still runs an earlier command buffer is held, and the held ones are committed together when the GPU or the recorded work runs out, or before anything else goes to the queue); `ab` alternates with the `DM_AB` phases, to measure it; kept in player builds for the iPhone A/B

name: DM_NVN_SUB_YIELD
meaning: `0` keeps `g_sub_mu` with the replay across each whole command node, as before, so a game submit that finds it taken waits for the rest of the node. By default such a submit counts itself waiting and the replay, between two commands of the node (the top of `mtl_exec`'s loop), lends it the lock for its command copy and takes it back after, at most once every 50 µs of a node; a lend no submit takes within 0.2 ms (a submitter woken but not running) ends the lending for the rest of that node, and the replay's time without the lock counts as its `g_sub_mu` wait, outside its node's cost; program and queue finalization never take a lent lock (`sub_lock_whole`). Ocarina of Time's submit thread waited about 1 ms a frame, 2-4 ms in heavy stretches. The queue line adds the lends a frame, the copies made in them, the lends not taken and the replay's time without the lock (`nvn_queue.inc` `nq_sub_yield`; `t_sub_yield`). Kept in player builds, for an A/B

name: DM_NVN_T2T_FROM
meaning: `=<frame>`: `DM_NVN_T2T_TRACE` records copies only from that frame on (default 0)

name: DM_NVN_T2T_TRACE
meaning: `=<W>x<H>:<file>`: after each copy into an RGBA16F texture of that size, copies the result into a trace buffer on the GPU timeline; 240 entries are written to the file

name: DM_NVN_TBUF_GPU_COPY
meaning: `0` copies a buffer texture below the device's linear-texture alignment on the CPU when its binding is encoded, as before; by default the aligned copy is made on the GPU timeline before the draw or dispatch that reads it, so it holds what earlier GPU work of the submission wrote (`nvn_mtl.m` `tba_prepare`)

name: DM_NVN_TEXCPU
meaning: `=1` logs non-packaged (non-swizzled) textures in CPU-visible pools

name: DM_NVN_TEXDUMP
meaning: `=<frame>:<path>`, `size=<W>x<H>:<path>` or `layers=<n>:<path>`: saves every colour render target of that frame as PNG (`%d` = serial × 100 + layer × 10 + level)

name: DM_NVN_TEXINFO
meaning: `=<W>x<H>` logs storage and description of every texture of that size on first use, registration and initialization (pool, flags, packaged, non-zero bytes, swizzles)

name: DM_NVN_TEXRAW
meaning: `=<serial>,…` or `info` (the textures `DM_NVN_TEXINFO` picked out): saves those textures' raw bytes at the `DM_NVN_TEXDUMP` frame, with a text header line

name: DM_NVN_TEXSNAP
meaning: `=<in-frame pass index>,…`: with `DM_NVN_TEXDUMP`, copies those passes' colour attachments as they end and saves them with the end-of-frame dump

name: DM_NVN_TEX_ALT2
meaning: `0` keeps one type-compatible view per texture ID, as before (kept in player builds, for the phone A/B). By default `tex_fit` keeps the one before it too: an ID that shaders read as two types (a 6-layer array as a 2D array and as a cube), or from two views, made one of the two again at every change between them and moved the type-view generation (`g_alt_gen`) with it. With `DM_NVN_ARGS_STATS=1` the texture lookups line counts the views by why they were made. Mac (`t_tex_seq`, an ID read as 2D and cube in turn, 20 rounds): 40 views made -> 2

name: DM_NVN_TEX_READAHEAD
meaning: `0` turns off the read-ahead of a texture's storage at its setup; by default a texture whose content the host may take from its storage (a CPU-readable pool, not render-target-like) has its storage asked for ahead (F_RDADVISE) at nvnTextureInitialize, so the replay's first-use reads find it in memory: [area loads waited on the replay's own page faults](reference/frame-rate.md#area-loads-waited-on-the-replays-own-page-faults)

name: DM_NVN_TEX_SEQ
meaning: `0` checks a packaged (or CPU-written) texture ID's view again after any guest write anywhere, as before (kept in player builds, for the phone A/B). By default the check that finds its pages unwritten since its upload keeps the write sequence of the memory pool's tracked range (`nvn_dirty.c` `nvn_dirty_since_seq`, moved after every write the range takes, at its registration and at its removal), and the fast tests take the view again while that pool has had no write: a write elsewhere no longer sends every packaged ID down the slow path (`nvn_mtl.m` `tex_by_id_ptr`; Ocarina of Time takes about 2,000 write faults a second across 4,700 pools). The check itself also reads the range's last write first and skips the pages when it is older than the upload. Mac (`t_tex_seq`, 192 packaged IDs in 96 pools, a write before each round): a write in another pool 13.7 -> 2.0 ns a lookup

name: DM_NVN_TREG_ID
meaning: `=<n>` logs every registration of texture ID n: what it holds from then on, and the frame being recorded

name: DM_NVN_TRIM_FRAMES
meaning: `0` counts the idle trims' 600 (upload staging, `DM_NVN_UPLOAD_TRIM`; re-upload spares, `DM_NVN_PKG_SPARE_IDLE`) in submissions again, as before b56ae61d; by default they are frames, converted with the session's own submissions a frame, so a game making many submissions a frame keeps its blocks and spares about 10 s

name: DM_NVN_TSV
meaning: `=<path>` writes the per-frame NVN call table and timing rows (frame, metric, value) to a TSV, read by `scripts/bench.py`

name: DM_NVN_TSV_CALLS
meaning: `0` makes `DM_NVN_TSV` write only the timing rows, without the call counts (about two thirds of the file)

name: DM_NVN_UB
meaning: `="name=item,…;…"`: alternating measurement in one run; odd phases of `DM_NVN_UB_N` frames (default 180) take one category in turn (`@set:<global>=<value>` or dropped shader keys) and log present times

name: DM_NVN_UBD_MEMO
meaning: `0` scans the deferred uniform update list for every lookup instead of remembering answers per range until the list changes (for timing)

name: DM_NVN_UBP_CHECK
meaning: `=1` checks every uniform shadow made from memory: the pass ends, the updates land, the replay waits for the GPU and compares (a difference is a red line; slow)

name: DM_NVN_UBP_RUNNING
meaning: `0` refuses a uniform shadow partly covered by inline updates of a running submission, as before; by default those updates are remembered by byte, each with its fence, and laid over memory in the shadow

name: DM_NVN_UB_COPY_THREAD
meaning: `0` copies uniform shadows of 512 bytes or more on the submit thread, as before (by default a worker copies them)

name: DM_NVN_UB_DEFER
meaning: `0` ends the render pass at every inline uniform update, as before; by default an update inside an open pass is deferred to the pass end and later draws read a shadow (off in TBDR mode)

name: DM_NVN_UB_LAZY
meaning: `=<n>`: the most deferred inline uniform updates kept across a render pass end (default 160); they land before the next copy, a conflicting draw or dispatch, or the submission end; `0` lands them at every pass end

name: DM_NVN_UB_N
meaning: `=<frames>`: the length of each phase of the same-process alternating measurement `DM_NVN_UB` (default 180, minimum 60)

name: DM_NVN_UB_PARTIAL
meaning: `0`: a uniform block the deferred updates cover only in part ends the pass, as before; by default its shadow starts from memory and takes the submission's queued updates (on by default)

name: DM_NVN_UNWIRE_UP
meaning: The upload-only unwire: memory pools that only texture uploads have read leave the residency set once every upload batch that reads them has come back and they have gone 3 s without an upload, so their guest-file pages are no longer wired and the kernel may drop them instead of compressing dirty memory (Ocarina of Time re-read 12.6 GB of guest-file pages in 120 s). A pool another use has looked up, a large pool's chunks, a sticky one (three re-adds within 10 s of their unwire) and every pool a GPU address was given in, which a raw pool table may name, stay, whether or not a table has been built yet (a late first table would otherwise put them all back at once in front of its draw). A later use puts the pool back through the usual lookup or the raw table before any command buffer that uses it is committed; a later upload reads it through a buffer of the upload batch over the texture's pages alone.
