At most one sweep every 500 ms, 256 pools or 512 MB a sweep, at a submission's start, and one at a memory trim without the 3 s rule. Pages are never discarded or unlocked by hand: leaving the set is all. `m` (the default until the byte-exact replays of game captures have passed) counts what would leave and changes nothing, and is what an unset or empty value gives; `1` on; `0` off (no 10 s line); `ab` with `DM_AB`. The `[mem] upload-only unwire` line every 10 s beside the guest file's line: unwired and re-added pools by cause, sticky, the resident pools by class (U1 / U2 / U3 / EV, with the MB the raw table keeps by how the address was given), uploads read through a batch buffer. Kept in player builds (`nvn_mtl.m` `up_unwire_sweep`, `pool_res_classes`; [frame-rate.md](reference/frame-rate.md#upload-only-pools-kept-wired-after-their-uploads))

name: DM_NVN_UNWRITTEN_DC
meaning: `0` disables optional stores elided for loaded, unchanged attachments (on by default, independent of TBDR lookahead), for equivalence comparisons; mandatory image-write preservation stays active

name: DM_NVN_UNWRITTEN_LOAD
meaning: `0` loads every colour attachment as before; by default a colour attachment that no draw of its pass writes is loaded as DontCare and stored as DontCare, so its memory stays as it was: when a draw opens a pass, a scan of the replay up to the pass's certain end (a SetRenderTargets to other targets, or the submission's end) finds the attachments no draw or clear may write, and a draw (or a clear triangle) that would write or read from the tile one of them after all ends the pass first and opens its own, which loads it (`nvn_mtl.m` `ldc_plan`; Donkey Kong Bananza's 38-90 MB a frame of unwritten loads). Not for clear-only, face-split, slice-merged, layered, kept-frame or multisampled passes. Counted in the `residency set` line (`colour loads skipped`, `pass ends for a draw that did`)

name: DM_NVN_UPLOAD_IDLE_MS
meaning: `=<ms>`: an opt-in idle trim of the upload staging by time, beside `DM_NVN_UPLOAD_TRIM`'s (which it leaves as it is): a slot with no batch for that long lets both its blocks and its demand go, its 4 MB block included, and a slot in use is shrunk to the peak of its last interval and drops an overflow block unused that long, each block out of the residency set at once (`nvn_mtl.m` `up_idle_release`; upstream NXNative 93c76c1cb). Unset or `0` (the default on every platform) trims nothing; set, `0` included, it writes `upload staging: slots hold N MiB; … blocks allocated, … trimmed` at the start, the first trim and every 30 s, for an A/B

name: DM_NVN_UPLOAD_REUSE
meaning: 0 keeps the original one-block upload-slot policy; default retains bounded demand-sized primary and overflow buffers after completion.

name: DM_NVN_UPLOAD_SRC_MB
meaning: `=<MiB>`: a budget for an upload batch's zero-copy buffers over guest texture storage (`up_big_src`), which the staging budget does not count: a texture whose source would pass it begins a new batch first, between textures only (one texture larger than the budget still goes in one batch). Unset or `0` (the default on every platform): no budget (`nvn_mtl.m` `up_src_budget`; upstream NXNative 31fdefeb4)

name: DM_NVN_UPLOAD_TRIM
meaning: `0` keeps each upload slot's grown staging block and its 32 MB overflow block for the rest of the run, as before; by default a slot lets them go after 600 submissions with no batch that needed them, back to its 4 MB block at most

name: DM_NVN_UP_BILINEAR
meaning: `0` lets MetalFX draw the game's own upscaler again where a profile's `upscaler_bilinear on` draws a bilinear stretch instead (the Quality preset sets it); `1` turns the stretch on in any game. Only with `DM_UPSCALER=metalfx`, and only for linear or square-rooted colour (sRGB-encoded input keeps MetalFX); taken at the next frame, so a preset picked in game applies (`nvn_mtl.m` `up_bil_on`, `up_mfx_encode`). Also from `Documents/env.txt`, player builds too ([The game's upscaler as a bilinear stretch](reference/rendering.md#the-games-upscaler-as-a-bilinear-stretch))

name: DM_NVN_UP_SLOTS
meaning: `=<n>`: how many upload batch slots rotate, each with its own command allocator and staging (`nvn_mtl.m` `up_slots_pick`), held to 3 to 8; a value that is not a number is ignored. Overrides the profile's `upload_slots` (3 without the key; Breath of the Wild 8, adapted from MacNativeGames 6ecb27c1 (MIT)). Performance; more slots let the submit thread run further ahead of the GPU before it waits for a slot, and can hold more staging. Kept from `Documents/env.txt` in a player build (`DM_PLAYER_BUILD=1`, `player_env.h`): `3` there is the off side of Breath of the Wild's A/B, read with `DM_NVN_WAITS=1` (the `[waits]` line's `upload slot`). The log's start names the count and its source

name: DM_NVN_VBAR_PASS
meaning: `0` ends the draw pass at a game barrier after vertex-stage shader writes, as before; by default the pass goes on behind a barrier from the vertex stage; `ab` alternates with `DM_AB`

name: DM_NVN_VBUF_CACHE
meaning: `0` turns off the cache of resolved vertex stream addresses and vertex argument table writes across draws (on by default), for A/B runs

name: DM_NVN_VCONV_CHECK
meaning: `=1` scans the indices again at every reuse of a cached vertex conversion range (`vconv_range`) and reports differences

name: DM_NVN_VCONV_CPU
meaning: `=1` converts integer vertex inputs fed formats of another class on the CPU, as before, instead of through the shader's shadow inputs (`<key>_bv`), and the integer-read-as-float formats too (no native fetch, `DM_NVN_I2F_NATIVE`)

name: DM_NVN_VCONV_KEEP
meaning: `=0` turns off the kept vertex conversions (`vk_get`); `=<n>` sets the smallest range kept, in vertices (default 4096)

name: DM_NVN_VCONV_RANGE
meaning: `0` / `1` overrides the profile's `vconv_range`: CPU vertex conversion only over the vertices each draw reads instead of the whole bound range

name: DM_NVN_VLOG
meaning: Set: logs each NVN memory pool as it is created (address, memory, size, flags) with a backtrace

name: DM_NVN_VSDUMP
meaning: Output file for post-vertex captures; used with DM_NVN_VSDUMP_KEY and the frame/count bounds

name: DM_NVN_VSDUMP_FROM
meaning: First presented frame eligible for a post-vertex capture (default 0)

name: DM_NVN_VSDUMP_KEY
meaning: Vertex key to capture, or `*` for all eligible vertex shaders; storage-writing shaders are excluded

name: DM_NVN_VSDUMP_MAX
meaning: Maximum post-vertex captures (default 1, or 256 for the wildcard key)

name: DM_NVN_WAITS
meaning: `=1` turns on the wait ledger: every place a host or game thread waits on the CPU for the GPU or the encode thread, counted per frame. Kept from `Documents/env.txt` in a player build (`DM_PLAYER_BUILD=1`, `player_env.h`)

name: DM_NVN_WIN_AREA
meaning: `0` makes passes on the window textures cover the whole texture, as before; by default a pass whose colour attachments are all window textures covers only the largest crop presented from them once it has held for 60 presents and covers at most 90% of the texture (`nvn_win_area.h`, `nvn_mtl.m` `present_enqueue` and `rp_begin_ex_`). One `window textures: passes on a WxH window texture limited to the presented crop's WxH` line when it starts. Also from `Documents/env.txt`, player builds too ([The window textures' passes limited to the presented crop](reference/rendering.md#the-window-textures-passes-limited-to-the-presented-crop))

name: DM_NVN_ZBLOCK
meaning: `=1` logs (`[zb]`) the all-zero blocks per level of each ASTC texture uploaded on the CPU (magenta when drawn); `=<folder>` also writes the raw storage of the first one per format and size

name: DM_OE_SCRIPT
meaning: Scripted applet state changes at given seconds, `key=value@seconds,…` with keys `focus`, `opmode` and `bg` (`bg=1` / `bg=0` run the whole background round trip), e.g. `bg=1@20,bg=0@25`

name: DM_OODLE_HOST
meaning: The Mac host binary that `shader_split.py` runs in its Oodle tool mode to decode Trinity packs (`ONEPACK` files); set by the NSP script

name: DM_OODLE_JOB
meaning: `=<job file>`: the host runs the game's own Oodle decoder on every record of the job file right before `nnMain`, writes `<job file>.out` and exits (Unreal shader archives)

name: DM_OODLE_MODULES
meaning: The rewritten modules the Mac host's Oodle tool mode loads when `shader_split.py` decodes Trinity packs; set by the NSP script

name: DM_OODLE_SERVE
meaning: `=1`: the host answers decode requests on stdin / stdout with the game's own Oodle (or LZ5) decoder from the guest main thread before the SDK starts, until stdin ends

name: DM_OPMODE
meaning: The operation mode the game sees: `0` handheld, `1` console (default: the profile's `op_mode`, console unless set); read once at startup

name: DM_PACKED_CHEATS
meaning: Folder of cheat files `build_ipa.sh` packs into the app as `dm/cheats` (the NSP script sets it from the game's mods folder, `dm/tools/game_mods.py`); the iOS app copies each into `Documents/cheats` at each start when that folder does not have it, keeping a file already there (a packed file the player deletes comes back at the next start)

name: DM_PAD_IDENTICAL
meaning: `0` stops reading identical pads here when GameController lists fewer of their model than IOKit has, such as two Pro Controllers over USB (each a player of its own: a Pro Controller from its report 0x30, another model from its HID elements; `pad_hid_mac.h`, `pad_pro.h`); `DM_HID_PADS=0` stops it too; Mac only

name: DM_PAD_MERGE
meaning: `=1` merges every controller into player 1, as before, instead of giving each controller a player of its own (Mac and iOS)

name: DM_PAD_PRESS_TO_JOIN
meaning: `1`: a controller is no player until one of its buttons is pressed, then it is the lowest player free, whatever its port, link or model, identical pads included (`front_mac.m`, `DmGamepad.m`, `pad_slots.h`); not with `DM_PAD_MERGE`. Launcher setting

name: DM_PATCH_FRONT
meaning: `=<bytes>`: the size of the patch area right before the module base for a long text (`BIG_TEXT`); set only by the rewriter's own rerun with the size it needs

name: DM_PHONE_MOTION
meaning: On iOS, whether the phone's own device motion drives player 1's six-axis sensor: `auto` (default) while no controller supplies fresh motion, `1` phone only, `0` never; each source keeps its own orientation

name: DM_PICTURE_FIT
meaning: `fill` scales the 16:9 picture on the iPhone and iPad until it covers the screen in landscape and crops the edges; `stretch` stretches it to cover the screen in landscape without cropping (the present draws it over the whole drawable, `mtl_present_stretch`); a portrait or tabletop split and a TV stay fitted; `fit` or unset, the largest 16:9 rectangle with black bars. Launcher and in-game menu setting

name: DM_PLAY_AT
meaning: Set at Play to the wall clock in seconds since 1970 (a fraction allowed) by the iPhone's and the Mac's settings screens, by `front_ios.m` and the Mac launcher for a start without the screen, and by a program hand-over on the Mac for the program it starts; a front end that runs the host may set it too. The host's start lines count from it: `start: Play at …` and `start: first frame N s after Play: host load, prepare, first frame` (`hle_lifecycle.c`, `start_line.h`); unset, they count from the host's own start

name: DM_PLAY_PRESET
meaning: Set by the Gate's Play: the preset this session starts with (`battery`, `balanced`, `quality`, `performance` or `custom`), for the play record's battery estimate (`PlayRecord.swift`, kept on the device only)

name: DM_POOL_IDS_8K
meaning: `1` / `0` overrides the profile's `pool_ids_8k`: a pool table's lists of IDs to take again at the next change hold 8,192 IDs, what one patch takes (`1`), or 1,024 (`0`, every other game's limit), past which that change builds the table whole (`nvn_mtl.m` `pool_ids_max`). Default: the profile's (Ocarina of Time on). With it on, one line `[nvn-mtl] pool tables: a list of IDs to take again holds up to 8192 IDs, as one patch takes (…)`; the counts to compare are `a new submission over too many retired IDs`, `a pool change over too many IDs without storage` and the tables built whole on the `pool for handles traced to no slot` and `[nvn] pool tables` lines. `0` in `Documents/env.txt` turns it off (a player build keeps it: not a `DM_NVN_*` key)

name: DM_POST_AA
meaning: Anti-aliasing: edge smoothing (Intel's CMAA2) of the game's picture in the present, before MetalFX, the bilinear scale and Sharpening: `off`, `edge`, `edge-sharp` (CMAA2's Extra Sharp; default: the profile's `post_aa`, off without it); `ab` with `DM_AB=<frames>` alternates off and edge (the present's 600-present GPU lines give both). The HUD and text are smoothed too. 8-bit RGBA / BGRA swapchains only. Launcher setting, and on the iPhone and iPad also in the in-game menu, which the present takes at its next frame (`mtl_present_aa_set`; the first pick of a run smooths once its kernels are made in the background)

name: DM_POWER_DETAIL
meaning: `0` drops the power detail (on by default, logging only): the `power detail up to frame N` line that follows each `power` line, with CPU energy, clock (cycles over CPU time) and cores busy on the performance and on the efficiency cores, the time the process's threads were runnable but waited for a core (`proc_pid_rusage` `RUSAGE_INFO_V6`, `nvn_power.h`), the battery level and charging state (iOS: battery monitoring on, cached on the main thread) and Low Power Mode (the thermal state is on the `power` line), a part the platform lacks (a Mac with no battery) said once; the `power tick at T s, frame N` line each second of presenting (CPU energy, CPU time and its share on performance cores, each cluster's clock, fps, GPU ms per second summed over command buffers and as the union of the frames' spans, both approximate, and the frames the acquiring thread ran demoted: not real-time or below priority 97, counted only on the thread the policy was set on, also on the `thread policy` line); and the `performance profile` line (`NSProcessInfo hasPerformanceProfile:`, again on each change). Kept in a player build

name: DM_PREEMPT
meaning: `0` / `1` overrides the profile's `core_preempt`: also check already-runnable higher-priority peers on the caller's core after every thread SVC

name: DM_PRELOAD
meaning: Set: on the Mac, runs the host's early background loading (`dm_host_preload_start`) as the iOS app does, to exercise that path

name: DM_PRESENT_AA_ITEMS
meaning: `=<fraction>` (above 0, at most 1): the share of the pixels edge smoothing's (CMAA2) blend item list holds (default 0.25; `1` is one per pixel, as before); a run that fills it makes it one per pixel from the next present on, said once

name: DM_PRESENT_DRAWABLE
meaning: `game` sizes the iPhone's and iPad's drawable at the picture's render size while the touch controls are drawn into the frame too (the controls laid out at the drawable's pixels, Core Animation scaling the layer to the screen); stands down, logged, where MetalFX upscales to the screen's pixels, under `DM_DRAWABLE_NATIVE=1` and on a TV. Unset or `screen`: the screen's pixels there, as before (`front_ios.m`, `touch_draw.h` `touch_drawable_scale`; docs/reference/rendering.md)

name: DM_PRESENT_FIFO
meaning: `0` makes the display link take the newest queued frame each tick, as before; by default it shows frames in order, at most one tick behind

name: DM_PRESENT_FX_KEEP
meaning: `1` keeps edge smoothing's (CMAA2) texture and lists and the MetalFX scaler's textures after the effect is turned off, as before; by default they are released once the effect has not run for 120 presents and the last present that ran it has completed

name: DM_PRESENT_HZ
meaning: `=<N>`: the frequency of presentation pacing (default 60); `0` means no frame limit and is for performance profiling only

name: DM_PRESENT_INTERVAL
meaning: `display` presents one frame per display-link tick whatever interval the game sets; `game` follows the game's present interval (default: the profile's `present_interval`); the launcher's Frame rate (`game` 30 fps, `display` 60 fps) for a game whose profile sets `present_interval_choice on`

name: DM_PRESENT_LATENCY
meaning: `=1` or `2`: overrides the display link's preferred frame latency for every screen and window mode; larger positive values use 2 (default 2 in variable-refresh fullscreen, 1 otherwise)

name: DM_PRESENT_LINK
meaning: Present pacing: `0` acquires the drawable itself, `1` (the default) presents on a 60 Hz display link, `2` uses a 120 Hz display link with a frame every other tick. Unset, a 60 fps game in fullscreen on a variable-refresh screen that keeps its variable mode (no fixed-rate mode, or `DM_SCREEN_MATCH=0`) at a multiple of 120 Hz takes the 120 Hz link of `2`; a value set here holds in every window and screen mode

name: DM_PRESENT_REPEAT
meaning: `1` presents on every display-link tick (off by default; the profile's `present_repeat` sets the default, Donkey Kong Bananza on; `0` turns it off; no launcher row; a player build keeps it from env.txt): a tick without a new frame shows the last frame again from its present snapshot (which it turns on), never the game's texture, not counted as a present; a held tick with the next frame waiting only with a ring of 3 (`DM_PRESENT_SNAP=3`). Frame generation is off with it (only `1` counts; a log line says so). An A/B of whether a steady present cadence keeps the GPU clock up ([rendering](reference/rendering.md#the-present-repeat-on-every-tick-dm_present_repeat))

name: DM_PRESENT_SHARPEN
meaning: Sharpening in the present (FSR1's RCAS fused into its draw): `0` off, `1` low, `2` medium, `3` high (default: the profile's `present_sharpen`, off without it); not drawn over a picture MetalFX scaled or a non-UNORM source. Launcher setting, and on the iPhone and iPad also in the in-game menu, which the present takes at its next frame (`mtl_present_sharpen_set`)

name: DM_PRESENT_SNAP
meaning: `=<n>`: present snapshots, a ring of n host textures (2 to 4; `1` = 2) the presents are copied to so the game's swapchain texture is free once its copy has run on the GPU; `0` off (default: the profile's `present_snap`)

name: DM_PRESENT_SNAP_WHOLE
meaning: `1` makes each present snapshot (`DM_PRESENT_SNAP`) copy the whole window texture, as before; by default it copies the present's crop alone when the crop lies in the texture and is smaller, at its own place in a slot of the texture's size (`nvn_mtl.m` `snap_region`; adapted from MacNativeGames 78cf9896 (MIT)); a player build keeps it (no filtered prefix)

name: DM_PRESENT_TRIM
meaning: `=<K>`: after K display-link ticks in a row that found two or more frames waiting, one tick takes the newest frame, dropping one, so a frame standing in the queue does not add a tick of latency for good; `0` off. Default: the profile's `present_trim` (an explicit `0` off), else 60 on iOS and off on the Mac; set, it wins over both, so `DM_PRESENT_TRIM=0` in `Documents/env.txt` turns the trim off. K must exceed the runs that frame-time jitter makes (60 is a second at 60 Hz)

name: DM_PRESENT_UPSCALE
meaning: `metalfx` scales a picture smaller than its rectangle on the screen through MetalFX's spatial scaler; `off` (the default) scales it bilinearly. Launcher setting, and on the iPhone and iPad also in the in-game menu, which the present takes at its next frame (`mtl_present_upscale_set`)

name: DM_PRESET
meaning: The launcher's preset (`battery`, `balanced`, `quality`, `performance`, or `custom` when the rows match none), not a row, only with frame generation on (`DM_FRAMEGEN=1` and not `DM_PRESENT_REPEAT=1`, as frame generation reads them; it is the only reader; without it the launcher neither sets nor logs it): set before the game starts at Play, at a start without the settings screen (Skip this screen next time, `DM_LAUNCHER=0`, a home screen shortcut, a program handing over) and at the Mac's start without its window, and by the iPhone's in-game menu after a preset change or a hand change to a preset row (under the menu's lock); an env file's value stays. Frame generation (`DM_FRAMEGEN`) steps aside in `battery` (Battery Saver), read again once a second

name: DM_PREV_PROGRAM
meaning: What `oe::GetPreviousProgramIndex` answers (default -1, started from HOME); `oe::ExecuteProgram` sets it for the program it starts; a relaunch removes it

name: DM_PROBE
meaning: `=module:offset,…` (Mac only): puts a `brk` at each guest address and on every hit prints the thread, registers, strings they point to and a backtrace, then runs the original instruction

name: DM_PROBE_ALL
meaning: Set: probe hits (`DM_PROBE`) also print x8–x18

name: DM_PROBE_DUMP
meaning: `=module:offset:length[:file]`: on the first hit of any probe, writes that range of guest memory to a file (default `run/<platform>/probe_dump.bin`)

name: DM_PROBE_EVERY
meaning: `=N`: every guest probe hit inside `DM_PROBE_FRAMES` counts, every N-th prints (its `#` is then the true hit count, for rates); `DM_PROBE_LIMIT` caps the printed ones

name: DM_PROBE_FRAMES
meaning: Presented frame or inclusive `start-end` range in which guest probes print observations

name: DM_PROBE_HEAP
meaning: `=<name>,<start>,<size>,<free list>,<used list>`: hex offsets of the sead heap layout the probes' `!xN` heap walk uses (default Mario's `0,28,30,b0,c8`)

name: DM_PROBE_HEAPFRAME
meaning: `=<vtable offset in main>` (hex): the probes' heap walk treats heaps of that class as frame heaps (head +0xe0, tail +0xe8)

name: DM_PROBE_HEAPNAME
meaning: `=<text>`: the probes' `!xN` heap walk reports only hits on heaps whose name contains the text

name: DM_PROBE_HEAPRAW
meaning: Set: the probes' heap walk also prints the heap object's first 0x130 bytes

name: DM_PROBE_HEAPWORDS
meaning: Set: the probes' heap walk also prints each used block's first two words

name: DM_PROBE_LIMIT
meaning: Maximum printed hits per guest probe; 0 or absent leaves the count unlimited

name: DM_PROBE_POLL
meaning: `=<address>[+<length>]` (hex, 4 bytes by default, up to 8): a host thread spins on the bytes and on each change snapshots every thread's pc, lr and frames, for writes the watch misses

name: DM_PROBE_WATCH
meaning: `=<address>[+<length>]` (hex, 8 bytes by default): write-protects that host page and reports who writes these bytes, without a debugger

name: DM_PROBE_X2
meaning: `=<bytes>` (hex): probe hits also dump that many bytes of the memory x2 points to

name: DM_PROFILE_IMAGE
meaning: The account picture the game sees: a 256x256 baseline JPEG of at most 128 KiB (else the built-in one); set by the Gate from the NX 18 Profile; never logged

name: DM_PROFILE_SEED
meaning: The player's NX 18 Profile (a folder holding `profile.stamp`, `name.txt`, `picture.jpg`) that NX 18 Beam puts in an iPhone or iPad app as `<App>/NX18ProfileSeed`: an `xcodebuild` build setting the Copy game resources phase reads (`stage_resources.sh`), or `build_ipa.sh`'s IPA packing (the NSP script's `--profile-seed`); the app takes it on its first start or when it is newer (`NX18Profile.applySeed`). Without one the app has none; never logged beyond its being in the app

name: DM_PROGRAM
meaning: `=<index>`: the program of a game of several programs that a host over their profiles runs (default 0; `main.c` `dm_game_cur`)

name: DM_PROGRAMS
meaning: Table of a game's programs on the Mac (`programs.tsv`: index, host, modules, run folder, environment): `oe::ExecuteProgram` starts the named one in this process's place; the NSP script's run command and the Mac app set it

name: DM_PROGRAM_ID
meaning: `=<hex>`: the program ID the host reports from `svcGetInfo(ProgramId)` (default: the profile's `program_id`)

name: DM_PSO_ARCHIVE
meaning: The folder of the per-game Metal 4 pipeline archive of pipeline bases (default `pso_archive/` beside `pso_user.tsv`); `off` keeps no archive; a GPU capture run keeps none either

name: DM_PSO_ARCH_WARM_FLUSH_MS
meaning: `=<ms>`: during a prewarm the game plays through (no prepare step) that is not compacting, the timer's flush hands the archive's period over once it is that old, then twice as long each time up to 16 times (default 60000; `0`: no flush until the prewarm ends or the period is full)

name: DM_PSO_BG_QUEUES
meaning: `=<n>` (1-8): the serial queues of the pipeline builds hybrid draws ask for in the background (default: one per two performance-level-0 cores, but at least half of Metal's concurrent compiles, `maximumConcurrentCompilationTaskCount`, up to 3; the log's `pipeline builds in the background` line gives both)

name: DM_PSO_BUNDLE
meaning: The pipeline archive made offline (`<GPU architecture>.mtl4a`, `prebuilt.tsv`), read only; the iOS app and Mac launcher set it to their `pso/` folder; `off` ignores it; a GPU capture run (`DM_GPU_CAPTURE`, Metal's capture layer loaded, `Info.plist` `MetalCaptureEnabled`) does not open it

name: DM_PSO_BUNDLE_GUARD
meaning: The crash guard of the pipeline archive bundled with the app (`nvn_pso_guard.h`): on by default on iOS, where `0` (or `off`, `false`, `no`) turns it off; off by default on the Mac, where `1` (or any value but those) turns it on. Off, the archive is used at every start and `pso_bundle_guard.tsv` (beside the device's own archive folder, `Documents/` on iOS) is neither read nor written. On, two starts in a row with the archive that do not get past their first frames in the foreground (a crash, or iOS ending the app; the background, the app switcher and the graceful exit do not count) make the next start leave it out and build the bases on the device (a long first start, once), and it stays out for that archive, app build and system build once a start without it gets past them

name: DM_PSO_DEMAND_RECORD
meaning: `0`: a pipeline a hybrid draw stands in for goes into `pso_user.tsv` only once built, not when first asked for (default: at once, so the next start's prepare step builds it)

name: DM_PSO_GPUS
meaning: `build_ipa.sh`: the GPU architectures, comma-separated, to build the offline pipeline archive for (`none` builds none); unset, a profile gets its `pso_gpu` list or `g19p` when absent

name: DM_PSO_HYBRID
meaning: `0`: a draw whose pipeline is not built yet waits for it instead of drawing with its shader pair's pulling pipeline meanwhile (on by default)

name: DM_PSO_HYBRID_KICK
meaning: `0`: when the pipeline archive bundled with the app holds cover pairs only (the pair list is the shader split's cover: every vertex shader with the same one or few pixel shaders, as for 13 Sentinels and Luigi's Mansion 3, and the probe line says `cover pairs only`), a hybrid miss does not build its pair's pulling base in the background for the pair's next miss; the draw waits for its layout base as before (on by default; no effect with real pairs or no bundled archive). For A/B tests: the `pipelines up to frame` line counts `pulling base builds kicked` and `not kicked`

name: DM_PSO_IOS_MIN
meaning: `build_ipa.sh`: the minimum iOS version of the offline pipeline archives (default the app's deployment target, `deploymentTarget` in `dm/ios/project.yml`); a device of another major version cannot open them and builds the bases itself

name: DM_PSO_KEEP_OLD
meaning: `1` opens every pipeline archive file as before: files of another shader chain are not removed at the start, and files written before the chain stamp are not probed or removed after the prewarm (default: removed, docs/reference/memory.md)

name: DM_PSO_LATER_START
meaning: `0` makes every start wait for the prepare step before its first frame, as the first start does; by default a start whose prewarm lists this device prepared to the end before (`pso_archive/prepared.tsv`: the same lists, shader chain, app build, system build, depth mode and bundled archive, and no archive file removed at the open) hands every line to the background on half the performance cores at utility QoS and the first frame does not wait (`nvn_mtl.m` `warm_later_ready`, `warm_later_bg`; the line `pipeline prepare: a later start: …`)

name: DM_PSO_LATE_S
meaning: `0` keeps every shader-only (`S`) line of the prewarm lists in the prepare step, before the first frame, as before; by default the step keeps only the `S` lines whose shader an `R`, `M` or `C` line also uses, and the rest load after the first frame is presented, on two workers at utility QoS (`nvn_mtl.m` `warm_split_late`, `warm_late_start`; the line `pipeline prewarm after the first frame: …` says what they loaded)

name: DM_PSO_MANIFEST
meaning: The prewarm manifest to use instead of the profile's `pso_manifest.tsv`; `off` turns the prewarm off

name: DM_PSO_MTL4
meaning: Retired: ignored with one log line (`DM_PSO_MTL4=<v> ignored: pipelines are always built through MTL4Compiler`); every pipeline is built through MTL4Compiler, with the archive, hybrid pipelines and prebuild, and the `MTLDevice` path it chose (`0`) is gone

name: DM_PSO_PAIRS
meaning: The prebuild's second shader pair table (default: `pso_pairs.tsv` beside the shader map)

name: DM_PSO_PREBUILD
meaning: `0` turns off the prebuild of every known shader pair's pulling base into the pipeline archive (on by default); `tool` runs the prebuild alone on the Mac and exits

name: DM_PSO_PREBUILD_DEPTH
meaning: `zero`: the prebuild tool (`DM_PSO_PREBUILD=tool`) builds bases for the near = 0 depth mode; the NSP script sets it from the profile's `depth_mode`

name: DM_PSO_PREBUILD_THREADS
meaning: `=<n>`: the workers of the prebuild tool (`DM_PSO_PREBUILD=tool`; default: Metal's concurrent compiles, `maximumConcurrentCompilationTaskCount`)

name: DM_PSO_PREBUILD_TRIM
meaning: `0` keeps the prebuild's own pipeline archive files (`pso_archive/pb*_<program ID>.mtl4a`, the running program's only) that a later prebuild found no base in, or that the archive bundled with the app makes redundant (removed by default)

name: DM_PSO_PREOPEN
meaning: `0`: the pipeline archive bundled with the app is opened at the game's first submission, as before; by default one of 256 MB or more starts opening at the game's start, once its address space is reserved (`mtl_pso_bundle_preopen`), beside the rest of its start, and the first submission waits only for what is left of the open (its open line says how long)

name: DM_PSO_PREPARE
meaning: `0` runs the prewarm in the background while the game starts, as without a window; `1` makes the first submission wait for the prewarm lists also without a window

name: DM_PSO_PREPARE_THREADS
meaning: `=<n>`: the workers of the prepare step that builds the prewarm lists before the first frame (default: the device's active cores)

name: DM_PSO_PULL_ALL
meaning: `=1`: every draw that has a pulling pipeline draws with it, never with the pipeline for its vertex layout

name: DM_PSO_READAHEAD
meaning: `1` reads the bundled pipeline archive's GPU code (the parts Metal reads at a pipeline's first use; its open already reads the libraries) into the file cache once the start's pipeline work is over, 8 MB at a time with rests, on one thread at utility QoS, so later in-play lookups find it in memory instead of on flash; it waits while hot, in Low Power Mode or in the background and stops under 1 GB of headroom to the memory limit (`nvn_mtl.m` `ra_step`). Unset or `0` (the default): no read-ahead. For the phone A/B of Ocarina of Time's in-play lookups (frame-rate.md, In-play archive lookups read the GPU code from flash)

name: DM_PSO_RECORD
meaning: `=<file>`: appends the shaders and pipelines used in the run to that file, for re-recording the prewarm manifest

name: DM_PSO_USER
meaning: The per-device list of shaders and pipelines built on the spot (default: `pso_user.tsv` in the parent of `DM_SAVE`)

name: DM_PSO_USER_QUEUE
meaning: `0` filters each new row of this device's pipeline list (`DM_PSO_USER`) against the lists and writes it on the recording thread, as before (the first row reads the whole seed and list there); by default the rows go to a serial queue of the list's own, written at exit and before an archive save too (`nvn_mtl.m` `pso_user_record`; adapted from MacNativeGames 7cdf1b27 (MIT)); a player build keeps it (no filtered prefix)

name: DM_PSO_WAITLOG
meaning: `=1` logs each draw that waited more than 20 ms for its pipeline, with its shader pair and why no stand-in served it

name: DM_QOS_EDGES
meaning: `=e1,e2`: the Switch priority edges of `DM_QOS_MAP` (default `44,59`)

name: DM_QOS_MAP
meaning: `=1` maps guest thread priority to QoS class: ≤ 44 user-interactive, 45–59 user-initiated, the rest utility (off by default: every guest thread runs user-interactive)

name: DM_REC
meaning: `=<file>`: writes player 1's physical input (keyboard, mouse touches, controllers; never `DM_KEYS` / `DM_CTL`) to the file as `DM_KEYS` steps in presented frames, for replaying a run (`DM_KEYS=@<file>`)

name: DM_REFL_IMG
meaning: `=<b-<chain>.img>`: `t_refl` converts every reflection json of that shader library image in both layouts (`DM_NVN_REFL_FIXED`) and compares them (`make check_t_refl REFL_IMG=…` runs it under Guard Malloc)

name: DM_REGIONS
meaning: `=<file>` writes the table of the SDK's address regions every 2 s (alias offset, size, where the request returns to in the game, bytes mapped, the part opened, the SDK offset the request came through; `hle_svc.c` "Address regions"); the NSP script's address region check sets it

name: DM_RELAUNCH
meaning: Set by `oe::RequestToRelaunchApplication` for the host it starts again: `DM_CTL` resumes at the end of its file instead of replaying it

name: DM_RENDER_SCALE
meaning: `0.5` to `1.0`: fixes the game's 3D views at that fraction of their size and turns its dynamic resolution off, for builds with a render scale stub; `1.0` (the default) keeps it. Up to the stub's largest scale (`RENDER_SCALE` in its fixups table): Hades II's render size stub takes up to `3.0` (3840x2160)

name: DM_REPLAY_RT
meaning: `1` / `0` overrides the profile's `replay_rt`: the 'NVN queue replay' and 'dm-encode' threads each declare a time-constraint policy (period the present thread's, computation sized to the thread's own CPU time per frame every 120 frames, raised at once by a frame past it, 0.1 to 0.8 of the period) instead of keeping QoS user-interactive alone (`nvn_rt.h`, `hle_nvn.c` `nvn_rtw_tick`). Default: the profile's (Ocarina of Time on); `0` in `Documents/env.txt` turns it off. The `thread policy` line then says whether each thread's policy is in effect and how many frames ran past it

name: DM_REPLAY_SPARES
meaning: `1` / `0` overrides the profile's `replay_spares`: 32 spare command copies (16 MB in all) instead of 4, and 64 spare pool tables (at most 24 MB in all) instead of 16, the table given when every spare is in flight going instead of the next to come back (`nvn_queue.inc` `nvn_replay_spares`, `nvn_mtl.m` `pool_table_give`). Performance only. Default: the profile's (Ocarina of Time on); `0` in `Documents/env.txt` turns it off; the `[nvn] queue` line's `command nodes without a spare copy` and the `pool tables up to frame` line's `tables made` / `reused` (written with the profile's key on or off) are the counts to compare

name: DM_RESOURCE_AOC
meaning: The add-on content folder the iOS build copies into the app's `aoc/` (empty for none); written by `gen_resources.py`, read by `stage_resources.sh`

name: DM_RESOURCE_BUILD
meaning: Package version (for example `v327680`), written to `Gen/resources.env` by `gen_resources.py`; with `DM_COPY_ROMFS=NO` the copy phase puts it in the `build=` field of the app's `romfs.id`

name: DM_RESOURCE_CHAIN_H
meaning: Path of `dm/gfx/nvn/dmsh_chain.h`, written to `Gen/resources.env` by `build_ipa.sh`; the Xcode copy phase (`stage_resources.sh`) stops when the prepared shaders are not of its chain version

name: DM_RESOURCE_MARKER
meaning: A file under the RomFS, written to `Gen/resources.env` by `build_ipa.sh`, that the Xcode copy phase (`stage_resources.sh`) checks for before copying the game files

name: DM_RESOURCE_MSLDIR
meaning: Name of the shader library folder (`b-<chain>`), written to `Gen/resources.env` by `build_ipa.sh`; the Xcode copy phase copies the shaders to `msl/<name>` in the app, or `msl/<name>.img` for an NVN game's one file

name: DM_RESOURCE_PROGRAMS
meaning: The table of a game's programs' files for the Xcode build phase (`stage_resources.sh`; `build_ipa.sh` writes it)

name: DM_RESOURCE_PSO
meaning: Folder of the offline Metal pipeline archive (empty for none), written to `Gen/resources.env` by `build_ipa.sh`; the Xcode copy phase copies it to `<App>/pso`

name: DM_RESOURCE_ROMFS
meaning: RomFS folder, written to `Gen/resources.env` by `build_ipa.sh`; the Xcode copy phase (`stage_resources.sh`) copies it into the app's `romfs`

name: DM_RESOURCE_SHADERS
meaning: iOS shader library folder or one file, written to `Gen/resources.env` by `build_ipa.sh`; the Xcode copy phase (`stage_resources.sh`) copies it into the app's `msl/b-<chain>` or `msl/b-<chain>.img`

name: DM_RESOURCE_TITLE
meaning: Game profile title ID, written to `Gen/resources.env` by `gen_resources.py`; with `DM_COPY_ROMFS=NO` the copy phase puts it in the `title=` field of the app's `romfs.id`

name: DM_RESOURCE_VERSION
meaning: Display version, written to `Gen/resources.env` by `gen_resources.py`; with `DM_COPY_ROMFS=NO` the copy phase puts it in the `version=` field of the app's `romfs.id`

name: DM_RES_CHECK
meaning: `=1` prints the first 40 textures or buffers a shader reaches through its argument block that are not in the residency set (textures attributed to their parent allocation)

name: DM_REWRITE_J
meaning: `=<positive integer>`: worker processes per module for `patch_nso.py`'s x18 scan and spin wait search; `=1` runs serially. Default: one per core directly, an automatic per-module budget in the NSP script. An explicit value overrides that budget

name: DM_ROMFS
meaning: The game's RomFS folder, mounted read-only as `rom` (default `$DM_ROOT/romfs`); the Mac launcher, the iOS app and the NSP script set it

name: DM_ROMFS_OVERLAY
meaning: `=<dir>[:<dir>…]`: RomFS reads look in these folders first, in order, and fall back to `DM_ROMFS` (for a modified copy of some files)

name: DM_ROOT
meaning: Workspace root (default `~/dm-work`): the host's and tools' default paths (RomFS, temporary storage, shader libraries under `build/cache/metal_shader_cache`, probe dumps) are under it

name: DM_RT
meaning: `0` leaves the thread that acquires the window on its QoS only, with no Mach time-constraint policy declaring the frame deadline (on by default; for power A/B). The replay threads' own policy is `DM_REPLAY_RT`

name: DM_RT_COMP
meaning: `=<ms>` fixes the computation the present thread's time-constraint policy declares; default `auto` re-declares it every 120 frames from that thread's per-frame CPU time (p90 and peak)

name: DM_RUMBLE
meaning: `0` turns game rumble off (on by default); launcher setting

name: DM_RUMBLE_GAIN
meaning: `=0..3` scales the rumble strength (default 1, `0` is silent); launcher setting

name: DM_RUMBLE_LOG
meaning: `=1` logs the game's vibration handle requests and, once a second, the values it sent, how many had no routed output and the peak amplitude

name: DM_RUMBLE_MIN
meaning: `=0..0.9`: controller rumble levels below it stay silent and the rest is stretched over the full range (default 0; the phone is unaffected); for games whose quiet HD rumble texture keeps rotating motors running (Mario Kart 8 Deluxe: 0.45); launcher setting

name: DM_SAVE
meaning: This run's save folder (must be set); the device save is `<DM_SAVE>_device`, and `pso_user.tsv` goes in its parent folder; the Mac launcher, the iOS app and the NSP script set it

name: DM_SAVED_CHOICES
meaning: `0` ignores the player's saved choices (launcher.<VAR> in the app's preferences) and leaves them saved; the Mac launcher and the iOS settings screen

name: DM_SAVE_SYNC
meaning: Cloud saves: the folder whose `<title ID>/save.dmsync` the save is synced through, `icloud` for iCloud Drive/nxnative Saves (the Mac); `0` or unset, off. The Mac launcher sets the folder chosen in its settings window's Cloud saves, the iPhone app the one picked in its launcher (dm/host/save_sync.h); regress.py, bench.py and the NSP script's own host runs set `0`

name: DM_SAVE_SYNC_CHOICE
meaning: Cloud saves: set by a front end that asks the player when the cloud's save and this device's both changed (any value: a save that changed on both sides is replaced on neither without a choice); `ask`: no choice yet, `cloud:<hash>` brings in the cloud's save with that hash, `local:<hash>` sends this device's over the cloud's save with that hash (`local:none`: the cloud had none), `offline`: the cloud could not be read before the start, so the host does not wait for it; unset, the newer save wins (dm/host/save_sync.c, docs/frontends.md); `hold` (the Mac launcher, when iCloud has not caught up before a game's first sync through a folder, dm/mac/MacFirstSync.swift): this start neither fetches nor sends, and nothing goes up at the game's exit

name: DM_SCHEME_NAME
meaning: Set by `build_ipa.sh` itself for xcodegen's `project.yml`: the Xcode scheme name, `DmIOS`, or `<display name> (<title ID>)` for a project prepared with `--prepare-xcode`

name: DM_SCREEN_ASPECT
meaning: `=<width/height>` (1.3 to 1.77, e.g. `1.43` for the iPhone Duo) renders a game whose profile has `screen_aspect on` in that shape: output 1920 wide, 1280-wide layout space, the HUD at the taller edges and 16:9's sides in view; `auto` (iOS) the app window's own shape when it is taller than 16:9, else 16:9; `0` or unset is 16:9; launcher setting

name: DM_SCREEN_ASPECT_SITES
meaning: `=<mask>` with DM_SCREEN_ASPECT: which of the profile's layout-size conversion stubs follow the taller layout, one bit each (default all)

name: DM_SCREEN_FOV
meaning: `off` with DM_SCREEN_ASPECT: the scene keeps the game's vertical angle (narrower sides) instead of 16:9's sides with more above and below

name: DM_SCREEN_HUD
meaning: `=<edge>,<listed>,<full width>,<full height>[,<tallest>]` with DM_SCREEN_ASPECT: the layout rules' distances and sizes in the 1280x720 space (default 280,100,1270,710,1300)

name: DM_SCREEN_MATCH
meaning: `0` keeps the screen's refresh rate in fullscreen; by default a Mac screen whose rate is not a multiple of the game's frame rate switches to one that is (144 → 120 Hz), and a variable-refresh screen to a fixed-rate mode at a multiple (ProMotion 120 → 60 Hz at 60 and 30 fps)

name: DM_SF_TRACE
meaning: `=1` logs every request on the game's own HIPC client sessions that the host answers (`hle_sf.c`)

name: DM_SHADER_FILES
meaning: `1` packs an NVN game's shader library into the unsigned IPA of `build_ipa.sh` as its separate files, `msl/b-<chain>/`, not as the one file `b-<chain>.img`, for install tools that cannot copy a large file (AltServer: 2 GiB) (`pack_ipa.py --shader-files`; off by default; `--shader-files` of the NSP script sets this)

name: DM_SHAKE_G
meaning: `=<G>`: on iOS, the acceleration beyond gravity above which a flick of the phone shakes the controller's six-axis sensor (default 1.5)

name: DM_SHARED_FONT
meaning: One font file served for every shared-font type except the Nintendo extension (default: each type's own file in `$DM_FONT_DIR`, made by `make_shared_fonts.py`; a type without one takes `standard.ttf`, and with no `standard.ttf` macOS's Arial Unicode as it is, which some games' font engines cannot load)

name: DM_SHARED_FONT_EXT
meaning: Font file served for shared-font type 5, the Nintendo extension with the button icons (default `$DM_FONT_DIR/nintendo_ext.ttf`, made by `make_shared_fonts.py`)

name: DM_SHOW_FPS
meaning: Vitals on the iPhone: `1` Standard (frame rate, CPU power, heat, battery and time in two bars beside − / +), `2` Detailed (adds GPU busy time, the longest frame and the performance-core share), `0` off; at IPA build it sets `DMShowFPS` in `Info.plist`, which `Documents/env.txt` overrides

name: DM_SIX_DELAY
meaning: `=0` (the default), `=auto` or `=<ms>` (up to 40): `DM_IMU_DELAY`'s playout delay for the six-axis states (`GetSixAxisSensorStates`) instead of the IMU samples. None by default: a Switch 1 game reads the newest state each frame (aiming, steering), so a delay only adds latency. Also through `DM_CTL`'s `env`

name: DM_SLEEP_STEP
meaning: `one` (or `1`): precise sleeps (`hle_thread.c` `sleep_precise`: SleepThread, the host hooks' sleeps and the clock waits' predicted sleeps) take one step planned for what each thread's sleeps of that length overshot so far, then the loop for what is left, instead of the loop's steps of 3/4 of the time left (about 2.4 wakeups for a 1 ms sleep on the iPhone); a wake more than 100 µs late sends the thread back to the loop for 256 sleeps. Unset, `loop` or `0`: the loop alone, the default. `ab` (or `ab:<k>/<n>`) alternates with `DM_AB`, for an iPhone battery A/B (wakeups/s, CPU W, sound and frame pacing). The threads line counts the late ends either way and, with the switch, the one-step sleeps, their steps and the late wakes. Kept in player builds. Not a player setting

name: DM_SLOWFRAME
meaning: `=1` writes the per-frame timing breakdown to the log only for dropped frames (kept in a ring of the last 16 frames, judged 8 frames late). Any value turns it on (leave the line out for off). Kept from `Documents/env.txt` in a player build (`DM_PLAYER_BUILD=1`, `player_env.h`) unless its value is empty or `0`, so a leftover `DM_SLOWFRAME=0` stays off there

name: DM_SPIN
meaning: `0` makes the rewriter's spin gate return at once, so guest poll loops spin with no sleep; the gate stays (on by default)

name: DM_SPIN_LIST
meaning: `=1` makes `patch_nso.py` print every guest poll loop it found and sends through a spin gate

name: DM_SPIN_POLL
meaning: `=<µs>`: how long a spin-gate wait polls before it sleeps with the yield back-off (default 2000; `0` yields on every pass)

name: DM_STALL_LOG
meaning: the freeze detector (`stall.c`), on by default (logging only, player builds too): `[RED] stall: no present for N s` and a state dump (fences, the feedback queue's heartbeat, the residency locks' holders, the upload slots, the encode thread, the present queue, the waits in progress, the thread table) when no present completes for that long while the game is in focus with the in-game menu closed and the guest clock running (no inline keyboard text box up); at most 3 a run, 30 s apart; `stall: presents resumed after N s` after one. `=<s>` sets the threshold (default 5), `=0` turns it off (`scripts/regress.py` sets 0)

name: DM_STARTED_BY
meaning: Set by NX 18 Beam's Play (`beam`, beam/Sources/Model/GamePlayer.swift) on a Mac game it starts: the in-game menu's Exit row then reads Exit and return to Beam and brings Beam to the front instead of reopening the app at its Gate (dm/mac/GameMenuMac.swift). Any other value, or unset: Exit and return to Gate

name: DM_STICK_MOTION
meaning: `1` starts with Right Stick Motion enabled: player 1 uses the right stick to turn the virtual six-axis sensor. Off by default; toggle it during play from the Mac Controls menu (⌘⇧G)

name: DM_STICK_RADIUS
meaning: the circle every stick is held inside (hle_hid.c stick_circle), 16384 to 32767; default 32767, the Switch's full scale. A smaller value (e.g. 30000, a calibrated Pro Controller's peak) tests a game that misbehaves at full tilt (Persona 4 Golden)

name: DM_SVC
meaning: `=1` logs memory SVCs (`SetHeapSize`, `MapMemory`, `Map`/`UnmapPhysicalMemory`) with their addresses and sizes

name: DM_SW2
meaning: `=1` turns on Switch 2 controllers over Bluetooth LE (Joy-Con 2, Pro Controller 2): the settings window's Switch 2 controllers. Off, no Bluetooth client is created and macOS asks nothing. The host also stays off when the app's Info.plist has no NSBluetoothAlwaysUsageDescription, without which macOS ends the process at the first Bluetooth scan

name: DM_SW2_GYRO_DPS
meaning: `=<degrees per second per count>` is the Switch 2 controllers' gyro scale (default 0.0607, measured on a left and a right Joy-Con 2; the Switch family's nominal 0.070 turned a 90 degree tilt into 104)

name: DM_SW2_HOST
meaning: `=aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff` names this Mac's Bluetooth address when the Mac's Bluetooth host controller does not give it (IOBluetooth): a paired Switch 2 controller wakes with an advertisement addressed to it, and pairing gives it this address

name: DM_SW2_MAP
meaning: `=a,b,c,d,e,f` replaces the built-in map from a Switch 2 controller's raw sensor channels (1 to 6: accelerometer x y z, gyro x y z, a minus flips the sign) to the Switch frame's acceleration x y z and rotation x y z, e.g. `-1,-2,-3,4,5,6` for a Joy-Con 2 held upright

name: DM_SW2_MODE
meaning: Experimental, off by default: `=1` makes `nn::pl::IsRunningOnOunce` answer yes (`hle_sdk16.c` `sw2_mode`), so a Switch 1 program that asks takes its Switch 2 branches, which may call Switch 2 SDK functions the host lacks. It does not reach a Nintendo Switch 2 Edition, which is a separate program (program 1) NX 18 does not build yet: Super Mario Bros. Wonder 1.2.1 uses the answer only for its title-screen upgrade offer, false when the upgrade add-on is present, and keeps its Switch 1 resolution (iPhone, 2026-11-14). Unset, empty, zeros, `off`, `no` or `false` keep the Switch 1 answer of X1.0; read at the first call, and logged once (`pl::IsRunningOnOunce: yes, a Switch 2`) only when on. Not the Switch 2 controllers (`DM_SW2`). Kept from `Documents/env.txt` in a player build (`player_env.h`). No CPU or GPU cost of its own

name: DM_SW2_MOTION
meaning: `=0` leaves out the motion of Switch 2 controllers (buttons, sticks and rumble stay)

name: DM_SW2_MOTION_SIDE
meaning: `=L` takes a Joy-Con 2 pair's motion from the left Joy-Con instead of the right one

name: DM_SW2_VERBOSE
meaning: `=1` logs the first report of each second of every Switch 2 controller: buttons, sticks, raw sensors, battery, and the bytes the parser does not read (0x18..0x2F and past 0x3C, in hex: whether a report carries the sensor's own timestamp or more than one sample is not known)

name: DM_SYMCHECK
meaning: `=1` checks every hashed module symbol lookup against a linear search and logs a red line for each mismatch

name: DM_TBUF_ALIGN
meaning: `=<bytes>` uses that value as the linear-texture alignment when it is larger than the device's `minimumLinearTextureAlignmentForPixelFormat`, for buffer textures and for linear textures on a pool's buffer: a Mac can then reproduce a phone's larger alignment (a 64-byte one fails the buffers and linear textures a device with 64 bytes cannot view), to check `tbuf_as_2d`'s aligned-row copy and the upload of unaligned linear textures (`linear_fit`)

name: DM_TEAM_ID
meaning: Apple team ID for the per-game Xcode project, used when `--team-id` / `TEAM_ID` is not given; `build_ipa.sh` uses the placeholder `0000000000` (unsigned) when unset

name: DM_TEMP
meaning: Temporary storage folder (default `$DM_ROOT/run/platform/temp`); stand-in system data goes in `<DM_TEMP>_sysdata`; the Mac launcher, the iOS app and the NSP script set it

name: DM_TEST_ACK
meaning: The first-start acknowledgement (NX18Welcome.swift): `1` shows it whatever `nx18.ack` says, `0` skips it (the Duo harness sets `0`). Taken from the launch environment only: an `env.txt` line is ignored (gate-ui GW33)

name: DM_TEST_ARCHIVE_CONSTANTS
meaning: Use optional function constants in the synthetic pipeline archive restart fixture

name: DM_TEST_ARCHIVE_MIXED
meaning: Mix a newly compiled shader function with compacted bases in the archive restart fixture

name: DM_TEST_BORDER
meaning: Path to the native t_border executable that test_dmsh_border.py runs a rewritten shader through on the GPU (`make check_t_border` sets it)

name: DM_TEST_BUILD
meaning: Build folder of `dm/host/tests` whose `t_svc_memory` `test_memory_profile.py` runs (default `build`; `make asan` sets `build/asan`)

name: DM_TEST_FRAMEWG_CRASH
meaning: Makes `dm/host/tests/t_framewg` also run a thread that joins the frame workgroup and ends without leaving, in a process of its own, and expect that process to end (libdispatch's `Thread exiting without leaving workgroup`): the case `frame_wg.c`'s key destructor is there for. Off by default because the crash leaves a crash report each run

name: DM_TEST_FS_FAIL
meaning: `=write:<n>[:<errno>]` makes the nth save write fail with that errno (default ENOSPC), which refuses the save transaction's commit

name: DM_TEST_FS_FAILAT
meaning: `=<point>[:<count>][,…]` makes steps of the save transaction (`mountclone`, `reclone`, `guestname`, `renameback`) fail with ENOSPC

name: DM_TEST_GEOMETRY
meaning: Path of the native `t_geometry` executable; `test_dmsh_geometry.py` runs its native geometry emitter checks only when it is set

name: DM_TEST_GEOMETRY_PRIMITIVE_ID
meaning: Path to the native t_geometry_primitive_id replay executable used by test_dmsh_geometry.py with DMSH_TEST_GPU=1.

name: DM_TEST_GPU_LOST
meaning: `=<n>` imitates the GPU access macOS revoked from the nth submission on: each submission's feedback reports `MTL4CommandQueueErrorAccessRevoked` and the GPU does not signal its fence, so the host stops presenting and the front end ends the game

name: DM_TEST_KEYRACE
meaning: `=<n>` creates up to n (at most 512) pthread keys on a thread of its own while the host starts up

name: DM_TEST_KILL_AT
meaning: `=write:<n>` exits the process (`_exit(9)`) at the nth save write, imitating a kill mid-write

name: DM_TEST_LEAK_GPU
meaning: `=1` allocates and keeps a 1 MB shared Metal buffer every 100 ticks: a GPU memory leak on demand

name: DM_TEST_LINK_STALL
meaning: `=<start s>,<duration s>`: counting from the first present, pauses the display link at that point for that long, to check the present fallback

name: DM_TEST_METAL4
meaning: `=1` / `=0`: the Mac app's launcher (`dm/mac/launcher.c`) takes the GPU as one with / without Metal 4, so `test_nsp_mac_app.py` runs its stand-in host on a Mac without it (GitHub's virtual Macs) and checks the refusal on one with it

name: DM_TEST_PRESENT_LAG
meaning: `=<every n>,<ms>[,<in a row>][;…]` sleeps that long before every nth present (and the ones after it in the run): a slow frame on demand

name: DM_TEST_STUCK_DRAW
meaning: In t_pso_archive's SIGTERM and hand-over cases, holds a draw in the graphics layer (dm_gfx_enter with no leave) so the graceful exit's drain never returns

name: DM_TEST_SWKBD_HOLD_MS
meaning: `=<ms>` (with `DM_KBD`) keeps the system keyboard up that long before `DM_KBD`'s text is returned, as a player typing would

name: DM_TEST_SWKBD_LAG_MS
meaning: `=<ms>` sleeps that long between the keyboard handing back its text and the game's thread getting the result, to check that auto-accept does not act early

name: DM_TEST_TRANSFORM_FEEDBACK
meaning: Path to the native t_transform_feedback executable used by the Python feedback tests

name: DM_TEST_UP_LOST
meaning: `=<batch index>` treats that batch of uploads as dropped, to exercise the re-upload path

name: DM_THERMAL_CAP
meaning: `0` turns off the thermal cap's heat cause, which holds the frame step, an engine limiter the host writes at 60 and a display-mode 60 fps present cap at 30 fps (a 120 fps engine limiter at 60) while iOS reports a serious or critical thermal state (on by default). A diagnostic switch; Low Power Mode keeps its own setting (`DM_LOW_POWER_CAP`)

name: DM_THR
meaning: `=1` logs each SVC (except `SleepThread`) with its first four arguments, and each `CreateThread` with entry, stack, priority and core

name: DM_THRCPU
meaning: `=<tsv path>[,<seconds>]` writes each thread's CPU time (100% = one core) and the total every interval (default 10 s); on iOS a relative path is under `Documents`, and `Documents/env.txt` can set it

name: DM_TOUCH_DRAW
meaning: `layer` draws the iPhone's and iPad's touch controls on their own layers over the game's layer, as before; by default (unset or `frame`) the live present draws them into the game's frame while they show, so iOS can show the game's drawables without compositing them (a refresh less between the present and the screen; `front_ios.m`, `DmGamepad.m` `touchDraw:`, `nvn_mtl.m` `touch_draw`; docs/reference/frame-rate.md). For an A/B of the two: `front end: touch controls …` says which draws them, at the start and at each change

name: DM_TOUCH_HAPTICS
meaning: `0` turns off the light haptic tap when a touch control is pressed (on by default); launcher setting

name: DM_TOUCH_LOG
meaning: `=1` logs each touch-screen sample with touch points (sample, finger, position, attributes) and each gesture entry, up to 500 lines

name: DM_TOUCH_OPACITY
meaning: `=<factor>` (0.1 to 2) multiplies the opacity of the iPhone and iPad touch controls' fills, outlines, labels and shadows (each capped at fully opaque, the shadows at their own): `1` Normal, the look they always had (the default), `0.4` Faint, `0.7` Light, `1.5` Strong. The menu button keeps the normal look. Launcher and in-game menu setting (Touch control opacity), applied at once

name: DM_TOUCH_SIZE
meaning: `=<factor>` (0.5 to 1) scales the iPhone and iPad touch controls, their distance from the edges and corners and their hit areas (the left stick's ring too; the undrawn right stick keeps its swipe length): `1` Large, the size they always had (the default), `0.85` Medium, `0.7` Small. An iPad draws them about 1.5 times as large as an iPhone does, so Small there is about an iPhone's Large. Launcher and in-game menu setting (Touch control size), applied at once

name: DM_T_DUMP
meaning: `tests/t_blend_zero.m` prints the red channel each draw stored, row by row

name: DM_UDC_SELFTEST
meaning: `=1` runs a start-up check of DontCare load and store on private depth-stencil and RGBA8 textures (clear, Load + DontCare, read back) and logs one result line

name: DM_UE_SHADERS
meaning: Folder of the Unreal shader code archives decoded by `uepak.py`, for `shader_split.py` (default `ue_shaders` beside the RomFS); needed when the RomFS has Unreal paks

name: DM_UE_TEXTURE_POOL
meaning: Megabytes Unreal's texture streaming pool (`r.Streaming.PoolSize`) is raised to, overriding the profile's `ue_texture_pool`; `0` keeps the game's own pool. On iOS only this switch turns it on (`Documents/env.txt`)

name: DM_UI_FONT
meaning: `=<file.ttf | .otf | .ttc>` is NX 18's UI font, the player's own, for every text NX 18 draws (launchers, prompts, progress screens, the Mac banner and Cheats window; `dm/host/ui_font.h`, `NXFont.swift`): `build_ipa.sh` copies it to `dm/uifont/ui.<ext>` with `DMUIFontFile` in `Info.plist` (the NSP script's `--ui-font` / `UI_FONT`); at run time it names another file, `0` or empty turns it off (the system font), unset the app's `DMUIFontFile` is used; the Mac launcher sets it for the host

name: DM_UI_FONT_NAME
meaning: The UI font's PostScript name: `build_ipa.sh` writes it as `DMUIFontName` (the NSP script reads it with fontTools); at run time `ui_font.h` sets it from the registered file, and Swift's `NXFont` and every other part look the font up by it (unset: the system font)

name: DM_UI_FONT_SCALE
meaning: `=<0.5 to 1.5>` scales every size NX 18's text asks for when the UI font is on (default 0.9: its letters are larger than the system font's at one size)

name: DM_UI_GLASS
meaning: `0` draws the Gate's hero buttons and the NX 18 card's rim as solid surfaces instead of glass, for the A/B (gate-ui §11, NX18Glass.swift)

name: DM_UI_IDLE
meaning: `0` brings back the Gate's endless flowing rails and constant 16 ms controller polling, for the idle A/B; by default the rails run one cycle after an input and the poll sleeps when input is idle (gate-ui GW19, GW20)

name: DM_UPSCALER
meaning: `metalfx` draws the game's own upscaler shaders (agl's NDSR network, found by the shader map) with MetalFX's spatial scaler (the launcher's default on iPhone and iPad); `game` runs them (the Mac launcher's default, and the host's when nothing sets it)

name: DM_VI_FRAME_TICKET
meaning: `0` makes `nn::vi::ListFrameHistory` take each frame's present-queue ticket at the game's present call, as before release 1, which reports a frame shown about a frame before its own present is handed on; unset (or any other value), the NVN queue worker gives the frame its ticket once its present is in the queue ([services](reference/services.md#a-frame-read-as-shown-before-its-own-present-was-handed-on)). For the device A/B of Minecraft Dungeons II, the Octopath Travelers and Luigi's Mansion 3; the host logs it once

name: DM_VSYNC_HZ
meaning: `=<Hz>`: rate at which a host thread fires the vi vsync event when the display link does not drive it (default 60)

name: DM_WAKE_UNLOCKED
meaning: `0` signals a woken guest thread while the waker still holds the thread lock, as before; by default the signal comes after the lock is let go, so the woken thread does not sleep again on it ([Wakes signalled after the scheduler lock is let go](reference/threads.md#wakes-signalled-after-the-scheduler-lock-is-let-go))

name: DM_WATCH
meaning: `=<s>` dumps all threads after that many seconds (SIGALRM) and turns on the stall watchdog; off unless set

name: DM_WATCH_SAMPLE
meaning: `=<path>` (Mac): when the stall watchdog fires, samples the process for 1 s with `/usr/bin/sample` and writes the thread stacks to that path

name: DM_WATCH_STALL
meaning: `=<s>`: when the frame loop makes no progress for that long (default 15 with `DM_WATCH`), logs a red line, dumps the threads and exits

name: DM_WEB_LOG
meaning: `1` logs each key an offline HTML page is given and where the focus is after it

name: DM_WEB_OFFLINE_RULES
meaning: `0` attaches no content rule list to a game's offline HTML pages, so their loads from http(s) and ws(s) are not blocked and a page loads as soon as it is opened, without waiting for the list to compile (`web_apple.m` `offline_rules`; on by default)

name: DM_WELCOME
meaning: The first-start welcome (NX18Welcome.swift, iOS): `0` skips it (tests, A/B; the Duo harness sets `0`), `1` shows it whatever `nx18.welcome` says; by default it shows once per app, on the first settings screen

name: DM_WINDOW
meaning: When set (to any value, `0` included) opens a Mac window with keyboard and controller input; unset runs headless with the guest on the current thread; the Mac launcher sets it

name: DM_WINDOW_TOP
meaning: `1` (Mac, with `DM_WINDOW`) orders the game window in front without activating it and keeps it above other apps' windows, so a covered window does not slow the run; `regress.py` sets it

name: DM_XCODE_DERIVED_DATA
meaning: Xcode derived data folder for `build_ipa.sh` (default `$W/build/ios/xcode-dd`); the NSP script points it into the game's build folder

name: DM_XCODE_PROJECT_DIR
meaning: Folder of the per-game Xcode project that `build_ipa.sh --prepare-xcode` makes (default `$W/xcode`); the NSP script sets it

name: DM_YIELD_BACKOFF
meaning: `0` turns off the yield back-off; `=<cap µs>[:<start µs>]` sets its sleep cap and the run of yields after which it starts (default 250:2000). Fields accept nonnegative integer microseconds through `INT64_MAX/1000`; invalid values fall back to the full default `250:2000`

name: DM_YIELD_CLOCK
meaning: Clock-reading yield loops: 0 uses ordinary yield backoff, 1 backs off from the start, 2 also sleeps to the predicted end (default)

name: DM_YIELD_PARK
meaning: Parked yields (`hle_thread.c` `park_yield`), on by default (unset, empty, `1` or `on`) since Ocarina of Time's phone A/B: a thread in a tight run of yields (`DM_YIELD_STORM`'s, which must count) park from 50 µs into the run, each further yield sleeping on a progress word for at most 50 µs and woken as soon as another guest thread makes progress (a thread SVC other than a yield, a host wait that blocks, a yield after guest work, an exit); the thread that acquires the window texture parks too; `=<cap µs>:<start µs>` sets both; the `power` line's top yielders add `parks P, woken W, T ms`; `0` / `off`: the yield path as before. Kept in a player build, where it applies to every game

name: DM_YIELD_STORM
meaning: Tight runs of yields (no other SVC and under 2 µs of guest work between two) and yield storms (tight runs past 500 µs), which the yield back-off never sees when the loop's x19–x28 move at each pass (`hle_thread.c` `ystorm_note`). `count` (the default; the profile's `yield_storm`) changes nothing; the `power` line's top two yielders are ranked by and lead with the CPU time of their tight runs (a yield's host time counted up to 2 µs), less sleeps, then the thread with the most yields when not among them (`T ms in tight runs (N yields: moved on Y, sched_yield Q; SleepThread ≤20.1 µs S; back-off sleeps M; yield storms R)`, the short `SleepThread` calls counted apart from the 0 / -1 / -2 yields), and the list ends with every thread's tight runs by length; `sleep` or `1`: once a storm is past 500 µs each further yield of a worker sleeps an eighth of the run so far, 10–50 µs (50 at the default start), until the thread does other work (`; storm sleeps Z`), while the thread that acquires the window texture keeps spinning; `=<cap µs>:<start µs>` (`DM_YIELD_BACKOFF`'s order) sleeps with those values; `0` / `off` neither counts nor sleeps, and the line is as before. Kept in a player build, where `sleep` applies to every game
